c.seed: social science research — Implicit Association Test measuring unconscious racial bias in decision-making outcomes

g.passage: Since its introduction in 1998, the Implicit Association Test (IAT) has been used to measure how quickly people pair images of faces from different racial groups with positive or negative words. Many researchers assumed that slower or faster pairings revealed hidden attitudes that would shape how people actually treat others. In 2013, psychologist Frederick Oswald and colleagues reviewed dozens of studies that had recorded both participants' IAT scores and their later choices, such as hiring recommendations or medical treatment decisions. They found that IAT scores predicted those choices only weakly, and no better than people's openly stated attitudes did. Oswald's team did not conclude that unconscious bias is absent; rather, they argued that a person's score on the test is a poor guide to how that particular person will behave.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: A review of research suggested that results from a widely used test of hidden racial attitudes reveal little about an individual's actual decisions.
A review of research suggested that unconscious racial bias plays no meaningful role in decisions such as hiring and medical treatment.
A review of research suggested that people's openly stated attitudes are a far more accurate predictor of behavior than any measure of hidden attitudes.
A review of research suggested that the test of hidden racial attitudes should be redesigned to measure decisions rather than word pairings.
g.explanation: 지문의 핵심은 Oswald 연구팀이 IAT 점수가 개인의 실제 선택(채용, 치료 결정)을 약하게만 예측한다는 것을 발견했다는 점이므로 A가 정답이다. B는 마지막 문장에서 연구팀이 무의식적 편향이 없다고 결론짓지 않았다고 명시하므로 틀리다. C는 진술된 태도가 IAT보다 '나을 것이 없었다(no better)'는 말을 '훨씬 정확하다'로 과장했다. D는 검사 재설계를 제안했다는 내용이 지문에 없다.
g.explanation_en: The text centers on Oswald's team finding that IAT scores only weakly predicted people's actual choices, such as hiring or treatment decisions, so A is correct. B is wrong because the last sentence explicitly says the team did not conclude that unconscious bias is absent. C distorts the detail: the IAT was "no better" than stated attitudes, which does not mean stated attitudes were far more accurate. D introduces a recommendation to redesign the test that the text never mentions.
g.design: 오답 B·C는 지문 세부(무의식 편향, 진술 태도 비교)를 과장·왜곡해 부분 근거를 갖게 했고, 마지막 문장의 단서를 정독해야 배제되도록 했다. 모든 선택지를 같은 문장 틀로 구성했다.

c.seed: social science research — Stanford Prison Experiment ethical critique and replication failures in 2018-2019

g.passage: For decades, the 1971 Stanford Prison Experiment was presented in textbooks as evidence that ordinary people placed in positions of power will spontaneously become cruel. In the study, psychologist Philip Zimbardo assigned college students to play guards or prisoners in a mock jail, and several guards soon behaved abusively. In 2018, however, researcher Thibault Le Texier published an analysis of archival recordings and documents showing that the experimenters had coached guards to be "tough" and had suggested specific tactics for intimidating prisoners. A 2019 commentary by psychologists Alex Haslam and Stephen Reicher added that guard behavior in a later, similar study varied widely depending on leadership and group identification rather than emerging automatically from the role itself. Together, these critiques suggest that the experiment's famous outcome may reflect the researchers' guidance more than any inevitable effect of the prison setting.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Recent analyses show that the guards in the Stanford Prison Experiment behaved no more harshly than participants in later studies that used a similar design.
Recent analyses suggest that the cruelty observed in the Stanford Prison Experiment was shaped by the experimenters' direction rather than produced by the assigned roles alone.
Recent analyses show that the Stanford Prison Experiment should be removed from textbooks because its archival records were incomplete.
Recent analyses suggest that leadership and group identification were the factors Zimbardo originally intended to measure in the Stanford Prison Experiment.
g.explanation: 지문은 이 실험이 권력이 자연스럽게 잔인함을 낳는다는 증거로 여겨졌지만, 2018년과 2019년의 비판이 그 결과가 연구자들의 지도에서 비롯되었을 수 있음을 보여 준다고 말한다. 따라서 정답은 B이다. A는 후속 연구를 언급하지만 지문은 두 연구의 가혹함 정도를 비교하지 않는다. C는 교과서와 기록 자료를 언급하지만 지문은 기록이 불완전했다고 하지도, 실험을 교과서에서 빼야 한다고 주장하지도 않는다. D는 리더십과 집단 동일시라는 요인을 가져오지만, 이것들은 후속 연구에서 나온 발견이지 Zimbardo가 원래 측정하려던 것이 아니다.
g.explanation_en: The passage says the experiment was long taught as proof that power naturally produces cruelty, but the 2018 and 2019 critiques show the result may come from the researchers' coaching instead. That makes B the correct answer. A mentions the later study, but the passage never compares how harsh the guards were in the two studies. C mentions textbooks and archival records, but the passage doesn't say the records were incomplete or argue that the study should be removed from textbooks. D picks up leadership and group identification, but those factors came from findings in a later study and were not what Zimbardo originally meant to measure.
g.design: Every choice starts with the same "Recent analyses..." frame. Each wrong answer borrows real details from the passage (the later study, textbooks and archives, leadership and group identification) but distorts them. To pick the right answer, you have to connect the traditional claim with what the critiques found.

c.seed: social science research — Pygmalion Effect and teacher expectations influencing student academic performance in classrooms

g.passage:
In 1968, psychologists Robert Rosenthal and Lenore Jacobson told teachers at a California elementary school that certain students had been identified by a test as "intellectual bloomers" likely to make rapid gains. In fact, those students had been chosen at random. By the end of the year, the designated students, particularly in the early grades, showed larger IQ gains than their classmates, a result the researchers attributed to the teachers' raised expectations. The study, which became known as a demonstration of the Pygmalion effect, was widely cited as evidence that teachers' beliefs alone can reshape student achievement.

Later researchers, however, have urged caution. Attempts to replicate the original findings produced mixed results, and a series of reviews by psychologist Lee Jussim and colleagues concluded that teacher expectations generally predict student performance accurately because they are based on real information about students, such as past grades, rather than because they create that performance. Jussim's team found that expectation effects do occur but are typically small, though they appear somewhat stronger for students from groups that teachers may know less about.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Although a famous study found that teachers' expectations raised student achievement, later research showed that such expectations have no measurable effect on how students perform.
Although teachers' expectations once strongly shaped student achievement, later research showed that their influence has declined as schools rely more on objective information such as past grades.
Although a well-known study suggested that teachers' expectations can powerfully drive student achievement, later research indicates that this influence is real but generally modest.
Although a well-known study suggested that teachers' expectations drive student achievement, later research indicates that the effect appears only among students in the early grades.
g.explanation: 지문은 1968년 연구가 교사의 기대만으로 성취가 바뀐다는 증거로 널리 인용되었지만, 후속 연구는 기대 효과가 실재하되 대체로 작다고 결론지었다는 흐름이므로 C가 정답이다. A는 '효과 없음'이라 했으나 지문은 효과가 '발생하지만 작다'고 하므로 과장이다. B는 과거 성적이 언급되긴 하지만, 영향력이 시간이 지나며 줄었다는 내용은 지문에 없다. D는 원 연구에서 저학년 효과가 컸다는 세부를 후속 연구의 결론으로 잘못 일반화했다.
g.explanation_en: The text describes a 1968 study widely cited as proof that teacher beliefs alone reshape achievement, then explains that later research found expectation effects do occur but are typically small, so C is correct. A goes too far: the text says the effects are real, just small, not absent. B misuses the mention of past grades; the text never says teacher influence declined over time. D takes the detail about early grades from the original study and wrongly presents it as the conclusion of later research.
g.design: The main idea requires combining the first paragraph's claim with the second paragraph's qualification; distractors A, B, and D each reuse a real detail (effects questioned, past grades, early grades) but distort how it connects to the conclusion.

c.seed: social science research — Sapir-Whorf Hypothesis on language structure shaping color perception across cultures

g.passage:
The idea that the words a language provides can shape how its speakers perceive the world, often associated with linguists Edward Sapir and Benjamin Lee Whorf, has been tested most rigorously in the domain of color. Russian, for example, uses two basic terms, "siniy" and "goluboy," for darker and lighter blues, whereas English uses only "blue." In a 2007 study, Jonathan Winawer and colleagues found that Russian speakers were faster than English speakers at telling apart two blues that fell on opposite sides of the siniy-goluboy boundary.

Yet the researchers also observed that this advantage disappeared when participants were asked to silently repeat a string of digits while performing the task, an activity that occupies verbal memory. Because Russian speakers' eyes did not change during the digit task, the result suggests that the language advantage depends on speakers actively drawing on their color words in the moment rather than on any permanent difference in how they see. Findings like these have led many researchers to favor a modest version of the hypothesis over the claim that language fixes the limits of perception.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Russian speakers perceive the color blue differently from English speakers because their language divides blue into two separate basic categories.
Experiments on color discrimination have shown that the words a language provides have no measurable effect on how its speakers perceive color.
Tasks that occupy verbal memory interfere with people's ability to distinguish colors, regardless of the language they speak.
Research on color discrimination indicates that language can influence perception, but mainly through speakers' real-time use of words rather than by permanently altering vision.
g.explanation: 지문은 러시아어 화자가 파란색 경계를 더 빨리 구분한다는 결과를 제시한 뒤, 언어 기억이 방해받으면 그 이점이 사라진다는 점을 들어 언어의 영향이 영구적 시각 변화가 아니라 실시간 단어 사용에 의존한다고 결론짓는다. 이 두 정보를 연결한 D가 정답이다. A는 첫 단락만 반영하며 '영구적으로 다르게 본다'는 해석은 둘째 단락이 부정한다. B는 언어 효과가 실제로 관찰되었으므로 지나치다. C는 숫자 과제가 모든 화자의 색 구분을 방해했다는 진술로, 지문은 러시아어 화자의 '이점'이 사라졌다고만 말한다.
g.explanation_en: The text first reports that Russian speakers distinguish blues across their two-term boundary faster, then shows that this advantage vanishes when verbal memory is occupied, concluding that language's effect depends on in-the-moment word use rather than permanent changes in vision. D connects both pieces, so it is correct. A reflects only the first paragraph and claims a lasting perceptual difference, which the second paragraph undercuts. B goes too far, since a language effect was in fact observed. C overgeneralizes: the text says only that the Russian speakers' advantage disappeared, not that everyone's color discrimination was impaired.
g.design: 첫 단락만 훑으면 A를, 숫자 과제 세부만 보면 C를 고르도록 설계하여 두 단락의 연결을 요구했다.

c.seed: social science research — Milgram Obedience Studies on authority compliance and moral responsibility boundaries

g.passage: In Stanley Milgram's obedience experiments of the early 1960s, volunteers were told to give what they believed were increasingly strong electric shocks to another person whenever that person answered a question wrongly. Many participants kept going while an experimenter calmly urged them on, and this result is often summarized as proof that ordinary people will obey any authority. Later analyses of Milgram's own records point to a narrower conclusion. Obedience fell sharply when the experimenter gave instructions by telephone, when two other "teachers" refused to continue, and when the study was moved from Yale University to a shabby office building. Also, when the experimenter said outright, "You have no other choice, you must go on," almost every participant who heard it stopped. Participants seemed willing to continue mainly when they could see themselves as helping a legitimate scientific project, not when they were simply being given orders.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: A closer look at Milgram's studies suggests that participants' compliance depended on specific circumstances, especially whether they saw the research as worthwhile and legitimate.
A closer look at Milgram's studies suggests that participants obeyed authority figures without question whenever those figures stayed calm and confident.
A closer look at Milgram's studies suggests that participants' compliance depended mostly on the prestige of Yale University, rather than on how instructions were given.
A closer look at Milgram's studies suggests that participants stopped obeying mainly because they felt other volunteers were watching them.
g.explanation: 지문은 '사람은 어떤 권위에도 복종한다'는 통념을 소개한 뒤, 여러 조건에서 복종이 줄었고 직접적 명령에는 오히려 중단했다는 근거를 들어 참가자들이 정당한 과학 연구를 돕는다고 여길 때만 계속했다고 결론짓는다. 따라서 A가 중심 생각이다. B는 지문이 반박하는 통념을 그대로 되풀이한다. C는 장소 변화라는 한 가지 세부 사항만 과장했고, 지문은 전화 지시나 명령 문구 같은 지시 방식도 중요했다고 말한다. D는 동료 '교사'의 거부라는 하나의 조건만 일반화한 것이며, 지문은 남이 지켜보는 것을 원인으로 들지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The text first presents the popular belief that people will obey any authority. It then challenges that belief by showing that obedience dropped under several conditions and that a direct order actually made people stop. It concludes that participants kept going when they saw themselves as helping legitimate science, so A is correct. B just repeats the popular belief that the text argues against. C blows up one detail, the change of location, and ignores the text's point that how instructions were given (by phone, or as a direct order) also mattered. D turns one condition, the other teachers refusing, into a general claim, and the text never says that being watched was the reason participants stopped.
g.design: Every option uses the same opening, so students have to tell the passage's overall claim apart from the popular view it rejects (B) and from single details stretched too far (C, D).

c.seed: social science research — Third Place Theory defining social gathering spaces beyond home and workplace

g.passage: In 1989, sociologist Ray Oldenburg introduced the term "third places" to describe informal gathering spots, such as cafés, barbershops, and neighborhood pubs, that are distinct from the home (the first place) and the workplace (the second). Many later writers treated the concept mainly as a celebration of cozy businesses, and some urban designers assumed that any attractive public venue would qualify. Oldenburg's own account, however, was more demanding. He argued that what makes a location a third place is not its décor or even its function but the kind of interaction it fosters: regulars who return without invitation, conversation as the main activity, and a leveling atmosphere in which visitors' jobs and incomes matter little. By this standard, a stylish coffee shop where customers work silently on laptops may fail to be a third place, while a plain corner diner full of chatting regulars may succeed.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Oldenburg argued that cafés and diners are better suited than homes and workplaces to fostering conversation among people of different incomes.
Oldenburg defined third places by the patterns of social interaction they support rather than by their appearance or the type of business they house.
Oldenburg believed that urban designers could create third places by building attractive public venues that draw regular visitors.
Oldenburg claimed that modern coffee shops have replaced traditional diners as the most common gathering spots outside home and work.
g.explanation: 이 글은 Oldenburg의 '제3의 장소' 개념이 흔히 오해되고 있으며, 실제로는 장식이나 기능이 아니라 그곳에서 생기는 상호작용(단골, 대화, 평등한 분위기)으로 정의된다고 말하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 대화와 소득 무관성이라는 세부를 담고 있지만, 카페가 집이나 직장보다 '더 낫다'는 비교는 글에 없다. C는 글에서 디자이너들의 잘못된 가정으로 제시된 내용을 Oldenburg의 견해로 바꿔 놓았다. D는 커피숍과 식당이라는 예시를 언급하지만, 둘 중 어느 쪽이 더 흔한지는 글에서 다루지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The text says Oldenburg's concept is often misunderstood. For him, a third place is defined by the interaction it fosters (regulars, conversation, and a leveling atmosphere), not by its décor or function, so B is correct. A picks up details about conversation and income, but the text never claims that cafés are better than homes or workplaces at fostering conversation. C takes the mistaken assumption the text assigns to urban designers and presents it as Oldenburg's own view. D mentions the coffee shop and diner examples, but the text never says which kind of place is more common.
g.design: 오답 선택지에는 지문 속 세부 내용(대화, 디자이너, 커피숍)을 일부러 넣어, 훑어 읽으면 맞는 답처럼 보이게 했다. 정답을 고르려면 대중적 오해와 Oldenburg 자신의 기준을 구분해야 한다.

c.seed: social science research — Broken Windows Theory linking minor disorder to increased serious crime in neighborhoods

g.passage: In 1982, social scientists James Q. Wilson and George Kelling proposed that visible signs of minor disorder in a neighborhood, such as broken windows, graffiti, and litter, signal that no one is in control, thereby inviting more serious crime. The idea, known as the Broken Windows Theory, shaped policing in several major cities, where officers began aggressively targeting small offenses. Later researchers, however, noted that crime fell during the same period in cities that did not adopt such tactics. Studies by sociologists Robert Sampson and Stephen Raudenbush further suggested that disorder and serious crime may both stem from deeper neighborhood conditions, such as concentrated poverty and weak ties among residents, rather than one directly causing the other.
g.question: According to the text, what did later research suggest about the relationship examined by Wilson and Kelling?
options: Minor disorder directly caused serious crime, but only in neighborhoods with concentrated poverty.
Minor disorder caused serious crime in cities whose police aggressively targeted small offenses.
Minor disorder and serious crime may both result from other underlying features of neighborhoods.
Minor disorder and serious crime declined only in cities that adopted Wilson and Kelling's recommendations.

Moreover, the chance that someone stepped in rose as the number of onlookers grew. Philpot's team does not dismiss the earlier laboratory findings; rather, they argue that while any single witness in a crowd may feel less personally obligated, a larger group simply contains more potential helpers, making it more likely that at least one of them will act.

g.passage: Psychologist Albert Bandura proposed that most people who act unethically do not simply abandon their moral standards. g.explanation: 지문은 회전 과제에서 언어 집단별로 다른 전략이 나타났음을 제시하고, 환경 차이라는 비판을 소개한 뒤, 같은 환경의 화자를 비교한 후속 연구에서도 언어가 전략을 예측했다고 결론 내린다. 따라서 A가 중심 생각이다. B는 비판자의 주장만 반영하며 후속 연구 결과와 어긋난다. C는 '정확도'를 말하지만 지문은 우열이 아니라 전략의 차이만 다룬다. D는 지문이 과제의 해석에 대한 비판을 다루기는 하지만 과제 자체가 무의미하다고 말하지 않으므로 지나치다.
g.explanation_en: The text describes a rotation task in which the two language groups used different strategies, presents the objection that their environments also differed, and then reports that studies comparing speakers in the same environment still found that language predicts strategy. C talks about accuracy, but the text describes different strategies, not one group doing better than the other. D goes too far: the critics question how to interpret the results, but the text never says the task can't reveal anything about mental representation.
g.design: To answer correctly, the student has to connect the original finding, the critique, and the follow-up evidence. B is the trap for students who skim and stop at the critique. C and D build on partial evidence from the text but overreach.

c.seed: social science research — Contact Hypothesis reducing prejudice through structured intergroup cooperation in schools

g.passage: Psychologist Gordon Allport proposed in 1954 that contact between members of different groups can reduce prejudice, but only under certain conditions: the groups must have equal status in the situation, pursue shared goals, and receive support from authorities. Later researchers tested this idea in schools, where simply placing students of different backgrounds in the same building often did little to change attitudes. In "jigsaw" classrooms, by contrast, each student in a mixed group was given one piece of a lesson that the others needed in order to complete an assignment. Because no student could succeed without the others, classmates came to depend on one another. Studies of such classrooms found that students in them reported more favorable views of peers from other groups than did students in conventionally taught classes, even though both sets of students attended the same integrated schools.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Research in schools showed that bringing students from different backgrounds into the same building was sufficient to reduce prejudice, as Allport had predicted.
Research in schools suggests that intergroup contact lessens prejudice most when it is organized so that students rely on one another to reach a common objective.
Research in schools suggests that jigsaw classrooms improved students' academic performance more than conventional classes did.
Research in schools showed that Allport's conditions for reducing prejudice could not be met in integrated schools.
g.explanation: 이 글은 Allport의 조건(공동 목표 등)을 소개한 뒤, 단순히 같은 학교에 다니는 것만으로는 효과가 적었지만 서로 의존하도록 구성된 jigsaw 수업에서는 편견이 줄었다는 결과를 제시하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 단순한 접촉이 '거의 효과가 없었다'는 지문 내용과 정반대이다. C는 jigsaw 수업을 언급하지만, 지문이 측정한 것은 학업 성취가 아니라 다른 집단 친구에 대한 태도이다. D는 jigsaw 수업이 통합 학교 안에서 Allport의 조건을 실현해 성과를 낸 것과 모순된다.
g.explanation_en: The text presents Allport's conditions, such as shared goals, and then shows that mere co-attendance did little, while jigsaw classrooms that made students depend on one another produced more favorable attitudes, so B is correct. A contradicts the statement that simply placing students in the same building often did little to change attitudes. C mentions jigsaw classrooms, but the studies measured views of peers, not academic performance. D is contradicted because jigsaw classrooms successfully met those conditions within integrated schools.
g.design: 정답은 '상호의존'을 다른 말로 바꿔 표면 일치를 피했고, A·C는 지문의 일부 사실(같은 건물, jigsaw)을 끌어와 정독해야 배제되도록 했다.

c.seed: social science research — Just-World Hypothesis causing victim-blaming and defensive attribution in misfortune situations

g.passage: Psychologist Melvin Lerner proposed that many people hold an unspoken belief that the world is fair: good things happen to good people, and bad things happen to those who somehow deserve them. In a series of experiments, Lerner found that observers who watched a participant receive what appeared to be painful electric shocks often rated that participant less favorably, especially when they were told they could do nothing to stop the shocks. Later researchers built on this work, arguing that such judgments are not simply expressions of cruelty. Instead, they suggest, blaming a victim allows observers to preserve the comforting sense that misfortune is predictable and avoidable, and therefore unlikely to strike them. Consistent with this view, studies have shown that people tend to blame victims most harshly when the victims' circumstances closely resemble their own, since a random misfortune befalling someone similar would be the most threatening to their belief in a fair world.
g.question: According to the text, why do observers sometimes judge people who suffer misfortune unfavorably?
options: Observers judge such people unfavorably because they feel guilty about being unable to prevent the suffering they witness.
Observers judge such people unfavorably because they assume that people who resemble them are more likely to have acted carelessly.
Observers judge such people unfavorably because doing so protects their sense that harm follows from avoidable causes and so will not happen to them.
Observers judge such people unfavorably because experiments like Lerner's encourage them to view participants as deserving of punishment.
g.explanation: 지문은 피해자를 탓하는 것이 불운이 예측·회피 가능하다는, 그래서 자신에게는 일어나지 않으리라는 위안을 지켜 준다고 설명하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 관찰자가 고통을 멈출 수 없었다는 세부를 이용하지만, 지문은 죄책감을 원인으로 제시하지 않는다. B는 자신과 비슷한 피해자를 가장 심하게 탓한다는 내용을 왜곡한 것으로, 그 이유는 부주의를 가정해서가 아니라 공정한 세상에 대한 믿음이 가장 크게 위협받기 때문이다. D는 실험 자체가 원인인 것처럼 말하지만, 지문에서 실험은 이 경향을 드러낸 것이지 만들어 낸 것이 아니다.
g.explanation_en: C is correct because the text says that blaming a victim preserves the comforting sense that misfortune is predictable and avoidable, and so is unlikely to strike the observer. A borrows the detail that observers couldn't stop the shocks, but the text never says guilt is the cause. B twists the finding about similar victims: they're blamed most harshly because they pose the biggest threat to belief in a fair world, not because observers assume they were careless. D treats the experiments as the cause, but in the text the experiments only revealed the tendency. They didn't create it.
g.design: 이 문항은 지문에 명시된 이유를 묻는다. 정답을 고르려면 두 단계가 필요하다. 먼저 "예측 가능하고 피할 수 있다"는 내용과 "자신에게는 일어나지 않을 것"이라는 내용을 연결하고, 그다음 "harm follows from avoidable causes"로 바꿔 쓴 표현을 알아봐야 한다. 오답 A와 B는 지문의 실제 세부(고통을 멈출 수 없음, 자신과 비슷한 피해자)를 이용하지만 원인을 잘못 붙였다.

c.seed: social science research — Sunk Cost Fallacy driving continued investment in failing relationships and projects

g.passage: Economists have long described the sunk cost fallacy as the tendency to keep investing in a failing endeavor simply because resources have already been spent on it. Psychologist Christopher Olivola wondered whether this tendency was limited to money and business decisions or whether it also shaped personal choices. In a series of studies, he presented participants with scenarios involving romantic relationships, friendships, and long-running hobbies, varying only how much time or effort had already gone into each. Participants who read that years had been invested in a struggling relationship were noticeably more likely to recommend staying in it than were participants who read about an equally troubled relationship of only a few months, even though the expected future benefits were described as identical. Olivola concluded that people treat past effort, not just past spending, as a reason to persist, which suggests the fallacy reaches well beyond the financial settings where it was first identified.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Olivola's research shows that people are more likely to stay in long relationships because those relationships offer greater future benefits than short ones do.
Olivola's research shows that the sunk cost fallacy influences financial decisions more strongly than it influences decisions about friendships and hobbies.
Olivola's research shows that economists were mistaken to define the sunk cost fallacy as a tendency that involves previously spent resources.
Olivola's research shows that prior investments of time and effort can lead people to persist in personal commitments, not only in monetary ones.
g.explanation: 지문은 매몰비용 오류가 돈 문제에만 국한되는지 의문을 제기하고, 연구 결과 시간·노력 같은 과거 투자도 관계 유지 판단에 영향을 준다는 결론을 제시하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 긴 관계를 유지하는 경향은 맞지만, 지문은 미래 이익이 동일하다고 명시했으므로 '더 큰 미래 이익' 때문이라는 이유가 틀렸다. B는 금융 영역과 개인 영역을 언급하지만 둘의 영향 강도를 비교한 내용은 지문에 없다. C는 경제학자의 정의를 언급하지만 Olivola는 그 정의를 틀렸다고 한 것이 아니라 적용 범위를 넓혔을 뿐이다.
g.explanation_en: The text asks whether the sunk cost fallacy is limited to money, then reports that past time and effort also pushed participants to recommend staying in personal commitments, so D is correct. A is right that people favored staying in long relationships, but the text says the expected future benefits were identical, so the reason A gives is wrong. B mentions both financial and personal settings, but the text never compares how strongly the fallacy works in each. C refers to the economists' definition, but Olivola didn't reject that definition; he just showed that it applies more broadly.
g.design: To get the answer, you have to connect the research question in the opening with the conclusion at the end. Each wrong answer borrows a real detail from the text (long relationships, financial settings, the economists' definition) but misstates how it relates to the findings.

c.seed: social science research — Echo Chamber Effect amplifying political polarization through algorithmic social media feeds

g.passage: Many commentators assume that algorithmic news feeds trap users in "echo chambers," showing them only views they already hold and thereby driving political polarization. To test this assumption, sociologist Mara Okonjo and colleagues tracked the feeds of several thousand volunteers over six months. Contrary to expectations, most participants regularly encountered posts from the opposing political side; their feeds were far less one-sided than the echo chamber image suggests. Yet participants' attitudes still grew more extreme over the study period. Okonjo's team found that the shift was linked not to a lack of exposure but to the kind of opposing content the algorithms favored: because posts provoking strong reactions are ranked highly, users mostly saw the angriest, most hostile examples of the other side's views. The researchers argue that polarization may therefore stem less from isolation than from repeated contact with the most inflammatory versions of opposing opinions.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Research suggests that algorithmic feeds may intensify political divisions not by shielding users from other viewpoints but by highlighting the most provocative expressions of those viewpoints.
Research suggests that algorithmic feeds may intensify political divisions by shielding users from other viewpoints, as commentators have long claimed.
Research suggests that algorithmic feeds may reduce political divisions because most users regularly encounter posts from the opposing side.
Research suggests that algorithmic feeds may intensify political divisions mainly because users deliberately seek out angry content that confirms their own beliefs.
g.design: 통념(반향실)과 연구 결과(노출은 있으나 자극적 콘텐츠 노출)의 두 정보를 연결해야 하며, 오답은 통념 수용, 노출 사실만 확대 해석, 원인 주체를 사용자로 바꾼 진술로 구성했다.
g.explanation: 지문은 반향실 통념과 달리 사용자들이 반대 진영 게시물을 자주 접했지만, 알고리즘이 가장 적대적인 게시물을 우선 노출해 양극화가 심해졌다고 말하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 연구가 반박한 통념을 그대로 따르는 진술이다. C는 반대 의견 노출이라는 사실은 맞지만 연구에서는 태도가 오히려 더 극단화되었으므로 틀리다. D는 '분노'라는 요소를 언급하지만, 지문은 사용자의 의도적 선택이 아니라 알고리즘의 순위 결정 방식을 원인으로 꼽는다.
g.explanation_en: The text says that, unlike the echo chamber assumption, users often saw posts from the other side, but the algorithms pushed the most hostile of those posts to the top, and attitudes became more extreme. That makes A correct. B repeats the assumption the study actually challenges. C gets the exposure finding right, but participants' attitudes became more extreme, not less. D mentions angry content, but the text blames the way the algorithm ranks posts, not users choosing that content on purpose.

c.seed: social science research — Authoritarian Personality Traits predicting obedience and prejudice across cultural populations

g.passage: For decades after its introduction in 1950, the F-scale, a questionnaire designed to measure "authoritarian personality" traits such as rigid deference to authority and hostility toward outsiders, was treated as a reliable predictor of both obedience and prejudice. Most of the supporting evidence, however, came from surveys of white, middle-class respondents in the United States. When social psychologist Anika Brandt and colleagues administered a revised version of the scale to adults in eleven countries, they found that high scorers everywhere tended to report greater willingness to follow orders from superiors. The link between high scores and prejudice, by contrast, varied sharply: it was strong in some samples but nearly absent in others, particularly where the groups regarded as outsiders were themselves favored by local authorities.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Brandt's team showed that the F-scale cannot predict any attitude reliably once it is used outside the United States.
Brandt's team found that one long-assumed outcome of authoritarian traits held across cultures, while the other depended on local circumstances.
Brandt's team concluded that prejudice is a stronger consequence of authoritarian traits than obedience is in most societies.
Brandt's team revised the F-scale mainly because earlier versions had relied on samples of white, middle-class Americans.
g.explanation: 지문은 F-척도가 복종과 편견을 모두 예측한다고 여겨졌으나, 11개국 연구에서 복종과의 연관은 일관되게 나타난 반면 편견과의 연관은 현지 권위자가 외부 집단을 어떻게 대하느냐에 따라 달라졌다고 말하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 미국 밖에서 척도가 아무것도 예측하지 못한다고 과장하는데, 복종 예측은 모든 곳에서 유지되었다. C는 관계를 뒤집은 것으로, 일관되게 나타난 것은 편견이 아니라 복종이었다. D는 표본의 한계라는 지문 속 세부 정보를 언급하지만, 그것을 개정의 이유로 단정할 뿐 연구 결과라는 핵심을 담지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: The text says the F-scale was assumed to predict both obedience and prejudice. Brandt's eleven-country study found that the link to obedience showed up everywhere, while the link to prejudice depended on whether local authorities favored outsider groups, so B is correct. A goes too far: the scale still predicted obedience in every country. C reverses the findings, since obedience, not prejudice, was the consistent outcome. D picks up a real detail about the limited earlier samples, but it treats that detail as the reason for the revision and leaves out the study's main finding.
g.design: To get the answer, students have to connect the two original predictions with the two different cross-cultural results. A and D each draw on true details from the text (an inconsistent result, and the narrow earlier samples), while C reverses which result was stable.

c.seed: social science research — Code-Switching Behavior among multilingual speakers adapting language in different social contexts

g.passage: Linguists once treated code-switching—the practice of alternating between two or more languages within a single conversation—as evidence that a speaker lacked full command of either language. Sociolinguist Ana Celia Zentella challenged this view through years of observation in a bilingual New York neighborhood, where children moved fluidly between Spanish and English. She found that the switches were rarely random: children shifted languages to signal a change in topic, to quote someone, to include or exclude a listener, or to soften a request. Moreover, the children who switched most often tended to be those with the strongest skills in both languages, since switching smoothly at grammatically appropriate points required knowing how each language's rules worked.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Zentella's research showed that children in bilingual neighborhoods use Spanish mainly when discussing family matters and English mainly when discussing school.
Zentella's research showed that code-switching is most common among children who are still learning one of their two languages.
Zentella's research showed that code-switching reflects skilled, purposeful language use rather than a gap in a speaker's abilities.
Zentella's research showed that children switch languages chiefly to exclude listeners who do not understand both languages.
g.explanation: 지문은 코드스위칭을 언어 능력 부족의 증거로 본 기존 견해를 소개한 뒤, Zentella의 연구가 전환이 목적에 따라 이루어지며 두 언어 모두에 능숙한 아이들이 가장 많이 전환한다는 점을 보여 주었다고 설명한다. 이 두 정보를 종합한 C가 중심 생각이다. A는 주제에 따라 언어를 바꾼다는 내용을 부풀린 것으로, 가족/학교 구분은 지문에 나오지 않는다. B는 가장 자주 전환하는 아이들이 두 언어 모두에 가장 능숙했다는 지문 내용과 반대된다. D는 여러 목적 중 하나(청자 배제)만을 주된 이유로 과장했다.
g.explanation_en: The text opens with the old view that code-switching shows a speaker lacks full command of a language. It then explains that Zentella found switches were purposeful and that the children who switched most were the most skilled in both languages. c.seed: social science research — Reactance Theory explaining resistance when personal freedoms face perceived restrictions

g.passage: In 1966, psychologist Jack Brehm proposed reactance theory to explain a puzzling pattern: people sometimes respond to persuasion by doing the opposite of what they are urged to do. According to Brehm, individuals hold beliefs about which behaviors they are free to choose, and when they perceive that one of those freedoms is being eliminated or threatened, they experience an unpleasant motivational state he called reactance. This state pushes them to restore the threatened freedom, often by valuing the forbidden option more highly or by deliberately performing the discouraged behavior. Later researchers found that the strength of this response depends less on what a message asks for than on how it is framed. In one study, students read identical recommendations to limit their alcohol intake; those who received forceful wording such as "you must" and "any reasonable person would agree" reported stronger intentions to drink than did those who received the same advice phrased as a suggestion.
g.question: According to the text, what did later research reveal about the response Brehm described?
options: The response is strongest when a message asks people to give up a behavior they already value highly.
The response occurs mainly among students, who are especially sensitive to limits on drinking alcohol.
The response fades once people recognize that the advice they received is reasonable.
The response is shaped more by the controlling tone of a message than by its actual content.
g.design: 질문은 'framing/wording' 어휘를 피하고 'later research'로 위치만 지정해, 지문의 '요청 내용보다 표현 방식' 진술과 연구 사례를 연결해야 D를 고를 수 있게 했다. A·B·C는 지문의 어휘(value, students, reasonable)를 차용한 부분 근거 오답이다.
g.explanation: 지문은 후속 연구가 반발의 강도가 메시지가 요구하는 내용보다 그 표현 방식에 달려 있음을 발견했다고 말하며, 같은 권고라도 강압적 문구를 받은 학생들이 더 강한 음주 의도를 보였다고 제시한다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 'valuing the forbidden option more highly'를 차용했지만 이는 반발의 결과일 뿐, 이미 높이 평가하는 행동일수록 반응이 강하다는 내용은 없다. B는 연구 대상이 학생이었다는 점만 일반화한 것으로 지문 근거가 없다. c.seed: social science research — Linguistic Markedness asymmetries in color term hierarchies across world languages

g.passage:
In 1969, Brent Berlin and Paul Kay proposed that languages add basic color terms in a predictable order: a language with only two terms distinguishes dark from light, a third term is almost always red, and terms for categories such as brown or purple appear only in languages that already name green, yellow, and blue. Later researchers have interpreted this pattern through the linguistic concept of markedness, which holds that some categories are treated as default, or "unmarked," while others depend on them. Supporting this view, words for early-sequence colors tend to be shorter, appear more often in everyday speech, and are learned earlier by children than words for late-sequence colors.

Yet linguist Delia Moreno argues that markedness describes the pattern without fully explaining it. In her survey of 62 languages, she found that the order in which communities adopted new color terms often matched the introduction of dyed goods and painted objects through trade. Communities with little exposure to such artifacts kept small color vocabularies even when their neighbors had large ones. Moreno concludes that the asymmetries among color terms reflect not only how perception is organized but also which distinctions a society has practical reasons to name.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Although color terms follow an order that markedness can describe, one researcher argues that cultural contact with colored artifacts also helps determine which terms a language develops.
Although color terms follow an order that markedness can describe, one researcher argues that children's word learning is the main reason early-sequence terms are shorter.
Although color terms once followed an order that markedness could describe, one researcher argues that trade has now erased the differences among languages' color vocabularies.
Although color terms follow an order that markedness can describe, one researcher argues that perception plays no role in which terms a language develops.
g.explanation: 지문은 색채어가 예측 가능한 순서로 생기며 유표성 개념으로 설명된다는 점을 소개한 뒤, Moreno가 색을 입힌 물건의 교역 노출 같은 사회적 요인도 순서를 결정한다고 주장한다는 내용이므로 A가 정답이다. B는 아동의 어휘 습득을 언급하지만, 이는 유표성을 뒷받침하는 근거일 뿐 Moreno의 주장이 아니다. C는 교역을 언급하지만, 지문은 노출이 적은 공동체가 작은 어휘를 유지했다고 하므로 차이가 사라졌다는 진술과 모순된다. D는 'not only ... but also'로 지각의 역할을 인정한 결론을 지나치게 극단화했다.
g.explanation_en: The text first presents the predictable order of color terms and its markedness interpretation, then reports Moreno's argument that exposure to dyed and painted goods through trade also shapes which terms appear, so A is correct. B mentions children's learning, but that is evidence for the markedness view, not Moreno's argument. C mentions trade, yet the text says communities with little exposure kept small vocabularies, so differences were not erased. D overstates Moreno's conclusion: her phrase "not only... but also" means perception still plays a role.
g.design: 네 선택지를 같은 문장 틀로 만들어 후반부만 다르게 했고, B·C는 지문 세부(아동 습득, 교역)를 차용해 부분적으로 맞아 보이게 했으며, D는 'not only'를 놓치면 고를 수 있는 함정이다.

c.seed: social science research — Terror Management Theory linking mortality awareness to defensive worldview reinforcement

g.passage: Terror Management Theory, developed by psychologists Jeff Greenberg, Sheldon Solomon, and Tom Pyszczynski, proposes that awareness of one's own mortality creates a potential for deep anxiety, which people manage partly by investing in cultural worldviews that promise lasting meaning. In early experiments, participants who were asked to write briefly about their own death later judged people who violated shared cultural norms more harshly than did participants who wrote about a neutral topic. Critics have noted that some recent large-scale replication attempts produced weaker effects than the original studies did. Yet even researchers who question the size of the effect generally agree that the original findings were important: they pushed psychology to treat existential concerns, once considered the domain of philosophers, as something that could be tested in the laboratory.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Terror Management Theory has been discredited by recent replication attempts, though it remains popular among philosophers who study existential concerns.
Although questions remain about how strong its effects are, Terror Management Theory helped make questions about how people face death a subject of experimental study.
Experiments on Terror Management Theory show that thinking about death makes people judge norm violators more harshly than any other topic does.
Terror Management Theory has persuaded most psychologists that cultural worldviews exist mainly to reduce anxiety about death.
g.explanation: 이 글은 이론과 초기 실험을 소개한 뒤, 재현 연구에서 효과가 약하게 나왔다는 비판이 있지만 이 이론이 실존적 관심사를 실험적으로 연구하게 만들었다는 데에는 대체로 동의한다는 결론으로 끝난다. 따라서 이 두 가지를 모두 담은 B가 정답이다. A는 재현 연구의 효과가 '더 약했다'는 내용을 '신빙성을 잃었다'로 과장했고, 철학자들 사이에서 인기가 있다는 말은 글에 없다. C는 실험 내용을 일부 반영하지만 비교 대상은 중립적인 주제 하나뿐이었으므로 '다른 어떤 주제보다'는 지나친 일반화이며, 세부 내용일 뿐 중심 생각도 아니다. D는 이론의 주장을 대부분의 심리학자가 받아들였다고 서술하지만, 글에서 연구자들이 동의한 것은 원래 연구가 중요했다는 점뿐이다.
g.explanation_en: The text introduces the theory and its early experiments, mentions critics who point to weaker replication results, and then ends on its main point: researchers broadly agree that the theory made existential concerns something that could be tested in experiments. B captures both the doubts and that lasting contribution, so B is correct. A exaggerates "weaker effects" into "discredited," and the text never says the theory is popular among philosophers. C draws on the experiment, but participants were compared only with people who wrote about a neutral topic, so "any other topic" goes too far, and it's a detail rather than the main idea anyway. D says most psychologists accept the theory's claim about worldviews, but the only thing the text says researchers agree on is that the original findings were important.
g.design: To answer correctly, students have to connect the critics' doubts with the agreement that follows "Yet." A, C, and D each take a real part of the text and push it too far.

c.seed: social science research — Moral Licensing allowing ethical behavior to justify subsequent unethical actions

g.passage: Psychologists studying moral licensing have found that people who have recently done something virtuous sometimes feel freer to act selfishly afterward, as though their good deed had earned them credit to spend. In one series of experiments, participants who first chose an environmentally friendly product later kept more money for themselves in an unrelated sharing task than did participants who had chosen a conventional product. Researchers Anna Merritt and Daniel Effron, however, have noted that the effect does not appear uniformly. When participants were prompted to view their earlier good act as an expression of who they are, rather than as an achievement they had completed, the later lapse in generosity often shrank or disappeared. The way people interpret their own virtue, in other words, appears to shape whether that virtue licenses later misconduct.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Choosing environmentally friendly products tends to make people less generous in later financial decisions than choosing conventional products does.
Moral licensing occurs mainly in laboratory settings and rarely appears in people's everyday choices outside experiments.
Whether a past good deed leads people to behave less ethically later depends partly on how they understand that deed.
People who see themselves as fundamentally virtuous are more likely than others to perform good deeds in the first place.
g.explanation: 지문은 도덕적 면허 효과를 소개한 뒤, 이전 선행을 정체성의 표현으로 볼 때 효과가 줄어든다는 점을 들어 '선행을 어떻게 해석하느냐가 이후 비윤리적 행동 여부를 좌우한다'고 결론짓는다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 실험 한 가지 결과로 지문에 나오기는 하지만, 효과가 균일하지 않다는 핵심 내용을 빠뜨린 세부 사항에 불과하다. B는 실험실과 일상의 차이를 다루는데, 지문에 없는 내용이다. D는 '자신을 어떻게 보는가'라는 소재를 빌려 왔지만, 선행을 처음에 할 가능성에 대한 주장은 지문에 나오지 않는다.

c.seed: social science research — Linguistic Taboo topics showing avoidance patterns and euphemism use in speech

g.passage: Linguists have long assumed that speakers replace taboo words with euphemisms mainly to spare listeners discomfort. Sociolinguist Mara Kessel tested this idea by recording conversations about death and illness among hospital staff and comparing them with conversations on the same topics among the staff's friends outside work. If politeness toward listeners were the main driver, euphemisms should have been most frequent when staff spoke with grieving families. __Instead, Kessel found that staff used the most euphemisms when talking with one another, even though colleagues were the listeners least likely to be upset by blunt terms.__ Kessel suggests that euphemism among professionals may serve less to protect listeners than to help speakers keep emotional distance from difficult subjects.

g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 청자 배려 가설이 예측한 것(유족과의 대화에서 완곡어 최다)과 달리 동료끼리 완곡어가 가장 많았다는 결과를 보고하며, 마지막 문장의 대안 설명(화자의 정서적 거리 두기)을 준비하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 동료가 가장 덜 동요한다는 언급은 있지만 문장이 연구 방법을 설명하지는 않는다. B는 결과가 기존 가정을 지지하는 것이 아니라 반박하므로 방향이 반대이다. C의 정서적 거리 개념은 마지막 문장의 내용이며 밑줄 문장은 결론이 아니라 그 근거가 되는 결과이다.

c.seed: social science research — Social Comparison Theory driving self-evaluation through upward and downward comparison processes

g.passage: According to social comparison theory, first proposed by psychologist Leon Festinger in 1954, people judge their own abilities by measuring themselves against others, especially when no objective standard is available. Later researchers distinguished two directions of comparison: upward comparison, in which people look to those who are doing better, and downward comparison, in which they look to those who are doing worse. Early studies tended to link upward comparison with lower self-esteem and downward comparison with comfort. __Yet a 1997 study by Penelope Lockwood and Ziva Kunda found that students who read about a highly successful peer in their own field sometimes felt more motivated, not less, provided they believed similar success was within their reach.__ Findings like this suggest that how a comparison affects a person depends less on its direction than on whether the person sees the other's position as attainable.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents evidence that complicates an earlier pattern and prepares for the text's broader conclusion.
It presents evidence that confirms an earlier pattern and extends it to a new group of people.
It presents evidence that explains why Festinger first proposed the theory described at the start of the text.
It presents evidence that reveals a flaw in how early researchers designed their studies of comparison.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 "Yet"으로 시작해 상향 비교가 자존감을 낮춘다는 초기 연구 경향과 달리 상향 비교가 오히려 동기를 높일 수 있음을 보여 주고, 마지막 문장의 '도달 가능성' 결론으로 이어지므로 A가 정답이다. B는 문장이 초기 경향을 확인한다고 하지만 실제로는 반박·복잡화한다. C는 Festinger의 이론 제안 동기를 설명한다고 하지만 1997년 연구는 이론의 기원과 무관하다. D는 초기 연구의 설계 결함을 말하지만, 지문은 방법론 비판 없이 결과의 해석만 수정한다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence opens with "Yet" and shows that upward comparison can sometimes increase motivation, which runs against the earlier pattern linking it to lower self-esteem. It also sets up the final sentence's conclusion about attainability, so A is correct. B is wrong because the sentence challenges the earlier pattern instead of confirming it. c.seed: social science research — Linguistic Atlas Project documenting dialectal variation across American English speaking regions

g.passage: Beginning in the 1930s, fieldworkers for the Linguistic Atlas Project traveled through communities along the eastern United States, asking residents what they called everyday items such as a dragonfly, a frying pan, or a paper bag. The resulting maps revealed sharp boundaries: "darning needle" clustered in one region, "snake feeder" in another. For decades, scholars treated these boundaries as fixed features of American speech. __Yet the fieldworkers had deliberately sought out older, lifelong rural residents with little schooling, reasoning that such speakers best preserved local forms.__ Later researchers argued that this sampling choice may have made regional differences appear more stable and distinct than they were among the broader population, where mobility and education were already blurring the lines.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It explains why the fieldworkers chose to ask about everyday objects rather than about grammar or pronunciation.
It identifies a feature of how the data were gathered that is used to call an earlier interpretation into question.
It offers evidence that the regional boundaries shown on the maps were confirmed by later researchers.
It describes a method the fieldworkers adopted after discovering that their initial maps were inaccurate.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 조사자들이 나이 많고 교육 수준이 낮은 농촌 주민만 골라 조사했다는 표본 선정 방식을 소개하며, 'Yet'으로 경계가 고정적이라는 기존 해석에 반론의 실마리를 제공하고 다음 문장에서 그 의문이 구체화되므로 B가 정답이다. A는 이유를 설명한다는 점은 비슷하지만, 그 이유는 질문 항목 선택이 아니라 응답자 선택에 관한 것이다. C는 후대 연구자를 언급하지만, 그들은 경계를 확인한 것이 아니라 오히려 의문을 제기했다. D는 조사 방법을 다룬다는 점은 맞지만, 처음 지도가 부정확하다는 것을 발견한 뒤에 바꾼 방법이 아니라 처음부터 의도적으로 택한 방법이다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence describes how speakers were sampled: the fieldworkers chose older, rural, less-schooled residents. Its opening "Yet" and the sentence that follows show that this detail is used to challenge the view that the boundaries were fixed, so B is correct. A is about a reason, but the reason concerns which speakers were chosen, not which questions were asked. C mentions later researchers, but they questioned the boundaries rather than confirming them. D is about method, but the fieldworkers chose this approach deliberately from the start; they did not adopt it after finding errors in their maps.
g.design: To answer, you have to link the sampling detail to both the "Yet" pivot and the critique in the next sentence. The wrong choices each get part of it right (giving a reason, mentioning later researchers, describing a method), so you have to compare them carefully against the passage to rule them out.

c.seed: social science research — Behavioral Activation Intervention reducing depression through structured activity scheduling protocols

g.passage: Behavioral activation (BA) is a therapy for depression that asks patients to schedule small, concrete activities, such as a ten-minute walk or a phone call to a friend, and to record their mood before and after each one. Critics have argued that BA works only because patients are seeing a therapist regularly, so that any structured contact would produce the same benefit. To test this claim, psychologist Rhea Okonkwo assigned 212 adults with moderate depression either to BA or to weekly sessions with a therapist that included the same amount of contact but no activity scheduling. __After twelve weeks, the BA group reported symptom reductions nearly twice as large as those of the comparison group, even though both groups had spent the same number of hours with their therapists.__ Okonkwo concludes that the scheduling protocol itself, rather than therapist contact alone, accounts for much of BA's effect.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents a finding that supports the critics' view that regular therapist contact explains BA's benefits.
It describes the procedure Okonkwo used to make sure the two groups received equal amounts of therapist contact.
It presents a result that undermines the critics' explanation and sets up Okonkwo's conclusion.
It points out a limitation of Okonkwo's study that leaves the critics' explanation open to question.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 상담 시간이 같았는데도 BA 집단의 증상 감소가 두 배 가까이 컸다는 결과를 보여 준다. 이는 '상담 접촉 때문'이라는 비판자들의 설명을 약화시키고, 마지막 문장의 결론(활동 계획 자체가 효과의 원인)으로 이어지므로 C가 정답이다. A는 결과가 비판자들을 지지한다고 해서 방향이 반대이다. B는 '시간이 같았다'는 부분에만 주목했지만, 문장의 핵심은 절차가 아니라 결과이며 절차는 앞 문장에서 이미 설명되었다. D는 연구의 한계를 말한다고 하지만, 지문에는 한계가 전혀 제시되지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence reports that the BA group improved nearly twice as much as the other group, even though both groups spent the same amount of time with therapists. That result weakens the critics' claim that therapist contact explains BA's benefits, and it leads into Okonkwo's conclusion in the last sentence, so C is correct. A gets the direction backward, because the finding works against the critics, not for them. B fixes on the phrase about equal hours, but the sentence's main job is to report a result; the procedure was already described in the sentence before it. D calls the sentence a limitation of the study, but the text never mentions any limitation.
g.design: To answer, the student has to connect the result to both the critics' claim and the conclusion. The wrong answers each grab a piece of the sentence: the mention of therapist contact (A), the equal hours (B), and the critics (D).

c.seed: social science research — Anthropomorphism Tendency projecting human characteristics onto nonhuman animals in narratives

g.passage: Psychologists have long assumed that people attribute human traits to animals mainly when the animals look or act like humans—a chimpanzee frowning, say, or a dog appearing to sulk. To test whether the structure of a story also matters, researcher Lena Hartmann gave participants short accounts of a beetle's behavior. Half read a plain list of the beetle's actions; the other half read the same actions arranged as a sequence with a goal, an obstacle, and an outcome. __Participants in the second group were far more likely to describe the beetle as "determined," "frustrated," or "proud," even though neither version mentioned the insect's appearance or used any emotional language.__ Hartmann concludes that narrative form alone can prompt people to project inner lives onto creatures that bear little resemblance to humans.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents a finding that confirms the long-held assumption that animals' humanlike behavior drives the attribution of human traits.
It identifies a flaw in Hartmann's design by noting that the two versions of the account did not differ in emotional language.
It describes how Hartmann's two groups of participants were selected before they read the accounts of the beetle.
It reports a result that supports the claim that the arrangement of a story can, by itself, lead readers to attribute feelings to animals.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 같은 행동을 목표·장애·결과 구조로 읽은 집단이 딱정벌레에게 감정을 더 많이 부여했다는 결과를 보고하며, 외모나 감정 어휘라는 다른 설명을 배제한다. 그래서 이 결과는 마지막 문장의 결론, 즉 서사 형식만으로도 투사가 일어난다는 주장을 뒷받침하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 결과를 제시한다는 점은 맞지만, 이 결과는 기존 가정을 확인하는 것이 아니라 그 가정에 도전한다. B는 감정 어휘가 없었다는 세부를 언급하지만, 그 점은 설계상 결함이 아니라 의도적인 통제다. C는 실험 방법과 관련되지만, 밑줄 문장은 집단을 어떻게 선정했는지가 아니라 결과를 보고한다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence reports that readers who got the goal-obstacle-outcome version gave the beetle far more emotions. It also rules out other explanations, since neither version mentioned the insect's appearance or used emotional language. That result supports the conclusion in the last sentence: narrative form alone can trigger projection, so D is correct. A is right that the sentence presents a finding, but the finding challenges the long-held assumption instead of confirming it. B points to the lack of emotional language, but that was a deliberate control, not a flaw in the design. C has to do with the study's method, but the sentence reports results, not how the groups were selected.
g.design: 이 문항을 풀려면 두 정보를 연결해야 한다. 밑줄 문장의 결과를 확인하고, 그것이 첫 문장의 가정과 마지막 문장의 결론 중 어느 쪽을 뒷받침하는지 판단해야 한다. A와 B는 지문의 세부를 부분적으로 활용하지만 해석이 반대로 되어 있다.

c.seed: social science research — Ritual Synchrony research showing group bonding increases through coordinated movement

g.passage: Many researchers have proposed that moving in time with others—marching, dancing, rowing—strengthens social bonds. Skeptics, however, noted that in most early studies, participants who moved together also shared a common goal, so any increase in cooperation might have come from teamwork rather than from synchrony itself. To address this concern, psychologist Bahar Tunçgenç and colleagues asked pairs of strangers to tap along to separate metronomes that were either matched or slightly mismatched in tempo, with no shared task to complete. __Afterward, pairs whose tapping had been synchronized reported feeling closer to each other and gave more money to their partners in an economic game than did pairs whose tapping had been out of sync.__ These results suggest that coordinated movement can foster affiliation even when no collaborative purpose is present.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It reports a finding that indicates the skeptics' alternative explanation cannot fully account for the bonding effect.
It reports a finding that indicates shared goals strengthen bonds more than synchronized movement does.
It reports a finding that indicates the earlier studies were flawed because they measured cooperation inaccurately.
It reports a finding that indicates mismatched tempos cause strangers to distrust one another.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 공동 목표가 없는 조건에서도 동기화된 쌍이 더 큰 친밀감과 관대함을 보였다는 결과를 제시하므로, 회의론자들의 '팀워크 때문'이라는 대안 설명으로는 효과를 다 설명할 수 없음을 보여 준다(A). B는 실험에 공동 목표가 아예 없었으므로 목표와 동기화를 비교한 것이 아니어서 틀렸다. C는 회의론자들이 지적한 것은 측정의 부정확성이 아니라 변수 혼재였으므로 틀렸다. D는 비동기 쌍이 상대적으로 덜 가까웠을 뿐 불신이 생겼다는 근거는 없으므로 틀렸다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence shows that synchronized pairs felt closer and were more generous even though they had no shared task, so the skeptics' teamwork explanation can't fully explain the effect—that's A. B is wrong because the study removed shared goals entirely; it never compared goals against synchrony. C is wrong because the skeptics' concern was a confound (goals mixed with synchrony), not inaccurate measurement of cooperation. D goes too far: out-of-sync pairs simply bonded less, and nothing shows they came to distrust each other.
g.design: To pick A, students have to link the result to the skeptics' confound mentioned two sentences earlier. B and C each borrow real pieces of the passage (shared goals, flaws in earlier studies) but misread how they relate. D overstates what the comparison shows. All choices follow the same sentence frame.

c.seed: social science research — Linguistic Frames shaping policy preferences through disease outbreak mortality versus survival emphasis

g.passage: In a classic experiment, participants were asked to choose between two programs to combat a hypothetical disease outbreak expected to kill 600 people. When the outcomes were described in terms of lives saved, most participants preferred a program that would save 200 people with certainty over a riskier alternative. When the identical outcomes were described in terms of deaths, however, most preferred the riskier option. Many researchers concluded that wording alone can reverse people's preferences. __Later studies complicated this conclusion, finding that the reversal weakens considerably when participants are told explicitly what happens to the remaining people—for instance, that 200 will be saved and 400 will die.__ This suggests that part of the original effect may arise because people fill in unstated outcomes differently depending on how a choice is phrased, not simply because certain words carry emotional weight.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents findings that confirm the conclusion researchers drew from the classic experiment about how wording affects preferences.
It presents findings that qualify an earlier interpretation and set up an alternative account of why that effect occurs.
It presents findings that reveal a flaw in how participants in the classic experiment were chosen for the study.
It presents findings that show wording has no measurable influence on people's choices about risky programs.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 '단어 표현만으로 선호가 뒤집힌다'는 기존 결론을 복잡하게 만드는(제한하는) 후속 연구 결과를 제시하고, 다음 문장이 말하지 않은 결과를 사람들이 다르게 채워 넣는다는 대안적 설명을 내놓도록 이끈다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 이 결과가 기존 결론을 확인하는 것이 아니라 복잡하게 만들기 때문에 틀렸다. C는 참가자 선정 방식은 지문에서 전혀 언급되지 않으므로 틀렸다. D는 효과가 '상당히 약해진다'고 했을 뿐 완전히 사라진다고 하지 않았으므로 지나친 주장이다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence describes later studies that "complicated" the earlier conclusion that wording alone reverses preferences. That leads directly into the next sentence, which offers a different explanation: people fill in unstated outcomes differently. That makes B correct. A is wrong because the findings complicate the earlier conclusion instead of confirming it. C is wrong because the text never discusses how participants were selected. D goes too far, since the text says the reversal "weakens considerably," not that wording has no influence at all.
g.design: To answer, students have to link the word "complicated" in the underlined sentence with the alternative account in the sentence after it. D is a trap for readers who skim and miss "weakens," and A is a trap for readers who see the topic stay the same and assume the finding agrees.

c.seed: social science research — Linguist Derek Bickerton's Creole Genesis Hypothesis explaining pidgin language evolution into full grammar systems

g.passage: When adults who share no common language are brought together, as on many colonial-era plantations, they often improvise a pidgin: a contact language with a small vocabulary and little consistent grammar. Linguist Derek Bickerton argued that the leap from pidgin to creole—a fully developed language—happens in a single generation, when children exposed only to the pidgin acquire it as their first language. Studying Hawaii, he observed that the children of pidgin-speaking laborers spoke with systematic markers of tense and aspect that their parents never used. __Strikingly, these markers resembled those found in creoles that had arisen independently in places such as Haiti and Guyana, even though the children had no contact with speakers there.__ Bickerton concluded that the children were not copying the grammar they heard but filling its gaps by drawing on an innate "bioprogram" for language.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents a finding that challenges Bickerton's claim that creoles emerge within a single generation.
It explains how the pidgin spoken by the Hawaiian laborers came to include markers of tense and aspect.
It offers a parallel that helps rule out borrowing as the source of the children's grammar, supporting Bickerton's conclusion.
It describes a feature that distinguishes Hawaiian creole from the creoles that developed in Haiti and Guyana.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 하와이 아이들의 문법 표지가 접촉이 없던 아이티·가이아나의 크리올과 닮았다는 점을 제시해, 아이들이 남에게서 빌려온 것이 아니라 타고난 '바이오프로그램'에서 끌어냈다는 마지막 결론을 뒷받침한다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 이 문장이 Bickerton의 주장을 반박하는 것이 아니라 지지하므로 틀렸다. B는 표지가 부모의 피진에는 없었다고 했으므로 틀렸다. D는 문장이 차이가 아니라 유사성을 강조하므로 틀렸다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence points out that the Hawaiian children's grammatical markers resembled those of creoles in Haiti and Guyana, places they never had contact with. That similarity rules out copying and sets up Bickerton's conclusion that the children relied on an innate "bioprogram," so C is correct. A is wrong because the sentence supports Bickerton's claim rather than challenging it. B is wrong because the text says the parents' pidgin never had these markers. D is wrong because the sentence stresses similarity, not a difference.
g.design: 정답을 고르려면 밑줄 문장의 유사성 근거를 마지막 문장의 선천성 결론과 연결해야 한다. 오답 A·D는 비교라는 점을 짚되 그 방향을 반대로 읽었고, B는 지문 속 세부 정보를 잘못된 출처에 연결했다.

c.seed: social science research — Sociologist Erving Goffman's Dramaturgy Theory analyzing social interaction as theatrical performance and self-presentation

g.passage: In The Presentation of Self in Everyday Life (1956), sociologist Erving Goffman proposed that ordinary social encounters can be understood as performances staged for an audience. A waiter, for instance, adopts a polished, deferential manner in the dining room—what Goffman called the "front stage"—while joking loudly with coworkers in the kitchen, or "back stage." __Critics have objected that this framework reduces people to calculating actors who never sincerely mean what they display.__ Goffman, however, did not claim that performers are necessarily insincere; many people fully believe in the roles they play, and he argued that a self is not hidden behind such performances so much as produced through them.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It offers an example that illustrates the contrast between the front stage and the back stage described earlier.
It presents evidence that Goffman later used to revise his account of how waiters behave at work.
It states the main conclusion of Goffman's theory, which the rest of the text supports with an example.
It introduces an interpretation of Goffman's theory that the following sentence argues is mistaken.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 비평가들이 고프먼의 이론을 '사람을 진심 없는 계산적 배우로 만든다'고 해석한다는 내용이고, 바로 다음 문장이 "however"로 고프먼은 그런 주장을 하지 않았다고 반박하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 웨이터 예시가 앞 문장에 있어 그럴듯하지만, 밑줄 문장은 예시가 아니라 비판이다. B는 고프먼이 이론을 수정했다는 언급이 지문에 없다. C는 밑줄 문장을 이론의 결론으로 보지만, 그것은 비판자들의 견해이고 글은 오히려 이를 부정한다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence reports how critics interpret Goffman's theory: that it turns people into calculating, insincere actors. The next sentence begins with "however" and argues that Goffman made no such claim, so D is correct. A might seem plausible because the waiter example comes just before, but the underlined sentence is a criticism, not an example. B is wrong because the text never says Goffman revised anything. C treats the critics' view as Goffman's own conclusion, but the text actually rejects that view.
g.design: 독자는 두 단계를 거쳐야 한다. 밑줄 문장이 비평가의 해석이라는 점을 파악하고, 이어지는 'however' 문장이 그 해석을 반박한다는 점까지 연결해야 한다. A와 C는 바로 앞 예시나 이론 내용에 기대고 있어 대충 읽으면 고르기 쉽다.

c.seed: social science research — Psychologist Carol Dweck's Growth Mindset research on fixed versus malleable intelligence beliefs affecting achievement

g.passage: Psychologist Carol Dweck has argued that students' beliefs about intelligence shape how they respond to difficulty. Students who view intelligence as fixed tend to interpret a hard problem as evidence of their limits, whereas those who view it as malleable tend to treat the same problem as a chance to improve. In one well-known study, Dweck and colleagues followed students through the transition to junior high school, a period when coursework typically becomes more demanding. __The two groups had entered with similar math grades, yet over the next two years, the students who saw intelligence as malleable pulled steadily ahead.__ For Dweck, this divergence suggested that mindset matters most not when tasks are easy but when challenges mount, since only then do the contrasting beliefs lead students to react differently.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It reports a finding that the text then uses to support a claim about when beliefs about intelligence have their greatest effect.
It reports a finding that challenges the idea that students' beliefs about intelligence influence how they respond to difficulty.
It reports a finding that explains why coursework tends to become more demanding during the transition to junior high school.
It reports a finding that shows students who began with higher grades were more likely to view intelligence as malleable.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 비슷한 성적으로 출발한 두 집단이 2년간 벌어졌다는 연구 결과를 제시하고, 마지막 문장이 이 '격차'를 근거로 마인드셋이 도전이 커질 때 가장 중요하다는 주장을 끌어내므로 A가 정답이다. B는 결과가 Dweck의 주장을 반박한다고 하지만 실제로는 뒷받침한다. C는 지문에 언급된 '과제가 어려워짐'을 끌어왔지만 그 이유를 설명하는 문장이 아니다. D는 두 집단의 출발 성적이 비슷했다는 내용과 정반대다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence reports that two groups starting with similar math grades drifted apart over two years, and the final sentence uses that divergence to argue that mindset matters most when challenges mount, so A is correct. B is wrong because the finding supports, rather than challenges, Dweck's view. C borrows the detail that coursework gets harder, but the sentence does not explain why that happens. D contradicts the text, which says the groups began with similar grades.
g.design: 모든 선택지를 'It reports a finding that...' 틀로 통일해 표면 일치를 막고, 밑줄 문장과 마지막 문장의 연결을 파악해야 정답을 고를 수 있게 했다. 오답 B와 C는 지문 요소를 부분적으로 활용한다.

c.seed: social science research — Anthropologist Mary Douglas's Purity and Danger framework examining cultural taboos and symbolic classification systems

g.passage: In Purity and Danger (1966), anthropologist Mary Douglas challenged the long-standing view that food taboos, such as the prohibitions in the book of Leviticus, were early forms of hygiene meant to avoid disease. Douglas argued instead that such rules follow from systems of classification: a culture sorts the world into categories, and things that fail to fit cleanly into any category come to be treated as polluting. __Pigs, for example, have cloven hooves like the cattle and sheep that the ancient Israelites considered proper livestock, yet unlike those animals they do not chew cud.__ On Douglas's account, it is this mismatch with the category, rather than any danger to health, that made the pig unclean. Dirt, in her famous phrase, is simply "matter out of place."
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents evidence that the hygiene-based view used to explain why pigs were considered dangerous to eat.
It gives a case of something that only partly fits a recognized grouping, illustrating the principle Douglas proposed.
It gives a case of a category the ancient Israelites invented, showing that Douglas's principle applied only to livestock.
It gives a case of an exception to Douglas's principle, which the following sentence then works to explain away.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 돼지가 갈라진 발굽은 있지만 되새김질을 하지 않아 '적절한 가축' 범주에 깔끔히 들어맞지 않음을 보여주며, 바로 앞 문장에서 제시한 Douglas의 원리(범주에 맞지 않는 것이 오염된 것으로 여겨진다)의 예시 역할을 하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 돼지가 언급된다는 점은 맞지만, 이 문장은 Douglas가 반박한 위생설이 아니라 그녀의 분류 이론을 뒷받침한다. C는 가축 범주를 언급한 점은 맞지만, 원리가 가축에만 적용된다는 제한은 지문에 없다. D는 다음 문장이 밑줄 문장을 해석한다는 점은 맞지만, 돼지는 원리의 예외가 아니라 원리를 확인해 주는 사례이다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence shows that pigs share one trait of proper livestock (cloven hooves) but lack another (chewing cud), so they don't fit the category cleanly. That makes them an example of the principle Douglas stated in the sentence before, so B is correct. A is tempting because the sentence is about pigs, but it supports Douglas's classification theory, not the hygiene view she argued against. C correctly notes that the livestock category comes up, but nothing in the text says her principle applies only to livestock. D is right that the next sentence interprets the pig case, but the pig confirms Douglas's principle rather than being an exception to it.
g.design: 정답은 '예시'라는 핵심어를 직접 쓰지 않고 바꿔 표현했고, 오답 세 개도 모두 'It ... a case of ...'라는 같은 문장 틀로 썼다. 각 오답에는 돼지, 가축 범주, 다음 문장의 해석처럼 지문에 실제로 나오는 요소를 하나씩 넣어, 훑어 읽으면 맞는 것처럼 보이게 했다.

c.seed: social science research — Economist Richard Thaler's Mental Accounting study on how people categorize financial decisions irrationally

g.passage: Standard economic theory holds that money is fungible: a dollar won in a lottery should be spent exactly as carefully as a dollar earned from wages, since either can buy the same goods. Economist Richard Thaler argued that people do not actually treat money this way. Instead, he proposed, individuals sort their funds into separate mental "accounts"—rent money, vacation money, windfall money—and apply different spending rules to each. __In one scenario Thaler examined, people who had lost a $10 theater ticket were far less willing to buy a replacement than were people who had lost a $10 bill on the way to the theater, even though the financial loss was identical in both cases.__ Thaler reasoned that the lost ticket was charged to the "entertainment" account, making the show seem to cost $20, whereas the lost cash was absorbed by a general account that left the entertainment budget untouched.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents evidence that standard economic theory accurately predicts how people will respond to equivalent financial losses.
It introduces a finding that Thaler went on to reject after considering how people budget for entertainment.
It offers a case in which people's choices conflict with the assumption described at the beginning of the text.
It describes a scenario showing that people are generally unwilling to spend money on entertainment after any loss.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 손실 금액이 같은데도 사람들의 선택이 달라지는 사례를 제시하며, 이는 첫 문장의 '돈은 대체 가능하다'는 표준 이론의 가정과 충돌하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 이 사례가 표준 이론을 지지한다고 하여 정반대이다. B는 Thaler가 이 결과를 뒤이어 해석한 것이지 기각한 것이 아니므로 틀리다. D는 현금을 잃은 사람들은 대체로 기꺼이 구매했다는 점을 놓치고 '어떤 손실이든'으로 지나치게 일반화했다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence describes people making different choices even though they lost the same amount, which goes against the opening assumption that money is fungible. That makes C correct. A gets it backward, because the scenario undercuts standard theory instead of supporting it. B is wrong because Thaler explains the finding in the next sentence rather than rejecting it. D overgeneralizes: people who lost cash were still fairly willing to buy a ticket, so the reluctance did not follow every kind of loss.
g.design: Two steps are required: connect the scenario back to the opening fungibility assumption, then confirm it contradicts that assumption. Distractors A and D each reuse real details (equal losses, reduced willingness), and B misreads the follow-up sentence.
