g.explanation:
정답 B. 분사구 'Rejecting the idea of one general intelligence'의 의미상 주어는 어떤 생각을 거부하는 행위자, 즉 Gardner이므로 주절 주어도 Gardner여야 한다.
A: 'the book'은 Gardner의 저작물이다. 수식 대상과 관련은 있지만 범주가 다르다(사람이 아니라 책). 책이 생각을 '거부한다'고 하면 수식어가 사람 대신 책에 걸리게 된다.
C: 'IQ tests'는 거부하는 주체가 아니라 오히려 비판받는 대상이라 수식어와 연결되지 않는 엉뚱한 주어다.
D: 수동태로 바꾸면서 'several distinct cognitive domains'가 주어가 되었다. 복수 주어와 동사 were의 수일치는 맞지만, 인지 영역들이 하나의 일반 지능이라는 생각을 거부할 수는 없으므로 현수 수식어가 된다.
g.explanation_en:
B is correct. The opening phrase "Rejecting the idea of one general intelligence" needs a subject that can actually reject an idea. That person is Gardner, so he must be the subject of the main clause.
A is wrong because "the book" is Gardner's work, not Gardner himself. It's a related noun from a different category, so the phrase would describe the book instead of the person who did the rejecting.
C is wrong because "IQ tests" are what Gardner was arguing against. They aren't the ones doing the rejecting, so the phrase would attach to an unrelated subject.
D is wrong because the passive version makes "several distinct cognitive domains" the subject. The subject and verb agree ("domains were"), but domains can't reject an idea, so the opening phrase is left dangling.
g.design: 이 문항은 분사구로 시작한다. 오답은 저작물 주어(A), 무관한 주어(C), 수일치는 맞지만 의미상 불가능한 주어(D)로 구성했다. 네 선택지 모두 문법적으로는 완전한 절이 되므로, 수식어가 의미상 누구를 가리키는지 판단해야만 정답을 고를 수 있다.

c.instruction: 완전한 독립절 두 개가 이어지는 문장을 만들되, 두 절 사이의 논리적 관계(대조, 인과, 부연설명 중 하나)를 분명히 드러내라. 정답은 그 관계에 어울리는 구두점 전략(등위접속사+쉼표, 세미콜론, 또는 마침표) 하나이며, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 구두점 종류는 맞지만 절 관계와 안 맞는 접속사를 쓴 경우, (2) 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이은 콤마 스플라이스, (3) 절 경계가 아닌 곳에 세미콜론을 넣어 절을 어색하게 쪼갠 경우로 만들어라. 정답 선택 시 단순히 구두점 유무가 아니라 절 간 의미 관계까지 고려해야 정답을 고를 수 있도록 하라.
c.seed: social science research — Sociologist Arlie Hochschild's Emotional Contagion research demonstrating mood transfer in airline flight attendant interactions

g.passage: In her study of airline flight attendants, sociologist Arlie Hochschild observed that moods moved readily between workers and passengers. An attendant's practiced warmth, she found, could noticeably calm anxious passengers______ that same warmth, sustained hour after hour across long shifts, often left the attendants themselves feeling emotionally depleted.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , for
, but
but;
g.explanation:
정답 C: 빈칸 앞(승무원의 따뜻함이 승객을 진정시킴)과 뒤(그 따뜻함이 승무원 자신을 지치게 함)는 모두 독립절이며, 승객에게는 이롭지만 승무원에게는 해롭다는 대조 관계이다. 따라서 쉼표+대조 등위접속사 ', but'이 알맞다.
A: 쉼표+등위접속사 형식은 맞지만 'for'는 '왜냐하면'이라는 이유를 나타낸다. 승무원이 지친 것이 승객이 진정된 이유는 아니므로 논리 관계가 맞지 않는다.
B: 쉼표 하나만으로 두 독립절을 이었으므로 콤마 스플라이스이다.
D: 세미콜론이 접속사 'but' 뒤에 와서 'but'이 앞 절에 붙어 버린다. 그러면 앞 절이 'but'으로 어색하게 끝나므로 절 경계를 잘못 나눈 것이다.
g.explanation_en:
C is correct. The text before the blank ("An attendant's practiced warmth... could noticeably calm anxious passengers") is an independent clause, and so is the text after it ("that same warmth... often left the attendants themselves feeling emotionally depleted"). The two ideas contrast: the warmth helps passengers but drains the attendants. A comma plus the contrasting coordinating conjunction "but" joins the clauses correctly and signals that relationship.
A is wrong because a comma plus a coordinating conjunction is the right structure, but "for" means "because." The attendants' exhaustion doesn't explain why the passengers calmed down, so the logic doesn't work.
B is wrong because it joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice.
D is wrong because putting the semicolon after "but" attaches the conjunction to the first clause, which then ends awkwardly on "but." The semicolon doesn't fall at the real boundary between the clauses.
g.design: 빈칸 양쪽에 독립절을 두고 둘 사이를 대조 관계로 만들었다. 오답은 (1) 형식은 맞지만 인과를 나타내는 접속사 for를 쓴 경우, (2) 콤마 스플라이스, (3) but 뒤에 세미콜론을 잘못 둔 경우로 구성했다. 그래서 구두점 형식만이 아니라 두 절의 의미 관계까지 따져야 정답을 고를 수 있다.

c.instruction: 짧은 부사적 삽입어구(however, for example, in fact 등)가 문장 중간에 등장하되, 이것이 두 독립절 사이에 낀 것인지 아니면 한 절 내부의 단순 삽입인지 헷갈리게 설계하라. 정답은 실제 절 구조(삽입어 앞뒤가 독립절인지 아닌지)에 맞는 구두점이며, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 삽입어를 절 경계로 착각해 불필요하게 세미콜론/마침표를 쓴 경우, (2) 실제 절 경계인데 쉼표만 찍어 콤마 스플라이스를 만든 경우, (3) 삽입어 앞뒤 쉼표를 하나만 찍어 비대칭으로 만든 경우로 구성하라. 문장을 읽고 삽입어 앞뒤가 각각 완전한 절인지 아닌지를 판별해야만 정답을 고를 수 있게 하라.
c.seed: social science research — Linguist Gillian Brown's Information Structure analysis explaining how speakers organize given versus new information sequencing

g.passage: Linguist Gillian Brown's research on information structure suggests that speakers tend to place familiar, or "given," information early in a sentence and save unfamiliar, or "new," information for the end. According to Brown, this ordering is not merely a stylistic habit ______ listeners who encounter new information before given information often take noticeably longer to connect it to what they already know.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: habit, in fact. Listeners
habit, in fact, listeners
habit; in fact listeners
habit; in fact, listeners
g.explanation:
빈칸 앞 "this ordering is not merely a stylistic habit"과 뒤 "listeners ... take noticeably longer ..."는 둘 다 독립절이다. 'in fact'는 두 번째 절을 이끄는 부사적 연결어이므로, 절 경계(세미콜론)는 in fact 앞에 오고 in fact 뒤에는 쉼표를 찍는다. 그래서 D가 정답이다. (참고: 선택지에서는 빈칸 앞 단어 habit이 반복되어 있지만, 비교 기준은 구두점이다.)
A: 절 경계를 in fact 뒤에 둔 경우다. 그러면 in fact가 앞 절 끝에 붙어 버려 뒤 절의 근거를 제시하는 연결 기능을 잃는다. 삽입어 자리를 절 경계로 착각한 오류다.
B: 독립절 두 개를 쉼표로만 이은 콤마 스플라이스다. in fact를 단순 삽입어로 보고 양쪽에 쉼표를 찍었지만, 실제로는 절 경계가 있다.
C: 세미콜론의 위치는 맞지만 in fact 뒤의 쉼표가 빠졌다. 문장 머리의 연결어를 뒤 내용과 분리하지 않은 비대칭 구두점이다.
g.explanation_en:
Look at what comes before and after the blank. "This ordering is not merely a stylistic habit" is a complete independent clause, and so is "listeners ... take noticeably longer to connect it to what they already know." Between two independent clauses you need a strong boundary. "In fact" belongs to the second clause because it introduces the supporting evidence. So the semicolon goes before "in fact," and a comma follows it. That makes D correct.
A puts the boundary after "in fact." This attaches "in fact" to the end of the first sentence, where it no longer introduces the evidence. The writer has mistaken the transition's position for the clause break.
B joins two independent clauses with only commas, which creates a comma splice. It treats "in fact" as a simple interrupter inside one clause, but there is a real clause boundary here.
C places the semicolon correctly but leaves out the comma after the introductory "in fact," so the transition isn't set off from the rest of its clause.
g.design: "in fact" looks like an interrupter inside one sentence, but it actually sits at the boundary between two independent clauses. Each wrong answer matches one assigned error type: A puts the clause break after the insert, B is a comma splice, and C has the comma on only one side.

c.instruction: 학술적 소재(연구, 인물, 현상 등)에 대한 3~4문장의 짧은 지문을 만들고, 마지막 문장은 앞 내용 중 특정 목적이나 강조점(예: 결과가 아니라 의도, 수치가 아니라 방향성)에 부합하는 전환어를 골라야 정답이 되게 하라. 오답 3개는 (1)앞 문장의 결과·부수적 사실과는 맞지만 지문의 핵심 강조점과는 어긋나는 전환어, (2)방향은 맞지만 논리관계(원인/대조 등)가 틀린 전환어, (3)전혀 다른 내용과 연결되는 전환어로 구성하라. 지문에 여러 개의 정보가 나열되되 그중 한 가지만 답과 직결되도록 설계한다.
c.seed: social science research — Anthropologist Fredrik Barth's Ethnic Boundaries study showing how groups maintain identity through symbolic markers

g.passage: In his 1969 introduction to Ethnic Groups and Boundaries, anthropologist Fredrik Barth challenged the assumption that ethnic groups survive because they remain isolated and culturally distinct. Studying Pathan communities along the Pakistan-Afghanistan frontier, he observed that people often crossed ethnic lines, traded with neighbors, and even adopted outsiders' customs, yet the groups themselves endured. What persisted, Barth argued, was not a complete inventory of cultural traits but a small set of markers, such as particular styles of dress or codes of hospitality, that members chose to display as signs of belonging. ______ a group could alter much of its culture over generations and still remain recognizably itself, provided those boundary-defining signals were maintained.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: By this logic,
Even so,
Likewise,
Before then,
g.explanation:
정답 A. 마지막 문장은 바로 앞 문장의 핵심 주장(정체성은 문화 전체가 아니라 소수의 상징적 표지가 유지한다)에서 끌어낸 함의다. 표지만 유지되면 문화 대부분이 바뀌어도 집단이 존속한다는 결론이므로 추론을 나타내는 'By this logic,'이 알맞다.
B 'Even so,'는 둘째 문장의 '경계를 넘나들었지만 집단은 존속했다'는 양보 구조와 비슷해 보여 끌리지만, 마지막 문장은 앞 주장과 맞서는 내용이 아니라 그 주장을 그대로 적용한 결과다. 따라서 양보·대조 관계는 맞지 않는다.
C 'Likewise,'는 마지막 문장이 앞 주장과 같은 방향이라는 점은 맞게 짚지만, 별개의 비슷한 사례를 덧붙이는 표현이다. 마지막 문장은 새로운 사례가 아니라 앞 주장에서 나온 귀결이므로 논리관계가 틀렸다.
D 'Before then,'은 시간 순서를 나타낸다. 지문에는 이런 연대기적 흐름이 없으므로 내용과 연결되지 않는다.
g.explanation_en:
The answer is A. The last sentence draws a conclusion from Barth's main claim in the sentence just before it: identity rests on a few markers that members display, not on a group's full set of cultural traits. If that's true, a group can change most of its culture and still survive as long as it keeps those markers. "By this logic," signals exactly this kind of inference.
B ("Even so,") is tempting because the second sentence already has a "despite this, they endured" pattern. But the final sentence doesn't push back against the claim before it. It applies that claim, so a contrast or concession transition doesn't fit.
C ("Likewise,") gets the direction right, since the final sentence agrees with Barth's claim. However, "Likewise" adds a separate, similar example. The final sentence isn't a new parallel case. It's a consequence of the claim, so the logical relationship is wrong.
D ("Before then,") signals a time sequence. The passage has no chronology for this to connect to.
g.design: Several facts are listed (crossing ethnic lines, trade, borrowing customs, persistent markers), but only the claim that markers sustain identity supports the final sentence as an inference. Each distractor has a different flaw: B fits a side detail (a group enduring despite crossing lines), C has the right direction but the wrong logical relationship (adding an example instead of drawing a conclusion), and D connects to content that isn't there (a time sequence).

c.instruction: 서로 배치되거나 상반된 것처럼 보이는 두 가지 관찰(실험 결과, 사례, 수치)이 제시된 짧은 지문을 만들고, 두 관찰을 종합했을 때 나오는 결론을 마지막 문장에서 올바른 전환어로 연결해야 정답이 되게 하라. 오답 3개는 (1)한쪽 관찰만 반영한 전환어, (2)두 관찰이 상반된다는 점만 보고 단순 대조로 처리한 전환어, (3)종합 결론과 무관한 전환어로 구성하라. 계산이나 복잡한 수치 없이 정성적 진술만으로 구성한다.
c.seed: social science research — Psychologist Elizabeth Loftus's False Memory research documenting implantation of entirely fabricated childhood experiences

g.passage: In a well-known study by psychologist Elizabeth Loftus, participants read short accounts of childhood events supplied by their relatives. One account, describing being lost in a shopping mall as a child, was entirely made up. After repeated interviews, a substantial minority of participants not only accepted the invented episode but also added vivid details of their own. Most participants, however, consistently said they had no memory of the event, even when told that a family member remembered it clearly. ______ false childhood memories seem to be possible to create but far from inevitable, with susceptibility varying considerably from person to person.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Nevertheless,
Taken together,
By contrast,
Meanwhile,
g.explanation:
정답 B: 지문에는 상반되어 보이는 관찰 두 가지가 나온다. (1) 상당수의 소수 참가자가 지어낸 기억을 받아들였고, (2) 대다수는 끝까지 거부했다. 마지막 문장의 '가능하지만 필연적이지는 않다'는 이 두 관찰을 함께 고려해야만 나오는 결론이므로, 종합을 나타내는 'Taken together,'가 알맞다.
A(Nevertheless,): 바로 앞 문장(대다수가 거부함)과 반대되는 내용이 이어질 때 쓰는 말이다. 따라서 첫 번째 관찰(기억 이식 가능)만 반영하는 셈이다. 그런데 마지막 문장은 앞 문장의 '거부'도 포함하므로 맞지 않는다.
C(By contrast,): 두 관찰이 서로 어긋난다는 점만 보고 단순 대조로 처리한 것이다. 마지막 문장은 앞 내용과 대비되는 새 사실이 아니라 두 관찰을 아우르는 결론이다.
D(Meanwhile,): 동시에 일어나는 별개의 사건이나 화제 전환을 나타내므로, 결론 도출과 관계가 없다.
g.explanation_en:
Correct answer, B: The passage gives two observations that seem to conflict. First, a substantial minority of participants accepted and added details to an invented memory. Second, most participants consistently rejected it. The last sentence says false memories are "possible to create but far from inevitable." You can only reach that conclusion by considering both observations at once, so "Taken together," is the right transition.
A ("Nevertheless,") would mean the last sentence goes against the sentence right before it, the one about most people resisting. That reflects only the first observation, but the conclusion actually builds on the resistance too.
C ("By contrast,") treats the two findings as a simple contrast. The last sentence doesn't set up a new opposing fact; it combines both findings into one conclusion.
D ("Meanwhile,") signals something happening at the same time or a change of topic, so it doesn't introduce a conclusion.
g.design: I paired two qualitative findings from Loftus's study that seem to conflict: some participants accepted the fabricated memory, but most rejected it. The last sentence states a conclusion that combines both. Each wrong answer matches one assigned type: A reflects only one finding, C treats the findings as a simple contrast, and D is unrelated to the conclusion.

c.instruction: 한 문장 안에서 수식어구나 비교 표현이 인접한 명사가 아니라 문장 앞부분의 다른 요소(주어나 앞 문장의 대상)를 가리키도록 설계된 짧은 지문을 만들고, 이 실제 지시 관계를 올바르게 파악해야 정답 전환어를 고를 수 있게 하라. 오답 3개는 (1)인접한 명사를 지시 대상으로 잘못 본 전환어, (2)문법적으로는 자연스럽지만 실제 지시관계와 어긋나는 전환어, (3)전혀 다른 요소를 지시 대상으로 삼은 전환어로 구성하라. 문장은 짧고 단순한 구조를 유지한다.
c.seed: social science research — Sociologist James Coleman's Rational Choice theory applying economic logic to educational tracking and peer influence

g.passage: Many sociologists of the 1960s explained students' academic choices mainly through cultural norms. James Coleman instead applied economic logic, treating students as rational actors who weigh costs against benefits. On his account, a student in a low academic track who stops studying is not rejecting the values of school. ______ that student, much like an investor avoiding a stock with poor returns, is turning down an effort whose payoff seems small among peers who reward other pursuits.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Likewise,
In other words,
Rather,
By contrast,
g.explanation:
정답 C(Rather). 빈칸 앞 문장은 '낮은 트랙 학생이 공부를 그만두는 것은 학교 가치를 거부하는 것이 아니다'라는 부정 진술이다. 빈칸 뒤 문장의 주어 'that student'는 바로 그 학생을 가리키고, 삽입구 'much like an investor...'도 바로 옆 명사 peers가 아니라 이 주어(학생)를 수식한다. 즉 뒤 문장은 같은 학생의 행동에 대해, 앞에서 부정한 해석(가치 거부) 대신 올바른 해석(합리적 투자 판단)을 내놓는다. '~가 아니라 오히려 ~'의 교정 관계이므로 Rather가 알맞다.
A(Likewise): 'like an investor'의 비교를 앞 문장의 '학교 가치'나 근처 명사와의 유사성으로 잘못 읽은 선택지다. 뒤 문장은 앞 문장과 비슷한 내용을 덧붙이는 것이 아니라 앞의 해석을 대체한다.
B(In other words): 문법적으로는 자연스럽지만, 뒤 문장은 '거부가 아니다'를 바꿔 말한 것이 아니다. 앞에서 부정한 해석을 대신할 새 설명을 내놓는 것이다.
D(By contrast): 1960년대 사회학자들과 Coleman의 대비를 기준으로 삼은 선택지다. 그 대비는 이미 둘째 문장에서 끝났다. 빈칸 앞뒤는 서로 다른 두 대상이 아니라 같은 학생에 대한 두 해석이므로 대조가 아니라 교정 관계다.
g.explanation_en:
The answer is C, "Rather." The sentence before the blank makes a negative claim: a low-track student who stops studying is *not* rejecting school values. After the blank, the subject "that student" refers to that same student. The phrase "much like an investor..." also describes this student, not the nearby noun "peers." So the final sentence gives the correct reading of the same student's behavior (a rational choice about investment) in place of the reading that was just denied. That "not X, but instead Y" correction is what "Rather" signals.
A ("Likewise") treats the "like an investor" comparison as if it showed a similarity to the previous sentence or a nearby noun. But the last sentence replaces the earlier interpretation. It doesn't add a similar point.
B ("In other words") sounds fine grammatically, but the last sentence doesn't restate "not rejecting school values." It offers a new explanation in place of the one that was denied.
D ("By contrast") takes the 1960s sociologists versus Coleman as the reference point, but that contrast was already made in the second sentence. The sentences around the blank give two readings of the same student, so they show a correction, not a contrast between two different things.
g.design: 삽입 비교구 'much like an investor'는 인접 명사 peers가 아니라 주어 that student를 수식한다. 그리고 그 학생은 앞 문장에서 부정된 해석의 대상이다. 이 지시 관계를 파악해야 교정의 전환어 Rather를 고를 수 있다. 오답은 인접 요소 오지시(Likewise), 문법상 자연스럽지만 관계가 틀린 것(In other words), 다른 요소인 1960년대 사회학자를 기준으로 삼은 것(By contrast)이다.

c.instruction: 그래프나 표에 두 개 이상의 변수(또는 텍스트 설명과 그래프 수치)가 함께 제시된 자료를 주고, 두 요소를 동시에 봐야만 결론을 낼 수 있는 질문을 만들어라. 정답은 두 변수를 모두 반영해야 하고, 오답 3개는 각각 '한쪽 변수만 본 결론', '다른 쪽 변수만 본 결론', '자료에 없는 제3의 변수로 결론'을 만든 것으로 구성하라.
c.seed: social science research — Linguist Sherry Turkle's Identity in Cyberspace study examining multiple self-presentations in online gaming communities

g.passage: In her research on online communities, Sherry Turkle described multiuser games as possible "identity workshops," spaces where people try out versions of themselves that differ from who they are offline. A research team building on her work surveyed players who keep more than one character, or persona, in online role-playing games. For each player, the team recorded two things: how many personas the player kept and how much those personas differed from the player's offline personality. The team proposes that playing many personas does not by itself lead to self-insight. Instead, the team argues, players gain self-insight when they keep several personas that each differ sharply from their offline selves.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the research team's proposal?
options: Players who kept five or more personas reported much more self-insight than players who kept only two personas, whether or not their personas resembled their offline personalities.
Players whose personas differed sharply from their offline personalities reported more self-insight than other players, and these players also tended to keep more personas than other players did.
Players who spent more than twenty hours a week in the games reported more self-insight than players who spent less time playing, regardless of how many personas they kept.

Among players who kept the same number of personas, those whose personas differed sharply from their offline selves reported the most self-insight, while players who kept many personas resembling their offline selves reported no more insight than players who kept few.
g.explanation:
정답 D: 연구팀의 주장에는 두 부분이 있다. (1) 페르소나의 개수만으로는 자기 통찰이 생기지 않는다. (2) 통찰을 낳는 것은 오프라인 성격과 크게 다른 페르소나를 여러 개 갖는 것이다. D는 페르소나 개수를 같게 맞춘 상태에서 차이 정도가 클수록 통찰이 크다는 것을 보여 주고, 오프라인 자아와 비슷한 페르소나는 개수가 많아도 효과가 없다는 것도 보여 준다. 두 변수를 함께 다루므로 주장의 두 부분을 모두 뒷받침한다.
A(한쪽 변수만 봄: 개수): 차이 정도와 상관없이 개수만으로 통찰이 늘어났다는 결과다. '개수만으로는 부족하다'는 주장과 정면으로 어긋난다.
B(다른 쪽 변수만 봄: 차이 정도): 차이가 큰 플레이어의 통찰이 컸다는 점은 주장과 맞아 보인다. 하지만 이 플레이어들은 페르소나 개수도 더 많았다. 그래서 통찰의 원인이 차이 정도인지 개수인지 가려낼 수 없다.
C(자료에 없는 제3의 변수): 연구팀이 기록하지 않은 플레이 시간으로 통찰을 설명한다. 연구팀의 주장과는 관계가 없다.
g.explanation_en:
Correct answer, D: The team's proposal has two parts. (1) The number of personas alone does not lead to self-insight. (2) Self-insight comes from keeping several personas that each differ sharply from the offline self. D compares players who kept the same number of personas and shows that the ones with more divergent personas reported more insight. It also shows that keeping many personas that resemble the offline self brings no extra insight. Because D looks at both variables together, it supports both parts of the proposal.
A looks only at the number of personas. It says insight rose with the number of personas whether or not they differed from the offline self. That contradicts the team's claim that numbers alone aren't enough.
B looks only at how much the personas differed. It seems to fit the proposal, but the players with divergent personas also kept more personas. So you can't tell whether their insight came from the divergence or from the number.
C uses a third variable, playing time, which the team never recorded. It tells you nothing about the team's proposal.
g.design: I used two variables: the number of personas and how much they differ from the offline self. Only D separates the two by holding the number of personas constant. The wrong answers are built from the number alone (A), divergence confounded with number (B), and an outside variable, playing time (C).

c.instruction: 지문에 상관관계나 동시 발생 사실만 제시하고, 이를 근거로 특정 가설(주장)의 인과성을 지지하는지 판단해야 하는 문항을 만들어라. 정답은 인과 방향과 대안 설명 가능성을 함께 고려해 타당하게 지지하는 것이어야 하고, 오답 3개는 각각 '상관을 그대로 인과로 오해', '인과 방향을 반대로 설정', '무관한 제3의 원인을 인과로 제시'로 구성하라.
c.seed: social science research — Anthropologist Catherine Lutz's Micronesian Emotions study challenging universality of emotion categories across Pacific cultures

g.passage: In the late 1970s, anthropologist Catherine Lutz lived on Ifaluk, a small atoll in Micronesia. She found that its residents sorted feelings into categories that do not line up neatly with the English words often treated as universal. For example, Ifaluk speakers use the word song for a kind of justified, morally charged anger. It is directed at someone who has broken a community rule, especially a rule about sharing food and labor. Lutz noticed that this emotion word is used most often in the same settings where duties to share are strongest. From this, she argued that a community's social arrangements actively shape which emotion categories its members recognize and use, rather than people everywhere starting from a fixed set of basic emotions.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Lutz's argument?
options: After a wage-labor program released some Ifaluk families, but not their neighbors on the same atoll, from traditional food-sharing duties, those families gradually used song less often than their neighbors did.
Several other Pacific atolls where duties to share food are strong also have a word for a justified, rule-enforcing anger similar to song.
Ifaluk children who learned to use song at an unusually early age grew up to be especially strict about following food-sharing rules as adults.
On Pacific islands where frequent typhoons make food scarce, both strict sharing duties and words like song are common, while both are rare on islands with plentiful food.
g.explanation: Lutz는 사회 구조(나눔 의무)가 원인이 되어 감정 범주(song)를 만든다고 주장한다. A는 같은 섬, 같은 환경에 사는 이웃 가구 중 일부에게서만 나눔 의무가 사라진 뒤에 song 사용이 줄었다는 발견이다. 원인이 결과보다 먼저 변했으므로 인과 방향이 맞고, 환경이 같으므로 제3의 요인도 통제된다. 따라서 주장을 가장 직접적으로 지지한다. B는 다른 섬에서도 같은 동시 발생이 나타난다는 것일 뿐이라 상관을 인과로 받아들이는 오류다. C는 감정어 학습이 나눔 행동을 낳는다는 뜻이어서 인과 방향이 거꾸로다. D는 식량 부족이라는 제3의 원인이 나눔 의무와 song을 함께 만들어 낸다는 설명이므로, 사회 구조가 감정 범주를 형성한다는 주장을 지지하지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: Lutz claims that social arrangements (sharing duties) cause emotion categories like song. Choice A describes a change that happened only to some families, while their neighbors on the same atoll kept the old duties. Song use dropped afterward, and only in the families whose duties changed. Because the cause comes before the effect, the direction is right. Because the environment is the same for both groups, a third factor is ruled out. That makes A the most direct support. Choice B just repeats the same co-occurrence on other islands, so it treats correlation as causation. Choice C runs the causation backward: learning the emotion word leads to stricter sharing. Choice D points to a third cause, food scarcity, that could produce both strict sharing and words like song. That offers an alternative explanation instead of supporting Lutz's claim.
g.design: 지문에는 나눔 의무와 감정어가 함께 나타난다는 사실만 제시했다. 정답은 시간 순서와 대조군(같은 섬의 이웃)을 갖춰 인과 방향과 제3 요인을 함께 통제한다. 오답은 각각 상관을 인과로 착각하는 경우(B), 인과 방향을 뒤집은 경우(C), 제3의 원인을 끌어들인 경우(D)로 구성했다.

c.instruction: 지문에 가설(주장)만 제시하고, 그 가설을 뒷받침하려면 어떤 추가 증거나 결과가 있어야 하는지 묻는 문항을 만들어라. 정답은 지문에 없는 가상의 결과이지만 가설의 논리 구조와 정확히 들어맞아야 하고, 오답 3개는 각각 '가설과 무관한 사실', '가설을 반박하는 결과', '이미 지문에 있는 사실을 재진술한 것'으로 구성하라.
c.seed: social science research — Psychologist Barry Schwartz's Paradox of Choice research linking abundant options to reduced decision satisfaction

g.passage: Psychologist Barry Schwartz has argued that an abundance of options can leave people less satisfied with the choices they make. According to Schwartz, the problem is not simply that more options take longer to sort through. Rather, when many alternatives are available, people more easily imagine that one of the options they passed over would have been better, and this sense of forgone possibilities lowers how much they enjoy whatever they end up choosing. Schwartz notes that, in surveys, shoppers often say they prefer stores with wide selections.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Schwartz's explanation of why abundant options reduce decision satisfaction?
options: Participants who chose a chocolate from a display of 30 varieties took longer to decide than participants who chose from a display of 6 varieties, and both groups rated their chocolate as equally enjoyable.

Participants who chose a chocolate from 30 varieties rated it less enjoyable than those who chose from 6, but this difference disappeared when the unchosen varieties were removed from view before tasting, so that participants could no longer compare their pick with the alternatives.
Participants who chose a chocolate from 30 varieties reported spending more total money on chocolate in the following month than participants who chose from 6 varieties.
When asked before choosing, most participants said they would rather pick a chocolate from a display of 30 varieties than from a display of 6 varieties.
g.explanation:
정답 B: Schwartz의 주장은 선택지가 많으면 만족도가 떨어지고, 그 원인이 선택 시간이 아니라 '포기한 대안과의 비교(놓친 가능성에 대한 생각)'라는 것이다. B는 만족도 저하를 보여 줄 뿐 아니라, 대안을 눈앞에서 치워 비교를 막으면 그 저하가 사라진다는 결과를 제시한다. 따라서 가설이 말하는 원인 메커니즘을 직접 확인해 준다.
A(가설을 반박하는 결과): 결정 시간은 더 길었지만 만족도에는 차이가 없었다. 이는 선택지가 많으면 만족도가 낮아진다는 핵심 주장과 정면으로 어긋난다.
C(가설과 무관한 사실): 이후 지출액은 결정 만족도나 포기한 대안과의 비교와 아무 관련이 없다.
D(지문 재진술): 사람들이 다양한 선택지를 선호한다는 내용은 지문의 설문 결과를 다시 말한 것일 뿐이다. 만족도가 어떻게 되는지나 그 원인에 대해서는 아무것도 보여 주지 않는다.
g.explanation_en:
Correct answer, B: Schwartz claims that having many options lowers satisfaction. He also says the cause is not the extra time spent deciding but people comparing their choice with the alternatives they gave up. B shows lower enjoyment with 30 varieties. It also shows that this drop disappears when the unchosen options are taken out of view, so participants can't compare. That result directly supports the cause Schwartz proposes.
A (contradicts the hypothesis): Choosing took longer, but enjoyment was the same in both groups. This goes against the central claim that more options reduce satisfaction.
C (irrelevant): How much people spent later has nothing to do with how satisfied they were with their choice or with comparing it to forgone options.
D (restates the passage): Saying people prefer large selections just repeats the survey finding already in the passage. It tells us nothing about satisfaction or what causes it.
g.design: 가설의 원인 메커니즘(포기한 대안과의 비교)을 따로 떼어 검증하는 가상 결과를 정답으로 했다. 오답은 각각 반박(만족도 차이 없음), 무관(지출액), 지문 재진술(선택지가 많은 쪽을 선호)로 만들었고, 모두 같은 초콜릿 실험 틀로 썼다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: social science research — Educationist Deborah Meier's Essential Schools movement emphasizing deep understanding over standardized test performance metrics

g.passage:
Text 1
Educator Deborah Meier, a leader in the Coalition of Essential Schools movement, argued that schools such as Central Park East in New York should judge students by portfolios and oral defenses rather than by standardized test scores. Supporters often cite the schools' high graduation and college-entry rates as proof that this approach produces deeper understanding than test-driven instruction does.

Text 2
Comparisons between Essential Schools and conventional schools are harder to interpret than they first appear. Families who sought out schools like Central Park East were often unusually invested in education, and such families tend to produce strong outcomes wherever their children enroll. Until researchers account for how students came to attend these schools, the schools' impressive graduation figures cannot by themselves reveal what the teaching methods accomplished.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the supporters' claim described in Text 1?
options: By arguing that portfolios and oral defenses measure student learning less accurately than standardized tests do
By asserting that the graduation and college-entry rates reported for Essential Schools were likely exaggerated
By cautioning that the cited outcomes may reflect who enrolled in the schools rather than how the schools taught
By suggesting that Essential Schools succeeded mainly because their families pressured teachers to focus on tests
g.explanation: Text 1의 지지자들은 높은 졸업률·대학 진학률을 교수법 효과의 증거로 본다. Text 2는 교육에 열성적인 가정이 이 학교를 선택했을 수 있으므로, 학생 선발 경로를 고려하기 전에는 그 수치가 교수법의 효과를 보여 주지 못한다고 말한다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 평가 방식 자체를 비판하지만 Text 2는 이를 다루지 않는다. B는 수치가 과장되었다고 하지만 Text 2는 수치를 인정하되 해석에만 의문을 제기한다. D는 가정이 언급된다는 점은 맞지만, 시험 위주 수업을 하라는 압력에 대한 언급은 없다.
g.explanation_en: In Text 1, supporters treat high graduation and college-entry rates as proof that the teaching approach works. Text 2 points out that unusually invested families chose these schools, so until enrollment is accounted for, the figures can't show what the teaching itself achieved. That makes C correct. A criticizes portfolios as an assessment tool, but Text 2 never evaluates assessment methods. B claims the numbers were exaggerated, but Text 2 accepts the figures and only questions how they're interpreted. D does draw on Text 2's mention of families, but Text 2 never says families pushed teachers to focus on tests.
g.design: To get this right, students have to connect the supporters' evidence in Text 1 with Text 2's point about who chose to enroll, which is a selection-effect problem. B and D both borrow details from Text 2 (the figures and the families) but twist them, so a quick skim can mislead.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: social science research — Sociologist Erving Goffman's Stigma theory analyzing social discrediting of individuals with visible or invisible marks

g.passage:
Text 1
In his 1963 book Stigma, sociologist Erving Goffman distinguished between the "discredited," whose stigmatizing attribute is readily visible to others, and the "discreditable," whose attribute can be concealed. Goffman argued that the discreditable face a distinctive burden: rather than managing others' reactions, they must constantly manage information, deciding whom to tell, when, and how. Some researchers have taken this to mean that concealment, though stressful, at least shields people from the open hostility the visibly stigmatized endure.

Text 2
Psychologist Diane Quinn's studies of people with concealable stigmatized identities, such as a history of mental illness, complicate that conclusion. Participants who concealed their identities reported less overt mistreatment, yet they also reported anticipating rejection more often, and that anticipation was closely tied to heightened anxiety and lower well-being. In Quinn's data, the vigilance required to keep a secret appeared to carry psychological costs comparable to, and sometimes exceeding, those linked to experienced discrimination.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would Quinn (Text 2) most likely respond to the interpretation that "some researchers" draw from Goffman's work in Text 1?
options: She would argue that the interpretation is mistaken because people who conceal a stigmatized attribute actually experience more overt hostility than those whose attributes are visible.
She would argue that the interpretation is sound because her participants confirmed that concealment removes the burden of deciding whom to tell about a stigmatized attribute.
She would argue that the interpretation is irrelevant because Goffman's distinction between visible and concealable attributes does not apply to histories of mental illness.
She would argue that the interpretation is incomplete because reduced exposure to open mistreatment may be offset by the strain of expecting it.
g.design: Two-step: identify the researchers' claim in Text 1 (concealment shields from hostility), then connect it to Quinn's mixed finding (less overt mistreatment but costly anticipation). Distractors A and B each borrow part of the texts.
g.explanation: Text 1에서 일부 연구자들은 숨기는 것이 스트레스는 있어도 공개적인 적대는 막아 준다고 해석한다. Quinn은 숨긴 사람들이 노골적 차별은 덜 겪었다고 인정하지만, 거절을 예상하는 데서 오는 불안 비용이 그만큼 크거나 더 크다고 보고하므로, 그 해석이 불완전하다고 볼 것이다. 따라서 정답은 D이다. A는 Quinn이 노골적 차별이 오히려 더 적었다고 보고했다는 점과 모순된다. B는 정보 관리의 부담이 사라진다고 하지만, Text 2는 비밀 유지에 경계가 필요하다고 강조한다. C는 Text 2가 정신질환 이력을 숨길 수 있는 정체성의 예로 직접 다루므로 틀렸다.
g.explanation_en: In Text 1, some researchers conclude that concealment, though stressful, at least protects people from open hostility. Quinn agrees that people who concealed faced less overt mistreatment, but she found that anticipating rejection carried costs as large as, or larger than, experienced discrimination. So she would see that interpretation as incomplete, which makes D the answer. A contradicts her finding that people who concealed reported less overt mistreatment, not more. B says concealment removes the burden of managing information, but Text 2 stresses the vigilance that keeping a secret requires. C is wrong because Text 2 uses a history of mental illness as an example of a concealable identity, so Goffman's distinction clearly applies to it.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: social science research — Linguist Anna Wierzbicka's Semantic Primes hypothesis proposing universal meaning units underlying all human languages

g.passage: Linguist Anna Wierzbicka has proposed that every human language contains a small set of "semantic primes"—basic meanings such as GOOD, KNOW, and BEFORE that cannot be defined using simpler words and that, she argues, appear as words or word parts in all languages. A central prediction of the hypothesis is that complex, culture-specific concepts in any language can be fully explained using only these primes. Critics have pointed to languages in which a supposed prime appears to be missing; for instance, some researchers claimed that a particular language had no single word for WANT. Wierzbicka's colleagues responded that, in that language, the meaning WANT is expressed reliably by a verb suffix rather than a separate word. If this response is accurate, it suggests that ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the critics' evidence does not undermine the hypothesis, since the hypothesis requires only that each prime be expressed in some form, not as a standalone word.
the critics' evidence does not undermine the hypothesis, since the meaning WANT can be defined using simpler meanings in that language.
the critics' evidence seriously undermines the hypothesis, since a meaning carried by a suffix cannot be used to explain culture-specific concepts.
the critics' evidence seriously undermines the hypothesis, since it shows that the number of primes varies from one language to another.
g.explanation: 지문은 프라임이 모든 언어에서 '단어 또는 단어의 일부'로 나타난다고 주장하며, 반론에 대한 답변은 WANT가 동사 접미사로 표현된다는 것이다. 이 두 정보를 연결하면 별도 단어가 없다는 비판은 가설을 반박하지 못하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 결론 방향은 맞지만, 프라임은 더 단순한 말로 정의될 수 없다는 지문 정의와 모순된다. C는 접미사가 개념 설명에 쓰일 수 없다는 근거 없는 전제를 둔다. D는 답변이 오히려 WANT의 존재를 보여 주므로 프라임 수가 다르다는 결론과 반대이다.
g.explanation_en: The passage says primes appear "as words or word parts" in all languages, and the response shows WANT is expressed by a verb suffix. Putting those together, the lack of a separate word doesn't count against the hypothesis, so A is correct. B reaches the right overall verdict but contradicts the definition of primes as meanings that cannot be defined with simpler words. C assumes without support that a meaning carried by a suffix can't help explain concepts. D gets it backward: the response shows WANT is present, not that the number of primes differs.
g.design: 정답을 고르려면 '단어 또는 단어의 일부'라는 정의를 접미사 답변과 연결해야 합니다(2단계 판단). B는 결론은 같지만 이유가 틀린 함정으로 설계했습니다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: social science research — Anthropologist Akhil Gupta's Globalization ethnography examining how international flows reshape local community identity formation

g.passage: Anthropologist Akhil Gupta's ethnographic work in a north Indian village examined how international forces—global development programs, agricultural science, and media—entered everyday life. Many scholars had assumed that such global flows simply erode local identities, replacing distinctive village traditions with a uniform, imported culture. Gupta found something different: farmers adopted high-yield seeds promoted by international agencies, yet they explained the seeds' performance using indigenous ideas about soil "heat" and bodily balance, and they defined themselves as a community partly by contrasting their practices with those of city officials and foreign experts. Because villagers were drawing on global resources to articulate what made them distinct, Gupta's findings suggest that ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: global flows had little effect on village life, since farmers continued to rely mainly on indigenous agricultural knowledge rather than imported techniques.
global flows can become materials through which local identities are actively reworked rather than simply erased.
global flows strengthened villagers' identities only after farmers rejected the seeds promoted by international agencies.
global flows produced a uniform culture in the village, even though farmers continued to use some traditional terms.
g.explanation: 지문은 농민들이 국제 기관의 종자를 받아들이면서도 토착 개념으로 해석하고, 외부인과의 대비로 공동체 정체성을 규정했다고 설명하므로, 세계적 흐름이 정체성을 지우지 않고 재구성하는 재료가 된다는 B가 정답이다. A는 토착 지식이 유지된 점은 맞지만 농민들이 실제로 종자를 채택했으므로 '영향이 거의 없다'는 결론과 모순된다. C는 정체성 강화라는 점은 일부 맞으나 농민들이 종자를 거부했다는 내용은 지문과 반대이다. D는 학자들의 기존 가정(균일화)을 그대로 따른 것으로, Gupta가 반박한 견해이다.
g.explanation_en: The passage says farmers adopted internationally promoted seeds but interpreted them through indigenous ideas and defined their community by contrast with outsiders, so global resources were used to reshape local identity—choice B. Choice A rightly notes that indigenous ideas persisted, but the farmers did adopt the new seeds, so global flows clearly affected village life. Choice C mentions stronger identity, which is partly supported, but the passage says farmers adopted the seeds, not rejected them. Choice D restates the scholars' earlier assumption of uniformity, which is exactly the view Gupta's findings challenge.
g.design: Medium: you have to connect two facts (the farmers adopted the seeds AND kept using local ideas) and see that this goes against the scholars' assumption. Choices A and C each get one part right, and D sounds reasonable if you skim.

c.instruction: 두 개의 짧은 텍스트(또는 텍스트와 연구 결과 요약)를 제시하고, 두 번째 텍스트의 저자나 연구자가 첫 번째 텍스트의 주장에 대해 보일 반응을 추론하는 문제를 만든다. 오답은 (1) 한쪽 텍스트 내용만으로 답한 경우, (2) 두 입장을 반대로 뒤바꾼 경우, (3) 두 텍스트 어디에도 없는 제3의 입장을 만든 경우로 구성한다.
c.seed: social science research — Psychologist Roy Baumeister's Ego Depletion Study on willpower as finite resource exhausted by self-control demands

g.passage:
Text 1
In a widely cited 1998 study, psychologist Roy Baumeister and colleagues asked hungry participants to resist a plate of freshly baked cookies and eat radishes instead. Afterward, these participants gave up on an unsolvable puzzle much sooner than participants who had been allowed to eat the cookies. Baumeister concluded that self-control draws on a limited inner resource, much like a muscle that tires with use: exerting willpower on one task leaves less of it available for the next.

Text 2
Psychologist Veronika Job and her colleagues surveyed participants about whether they believed willpower is easily used up or whether they believed exerting self-control can be energizing. Participants then completed a demanding self-control task followed by a second one. Only those who believed willpower is easily exhausted performed worse on the second task; participants who rejected that belief showed no decline. Job's team argued that people's beliefs about willpower shape whether its "depletion" appears at all.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would Job and her colleagues (Text 2) most likely respond to Baumeister's conclusion in Text 1?
options: They would argue that Baumeister's participants quit early on the puzzle because hunger, rather than any use of self-control, had weakened their concentration.
They would argue that Baumeister's conclusion holds for all people, since a demanding first task reliably drains a fixed store of willpower regardless of what participants believe.
They would argue that Baumeister's conclusion treats as a universal fact a decline that may depend on whether people expect their willpower to run out.
They would argue that Baumeister's conclusion overstates the role of willpower, since performance on a second task depends mainly on how skilled participants are at that task.
g.explanation:
정답 C: Text 2는 '의지력이 쉽게 고갈된다'고 믿는 사람에게서만 두 번째 과제 수행 저하가 나타났음을 보여 준다. 따라서 Job 팀은 Baumeister가 보편적 한정 자원으로 본 현상이 사실은 믿음에 좌우될 수 있다고 반응할 것이다.
A(제3의 입장): 배고픔이 원인이라는 설명은 두 텍스트 어디에도 없다. Job 팀은 생리 상태가 아니라 믿음을 변수로 제시한다.
B(입장 뒤바꿈/Text 1만 반영): '믿음과 무관하게 고정된 자원이 고갈된다'는 것은 Baumeister 쪽 논리이며, Text 2의 결과와 정면으로 충돌한다.
D(제3의 입장): 과제 숙련도는 어느 텍스트에서도 언급되지 않는다. '의지력 역할을 과장했다'는 표현이 그럴듯해 보일 뿐이다.
g.explanation_en:
Correct answer, C: Text 2 found that performance dropped on the second task only for people who believed willpower is easily used up. So Job's team would say that what Baumeister treated as a universal limited resource may actually depend on what people believe.
A is wrong because it brings in a third view. Neither text says hunger is the cause. Job's team points to beliefs, not physical state.
B is wrong because it reverses the stances and draws only on Text 1. The claim that a fixed store drains regardless of belief is Baumeister's logic, and Text 2's results contradict it.
D is wrong because it also adds a view found in neither text. Skill at the task is never mentioned. The phrase "overstates the role of willpower" only sounds like a critique Text 2 would make.
g.design: I paired a summary of Baumeister's study with a study on how beliefs moderate depletion, and the student has to infer the reaction. The wrong answers are a third view (hunger), a reversal that relies only on Text 1 (fixed depletion for everyone), and another third view (task skill). All options use the same "They would argue that..." frame.

c.instruction: 인물의 행동이나 진술에 표면적으로 드러나지 않는 의도나 태도를 짧은 지문으로 제시하고, 겉으로 말한 것과 실제 상황(또는 결과) 사이의 어긋남으로부터 함의를 추론하게 한다. 오답은 (1) 지문에 명시된 문장을 그대로 가져온 오답, (2) 어긋남을 반대로 해석한 오답, (3) 지문과 무관한 일반적 상식을 답으로 만든 오답으로 구성한다.
c.seed: social science research — Sociologist Erving Goffman's Footing concept analyzing conversational participation shifts and speaker alignment changes

g.passage: Sociologist Erving Goffman used the term "footing" to describe the stance a speaker takes toward their own words, noting that a person may present a statement as their own view or as someone else's. In one meeting that researchers recorded, a department manager announced a new scheduling policy that many employees disliked. When a staff member objected, the manager said, "Look, I'm just passing along what headquarters decided," even though the meeting notes later showed that the manager had drafted the policy and pushed for it at headquarters. A few minutes later, after an employee praised the policy's flexible break times, the manager answered, "Yes, I worked hard to get that part included."
g.question: Based on the text, what can most reasonably be inferred about the manager's comments during the meeting?
options: The manager was only passing along a decision made at headquarters, so the manager could not answer employees' objections.
The manager changed how the comments were presented because the manager came to doubt the policy after hearing the staff member's objection.
The manager's comments show that people in leadership roles usually avoid explaining unpopular decisions to the employees they affect.
The manager presented the same policy either as someone else's choice or as personal work, depending on whether the part being discussed was criticized or praised.
g.explanation:
정답 D: 매니저는 비판을 받을 때는 "본사 결정을 전할 뿐"이라며 정책을 남의 것처럼 말했지만, 실제로는 자신이 직접 정책 초안을 쓰고 밀어붙였다. 반면 칭찬을 받자 "내가 애써 넣었다"며 자기 공으로 돌렸다. 말한 것과 실제 사이의 이런 차이로 보아, 매니저는 반응에 따라 자기 말에 대한 입장(footing)을 전략적으로 바꿨다고 추론할 수 있다.
A: 지문에 나온 매니저의 말을 그대로 사실로 받아들인 오답이다. 회의록을 보면 그 말은 사실이 아니다.
B: 어긋남을 반대로 해석한 오답이다. 매니저는 정책을 의심한 것이 아니다. 오히려 칭찬받은 부분은 자기 공으로 내세웠다.
C: 지문과 상관없는 일반론이다. 지문은 리더 전반의 경향을 다루지 않고 한 사람의 입장 전환을 다룬다.
g.explanation_en:
Correct answer, D: When the manager was criticized, they said they were "just passing along" headquarters' decision. But the meeting notes show the manager actually drafted the policy and pushed for it. Later, when someone praised part of the policy, the manager took credit for it. This gap between what the manager said and what really happened suggests the manager changed their footing on purpose: they avoided responsibility when the policy was criticized and claimed ownership when it was praised.
A: This choice treats the manager's own words as true. The meeting notes show they weren't.
B: This choice reads the mismatch backward. Nothing in the text shows the manager came to doubt the policy. In fact, the manager proudly claimed part of it afterward.
C: This is a general claim about leaders that the text doesn't support. The text describes one manager's shifts, not a common pattern among leaders.
g.design: 이 문항은 회의록이 보여 주는 사실과 매니저가 말한 내용 사이의 어긋남에서 매니저가 입장을 전략적으로 바꿨다는 함의를 추론하게 만들었다. 오답은 세 가지 유형으로 구성했다. A는 지문의 말을 그대로 옮긴 것, B는 어긋남을 반대로 해석한 것, C는 지문과 무관한 일반 상식이다.

c.instruction: 지문에 하나의 넓은 주장과 그를 뒷받침하는 좁은 세부사실을 함께 제시하고, 지문 전체의 핵심 요지로 가장 적절한 범위의 진술을 고르게 한다. 오답은 (1) 세부사실 하나만을 전체 요지인 것처럼 과잉축소한 것, (2) 지문이 다루지 않은 범위까지 과잉확장한 것, (3) 넓은 주장과 세부사실을 뒤섞어 범위가 어긋난 것으로 구성한다.
c.seed: social science research — Linguist Paul Grice's Conversational Implicature theory explaining how speakers convey meaning beyond literal utterance

g.passage:
When a professor's recommendation letter for a student applying to graduate school in philosophy says only that the student "has excellent handwriting and always attended class," readers rarely conclude that the professor admires the student. Philosopher of language Paul Grice argued that such inferences are not accidents of interpretation but follow from a general expectation that conversation is cooperative: listeners assume that speakers are trying to say as much as is needed, no more, and to be truthful, relevant, and clear. Because the letter conspicuously omits any comment on the student's philosophical ability—the very thing a reader would need to know—the reader infers that the writer has nothing favorable to say about it.

Grice called meanings of this kind "implicatures," and he stressed that they differ from what words literally encode. An implicature can be canceled without contradiction: the professor could add, "and, incidentally, she is the most gifted philosopher I have taught," and the earlier inference would simply dissolve. Literal content cannot be withdrawn this way, which, for Grice, showed that much of what speakers communicate arises from shared assumptions about how conversation works rather than from the words themselves.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Grice held that listeners derive much unstated meaning by assuming speakers are cooperating, and that such meaning, unlike literal content, can be retracted.
Grice held that a recommendation letter silent about a student's ability signals the writer's low opinion of that student.
Grice held that nearly all human communication, spoken or not, depends on cooperative assumptions rather than on the meanings of words.
Grice held that implicatures can be canceled because recommendation letters are expected to say no more than is needed.
g.explanation:
정답 A: 지문의 넓은 주장(협력 가정에 따른 함축 추론)과 이를 문자적 의미와 구분하는 핵심 특징(취소 가능성)을 정확한 범위로 함께 담는다.
B(과잉축소): 추천서 사례는 이론을 보여 주는 세부사실 하나일 뿐 전체 요지가 아니다.
C(과잉확장): 지문은 화자가 전달하는 것 중 '상당 부분(much)'을 말할 뿐, 말 이외의 소통까지 포함한 '거의 모든' 소통이 단어 의미와 무관하다고 하지 않는다.
D(범위 혼합): 취소 가능성이라는 일반 원리와 추천서 사례를 잘못된 인과관계로 엮었다. 지문에서 취소 가능성은 함축이 문자적 내용과 다르기 때문이지, 추천서 관행 때문이 아니다.
g.explanation_en:
A is correct. It captures the passage's broad claim (listeners infer unstated meaning by assuming speakers are cooperating) along with the key feature that sets such meaning apart from literal content: it can be canceled. The scope is just right.
B is too narrow. The recommendation letter is only the example the passage uses to illustrate the theory, not the overall point.
C goes too far. The passage says "much" of what speakers communicate comes from shared assumptions. It never says nearly all communication, including nonspoken communication, works this way rather than through word meaning.
D blends the general principle and the example in the wrong way, creating a false cause. In the passage, implicatures can be canceled because they aren't part of literal content, not because of how recommendation letters are expected to be written.
g.design: 넓은 주장(협력 원리와 취소 가능한 함축)과 좁은 사례(추천서)를 함께 제시했다. 오답은 사례만 다룬 과잉축소, 'nearly all/spoken or not'으로 범위를 넓힌 과잉확장, 원리와 사례를 잘못된 인과로 엮은 범위 혼합으로 구성했고, 네 선택지 모두 같은 'Grice held that…' 문장 틀을 썼다.

c.instruction: 지문에 '한때 ~라고 여겨졌으나(통념)' 다음 'however/but/실제로는' 류의 전환어와 함께 이를 뒤집는 새 증거나 반박 문장을 제시하고, 빈칸이 그 반박된 결과를 표현하도록 한다. 정답은 통념과 정반대 방향의 의미를 가진 어휘로 하고, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 통념 쪽 단어를 그대로 쓴 것, (2) 전환어를 못 읽고 통념과 같은 방향이지만 강도만 다른 단어, (3) 반박 대상과 무관한 제3의 의미 단어로 구성한다. 전환 지점 앞뒤 문장만으로 답이 결정되게 하고 문장 길이나 어휘 난이도는 중간 수준을 유지한다.
c.seed: social science research — Anthropologist Sherry Ortner's Practice Theory examining how individual actions reproduce and transform social structures

g.passage: For decades, many anthropologists treated social structures—kinship rules, gender hierarchies, systems of rank—as forces operating largely above individuals, who were seen as simply carrying out roles assigned to them. In her work on practice theory, however, Sherry Ortner argued that everyday actions do more than passively mirror these systems: by repeating, bending, or resisting customs, people continually remake them. On her account, ordinary individuals are ______ both sustaining and altering the structures that shape their lives.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: incidental to
instrumental in
somewhat peripheral to
indifferent to
g.explanation:
정답 B. 'however' 앞 문장은 개인이 주어진 역할만 수행한다는 통념이고, 뒤 문장은 사람들이 관습을 반복·변형·저항하며 구조를 계속 '다시 만든다'고 반박한다. 따라서 Ortner의 견해에서 개인은 구조를 유지하고 바꾸는 데 핵심적 역할을 하는 존재, 즉 'instrumental in'이다.
A 'incidental to'(부수적인)는 반박된 통념을 그대로 반영한다.
C 'somewhat peripheral to'(다소 주변적인)는 전환어를 놓쳐 통념과 같은 방향에서 강도만 약하게 만든 것이다.
D 'indifferent to'(무관심한)는 역할의 크기가 아니라 개인의 태도에 관한 말이라 지문의 논점과 무관하다.
g.explanation_en:
The answer is B. The sentence before "however" gives the old view: individuals simply carry out roles assigned to them. The sentence after it rejects that view. People repeat, bend, or resist customs, and in doing so they "continually remake" social structures. So in Ortner's account, individuals play a central role in keeping structures going and in changing them. That makes them "instrumental in" doing so.
A ("incidental to") repeats the old view that the passage rejects.
C ("somewhat peripheral to") misses the turn at "however." It points the same way as the old view and just makes it a little weaker.
D ("indifferent to") describes how people feel, not how big a role they play, so it doesn't fit the passage's point.
g.design: The blank follows "however" and states the reversed view. The wrong answers are: A, the old view itself; C, the same direction as the old view but weaker; D, an unrelated meaning about attitude. All four options use the same "adjective + preposition" pattern.

c.instruction: 지문에 'is not X, but rather Y' 또는 'it isn't that A; instead B' 형태로 부정어 뒤에 대조 표현이 이어지는 문장을 만들고, 빈칸이 그 대조 표현(B) 자리에 오게 한다. 정답은 부정된 개념(X)과 반대 극성을 가진 어휘로 하고, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 부정어를 무시하고 X와 같은 의미 단어, (2) 부정 구조를 이중으로 잘못 해석해 극성을 다시 뒤집은 단어, (3) 대조 구조와 무관한 유사 발음/철자 단어로 구성한다.
c.seed: social science research — Psychologist Daniel Kahneman's Anchoring Effect demonstrating numerical priming influences on subsequent estimation judgments

g.passage: In a well-known experiment, psychologists Daniel Kahneman and Amos Tversky spun a rigged wheel that stopped on either 10 or 65, then asked participants to estimate the percentage of African nations in the United Nations. Those who saw 65 gave much higher estimates than those who saw 10, even though the number was obviously random. Afterward, most participants insisted that the wheel had played no part in their reasoning. The researchers therefore concluded that the pull of such an anchor is not a deliberate strategy that people choose to follow but rather an ______ influence, one that shapes judgments without the person ever noticing it.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: intentional
self-correcting
unwitting
unwritten
g.explanation: 정답 C(unwitting). 'not a deliberate strategy ... but rather ______' 구조에서 빈칸은 부정된 '의도적(deliberate)'과 반대 극성이어야 한다. 참가자들이 바퀴의 영향을 부인했다는 점과 'without the person ever noticing it'이 '자신도 모르는' 영향이라는 뜻을 뒷받침한다. A(intentional)는 부정어를 무시한 오답으로, deliberate와 같은 뜻이라 대조가 성립하지 않는다. B(self-correcting)는 부정을 이중으로 잘못 읽은 오답이다. '의도적이지 않다'를 '사람들이 의식적으로 바로잡는다'로 다시 뒤집어 해석한 것인데, 이는 의식적 통제를 전제하고 실험 결과(추정치가 앵커 쪽으로 쏠림)와도 어긋난다. D(unwritten)는 unwitting과 철자·발음만 비슷할 뿐, '성문화되지 않은'이라는 뜻이라 문맥과 관련이 없다.
g.explanation_en:
The correct answer is C (unwitting). The sentence uses a "not X but rather Y" pattern: the anchor's pull is "not a deliberate strategy" but rather an ______ influence. So the blank needs the opposite of "deliberate." Two clues back this up: participants denied that the wheel mattered, and the influence works "without the person ever noticing it." Both point to an influence people aren't aware of, which is what "unwitting" means.

A (intentional) ignores the negation. It means the same thing as "deliberate," so the contrast falls apart.

B (self-correcting) comes from misreading the negation and flipping it back again. It treats "not deliberate" as if people were consciously correcting for the anchor. That assumes the very conscious control the text rules out, and it also contradicts the result: estimates moved toward the anchor.

D (unwritten) only looks and sounds like "unwitting." It means "not written down," which has nothing to do with the context.
g.design: I put the blank in the Y slot of a "not a deliberate strategy but rather ___" sentence, so the answer is the opposite of "deliberate." The wrong answers are a synonym that ignores the negation, a double-negation misreading that suggests conscious correction, and a word that only looks and sounds like the answer.

c.instruction: 지문을 두 단계(예: 상황 묘사 후 화자의 숙고, 또는 기존 주장 소개 후 저자의 반박/선언)로 구성하고, 빈칸을 두 번째 단계의 시작 지점에 배치해 앞 단계와 다른 서술 기능을 하도록 한다. 정답은 두 번째 단계의 기능(숙고, 반박, 선언 등)에 맞는 어휘로 하고, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 첫 번째 단계에 어울리는 단어, (2) 두 단계 어디에도 맞지 않는 중립적 단어, (3) 의미는 비슷하나 문장이 요구하는 품사/기능이 다른 단어로 구성한다.
c.seed: social science research — Educationist Deborah Britzman's Queer Pedagogy framework interrogating heteronormative assumptions in classroom knowledge production

g.passage: In the 1990s, many teacher-education programs responded to the absence of gay and lesbian lives from school curricula by adding them in: a unit here, a novel there, each meant to supplement lessons already in place. Educationist Deborah Britzman, however, ______ this additive approach, arguing in her work on queer pedagogy that the deeper problem is not which knowledge is missing but how classrooms decide, before any lesson begins, what counts as "normal" knowledge at all.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: expanded upon
described
skeptical of
called into question
g.explanation:
지문은 두 단계로 되어 있다. 앞부분은 교육 프로그램들이 교육과정에 내용을 '추가'한 방식을 설명하고, 'however' 뒤 빈칸부터는 Britzman의 반박이 시작된다. 그는 문제가 빠진 지식에 있지 않고 무엇을 '정상적' 지식으로 보는지 정하는 방식 자체에 있다고 주장하므로, 추가 방식에 이의를 제기했다는 뜻의 D 'called into question'이 맞다.
A 'expanded upon(확장했다)'은 내용을 보충한다는 앞 단계의 흐름에는 어울리지만, 'however'와 뒤이은 반론과는 맞지 않는다.
B 'described(서술했다)'는 중립적인 말이라 앞 단계의 내용과도 뒤 단계의 비판 기능과도 연결되지 않는다.
C 'skeptical of'는 의미는 비슷하지만 형용사구다. 주어 뒤에 동사가 필요한 자리인데 'was'가 없어 문법적으로 성립하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en:
The text has two stages. The first describes how programs dealt with the gap by adding content. The second stage starts at the blank after "however," where Britzman pushes back: she argues the real problem is how classrooms decide what counts as "normal" knowledge, not which content is missing. So the blank needs a verb phrase that expresses a challenge, and "called into question" (D) fits.
A, "expanded upon," fits the first stage's idea of supplementing content, but it clashes with "however" and with the critique that follows.
B, "described," is neutral. It does nothing to signal the rebuttal that the second stage requires.
C, "skeptical of," is close in meaning, but it's an adjective phrase. The sentence needs a main verb after the subject, and without "was" the sentence is ungrammatical.
g.design: The blank opens the second stage (the rebuttal after "however"). The wrong answers are a phrase that fits the first stage (expanded upon), a neutral verb (described), and a phrase with similar meaning but the wrong part of speech (skeptical of).

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: physical science — Graphene production methods and electrical conductivity enhancement techniques

g.passage: Graphene, a single layer of carbon atoms arranged in a hexagonal lattice, conducts electricity remarkably well in laboratory samples, but the methods used to make it in large quantities tend to undermine that property. The cheapest approach, chemically peeling apart graphite and then removing the oxygen added during the process, yields large amounts of material, yet the resulting flakes are riddled with holes and leftover oxygen groups that scatter electrons. Materials scientist Priya Raman and her colleagues reasoned that the defects themselves might be repaired after production rather than avoided beforehand. They exposed chemically produced graphene to a brief pulse of intense microwave radiation, which heated the flakes to over 2,000°C in about two seconds. The treatment drove off most of the remaining oxygen and allowed carbon atoms to resettle into an orderly lattice, raising the material's conductivity nearly to that of graphene grown by slower, far more expensive vapor-deposition methods.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Researchers found that flaws introduced by an inexpensive way of making graphene could be largely corrected afterward, bringing its electrical performance close to that of costlier graphene.
Researchers found that an inexpensive way of making graphene could be modified to prevent flaws from forming, making costlier production methods unnecessary for most uses.
Researchers found that heating graphene to extreme temperatures removes oxygen groups, although the process leaves its carbon lattice too disordered to conduct electricity well.
Researchers found that graphene made by vapor deposition conducts electricity better than any other form of carbon, which explains why it remains the most widely used type.
g.design: 정답은 '사후 결함 복구'라는 핵심을 바꿔 말하고, B는 '사전 예방'으로 Raman의 논리를 뒤집었으며, C는 산소 제거라는 세부는 맞지만 결과를 반대로, D는 지엽적 비교 대상을 중심으로 삼았다. 모든 선택지가 같은 'Researchers found that...' 틀을 쓴다.
g.explanation: 지문은 값싼 화학적 그래핀 생산법이 결함을 남기지만, Raman 연구팀이 마이크로파 처리로 생산 후 결함을 복구해 고가 방식에 가까운 전도도를 얻었다고 설명하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 결함을 '사전에 막는다'고 하지만 지문은 미리 피하는 대신 나중에 고친다고 명시하며, 고가 방식이 불필요하다는 주장도 없다. C는 산소 제거는 맞지만 탄소 원자가 질서 있는 격자로 재배열되어 전도도가 올랐다는 내용과 반대된다. D는 기상 증착 그래핀을 비교 기준으로만 언급한 점을 과장했고, 가장 널리 쓰인다는 정보도 지문에 없다.
g.explanation_en: The text explains that cheap chemical production leaves graphene full of defects, and that Raman's team used a microwave pulse to repair those defects after production, bringing conductivity close to that of expensive vapor-grown graphene, so A is correct. B says the flaws are prevented from forming, but the text specifically says the defects were repaired afterward instead of avoided, and it never claims that costlier methods become unnecessary. C is right that oxygen is removed, but it contradicts the text, which says the carbon atoms resettled into an orderly lattice and conductivity increased. D takes vapor-deposited graphene, which the text mentions only as a point of comparison, and makes it the focus; the text also never says it is the most widely used type.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

c.seed: physical science — Perovskite crystal lattice defects affecting solar cell efficiency

g.passage: Perovskite solar cells have attracted attention because they can be made cheaply from solutions rather than from the ultrapure silicon wafers that conventional panels require. That low-temperature processing, however, leaves the crystals riddled with defects, such as missing ions and misaligned grain boundaries. Researchers long assumed these flaws would trap electrons and sharply reduce efficiency, as similar defects do in silicon. Yet perovskite cells routinely convert more than 25 percent of sunlight into electricity. Studies by materials physicists suggest an explanation: most of the common defects in perovskites create energy states that lie very close to the edges of the material's energy bands rather than deep within the gap between them. Electrons that fall into such shallow states can easily escape again, so the defects do little to hinder the flow of current. The material, in other words, appears to be unusually tolerant of its own imperfections.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Perovskite solar cells reach high efficiency because researchers have learned to remove nearly all the defects that solution processing creates.
Perovskite solar cells perform well despite their many crystal defects because those defects mostly produce energy states that barely impede electrons.
Perovskite solar cells are more efficient than silicon panels because perovskite defects free trapped electrons that silicon would hold.
Perovskite solar cells are cheaper to make than silicon panels because they can be processed at low temperatures from solutions.
g.explanation: 지문은 페로브스카이트 결정에 결함이 많은데도 효율이 높은 이유가 결함이 얕은 에너지 준위를 만들어 전자 흐름을 거의 방해하지 않기 때문이라고 설명하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 결함이 제거되었다고 하지만, 지문에서는 결함이 그대로 남아 있어도 영향이 적다고 한다. C는 실리콘과 비교해 더 효율적이라고 주장하고 결함이 전자를 풀어 준다고 하는데, 둘 다 지문에 없는 내용이다. D는 지문 앞부분의 세부 내용일 뿐이고 글의 핵심인 결함 허용성을 담지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: B is correct because the text explains that perovskite cells stay efficient despite having many defects. Most of those defects create shallow energy states that electrons can easily escape. A is wrong because the text says the defects remain, not that they are removed. C makes two claims the text doesn't support: that perovskites are more efficient than silicon, and that the defects actively release electrons. D repeats a detail from the opening but misses the text's central point, which is that the material tolerates its defects.
g.design: I made all four choices use the same "Perovskite solar cells ... because ..." frame. A and C each contain partly correct ideas, so you have to compare them closely with the text to rule them out. D is a true detail from the opening, which makes it a tempting choice for someone who only skims.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

c.seed: physical science — Aerogel synthesis and thermal insulation properties at extreme temperatures

g.passage: Aerogels, made by replacing the liquid in a gel with gas while leaving its solid framework intact, are among the best thermal insulators ever produced. Their effectiveness comes from structure: a web of nanoscale pores so small that gas molecules collide with pore walls more often than with one another, which sharply limits heat transfer. Traditional silica aerogels, however, have a weakness. Above roughly 600°C, their delicate silica networks begin to sinter, with the particles fusing so that the pores collapse, and they turn brittle enough to crack under repeated heating and cooling. In 2019, a team led by materials scientist Xiang Xu reported an aerogel built from hexagonal boron nitride arranged in a double-paned, hyperbolic architecture. Instead of fracturing when heated, the material's thin walls flex slightly, absorbing the strain. The aerogel kept its insulating ability after hundreds of rapid swings between about −198°C and 900°C, conditions that would ruin conventional silica versions.
g.question: According to the text, what problem did the aerogel developed by Xu's team overcome?
options: Gas molecules in conventional aerogels collide with one another too frequently, allowing heat to pass through the pores.
Conventional aerogels lose their insulating ability when cooled to around −198°C because their pores fill with condensed gas.
Conventional aerogels tend to degrade structurally when exposed to high heat and repeated temperature changes.
Conventional aerogels are too rigid to be shaped into the double-paned forms needed for practical insulation.
g.explanation: 지문은 기존 실리카 에어로겔이 약 600°C 이상에서 소결되어 기공이 무너지고, 가열과 냉각이 반복되면 균열이 생길 만큼 부서지기 쉬워진다고 설명한다. 이어서 Xu 연구팀의 질화붕소 에어로겔은 휘어지며 변형을 흡수해 극심한 온도 변화를 수백 번 겪고도 단열 성능을 유지했다고 하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 오히려 나노 기공이 기체 분자끼리의 충돌을 줄여 준다는 지문 내용과 반대이며, 기존 에어로겔이 해결해야 할 문제로 제시되지도 않았다. B는 −198°C라는 수치를 끌어왔지만 저온에서 기체가 응축된다는 설명은 지문에 없다. D는 '이중 창' 구조를 언급하지만, 기존 에어로겔이 그 형태로 성형되지 못한다는 내용은 지문에 없다.
g.explanation_en: The text explains that conventional silica aerogels sinter above roughly 600°C, which makes their pores collapse, and that they turn brittle enough to crack under repeated heating and cooling. Xu's boron nitride aerogel flexes to absorb strain and survives hundreds of extreme temperature swings, so C is correct. A actually reverses the text: the nanoscale pores reduce collisions between gas molecules, and the text never presents those collisions as a problem with conventional aerogels. B borrows the −198°C figure, but the text says nothing about gas condensing at low temperatures. D mentions the double-paned design, but the text never says conventional aerogels can't be shaped that way.

c.seed: physical science — Sonoluminescence bubble collapse creating light from acoustic cavitation

g.passage: When a liquid is blasted with intense sound waves, tiny gas bubbles can form, swell, and then collapse violently, a process called acoustic cavitation. In 1990, physicist Felipe Gaitan showed that a single bubble trapped in a flask of water by a standing sound wave could be made to collapse over and over, giving off a faint flash of blue-white light with each cycle. This effect, called sonoluminescence, had first been noticed decades earlier in clouds of bubbles, but isolating one bubble let researchers time the flashes precisely. They found that each flash lasts less than a billionth of a second, far shorter than many had expected. Yet even with this precision, researchers still disagree about what produces the light. Some argue that the collapsing bubble heats its gas enough to form a glowing plasma, while others propose that the light comes from chemical reactions or from electric charges separating at the bubble wall, and no single model yet accounts for all the measurements.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Trapping a single bubble showed that sonoluminescence flashes last far longer than earlier studies of bubble clouds had suggested.
Gaitan's single-bubble experiment confirmed that sonoluminescence results from gas heated into a glowing plasma during collapse.
Researchers abandoned the study of bubble clouds after Gaitan found that a single bubble produces brighter and more regular flashes.
Although isolating one bubble let researchers measure sonoluminescence precisely, the cause of its light remains unsettled.
g.explanation: 지문은 단일 기포 실험으로 섬광을 정밀하게 측정할 수 있게 되었지만, 빛의 원인에 대해서는 여전히 합의가 없다는 점을 중심으로 하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 섬광 시간을 언급하지만, 섬광은 예상보다 '짧았다'고 했으므로 방향이 반대다. B는 플라스마 가설을 언급하지만, 그것은 여러 가설 중 하나일 뿐 실험으로 확인된 것이 아니다. C는 기포 구름 연구를 포기했다거나 더 밝았다는 내용을 담고 있는데, 이는 지문에 나오지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The text's focus is that a single-bubble setup made precise measurement of the flashes possible, but scientists still disagree about what causes the light, so D is correct. A mentions flash duration, but the text says the flashes were shorter than expected, not longer. B names the plasma idea, but the text presents it as only one of several competing explanations, not a confirmed one. C claims that researchers abandoned bubble-cloud studies and that the flashes were brighter, and the text says neither.
g.design: 오답 A와 B는 지문의 실제 세부(섬광 시간, 플라스마 가설)를 활용하되 방향을 뒤집거나 과도하게 확정했다. 그래서 '정밀 측정 + 원인 미해결'이라는 두 정보를 함께 연결해야 정답 D를 고를 수 있다.

c.seed: physical science — Metamaterial negative refractive index and invisibility cloak design

g.passage: Metamaterials are engineered structures built from repeating units smaller than the wavelength of the light or radio waves they are meant to control. Because their behavior depends on the shape and arrangement of these units rather than on their chemical makeup, some metamaterials can bend waves in the "wrong" direction, giving them a negative refractive index—a property no natural substance has. This ability has fueled widespread excitement about invisibility cloaks that would guide light smoothly around an object, as water flows around a stone. Physicist Andrea Alù and others, however, have pointed out a stubborn obstacle. The resonant structures that produce such unusual bending work well only within a narrow band of frequencies, and they absorb some of the energy passing through them. A cloak tuned to hide an object from one color of light would therefore leave the object visible, and possibly casting a faint shadow, under ordinary white light. For this reason, the most successful demonstrations so far have concealed small objects from microwaves or a single wavelength, not from the full range of light the human eye detects.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Although metamaterials can bend waves in ways natural substances cannot, their reliance on narrow-band resonant structures limits their use for hiding objects from everyday visible light.
Although metamaterials can bend waves in ways natural substances cannot, their chemical makeup must be altered before they can be used to hide objects from microwaves.
Although metamaterials have generated excitement about invisibility cloaks, researchers have now built cloaks that conceal objects across the full range of visible light.
Although metamaterials are made of units smaller than a wavelength, their main scientific value lies in absorbing energy rather than in redirecting waves.
g.explanation: 지문은 메타물질이 음의 굴절률이라는 특이한 성질을 가지지만, 그 성질을 만드는 공진 구조가 좁은 주파수 대역에서만 작동하고 에너지를 흡수하기 때문에 일반 백색광에서 물체를 숨기기 어렵다는 점을 핵심으로 제시하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 지문이 메타물질의 성질은 화학 조성이 아니라 구조에서 나온다고 했고, 마이크로파 은폐는 이미 성공했다고 했으므로 틀리다. C는 가시광선 전 범위를 숨기는 것은 아직 이루지 못했다는 지문 내용과 반대된다. D는 에너지 흡수를 장점이 아니라 한계로 언급한 지문 내용을 잘못 해석했다.
g.explanation_en: The passage explains that metamaterials can have a negative refractive index, but the resonant structures behind this property work only in a narrow frequency band and absorb energy, so cloaks fail under ordinary white light. That makes A the correct answer. B is wrong because the text says metamaterial behavior comes from structure, not chemical makeup, and it says microwave cloaking has already been demonstrated. C contradicts the passage, which says the full visible range has not yet been achieved. D misreads energy absorption, which the text presents as a drawback, not as the material's main value.
g.design: 이 문항은 중간 난이도에 맞춰 지문에서 두 정보를 연결해야 풀리도록 만들었다. 메타물질이 가진 특이한 성질과 실제 응용을 가로막는 한계를 함께 묶어야 주제가 잡힌다. 오답 B와 D는 지문에 나온 세부 정보(화학 조성, 마이크로파, 에너지 흡수, 파장보다 작은 단위)를 잘못 결합한 것이고, C는 글 앞부분의 기대감만 훑어 읽은 학생이 고르도록 설계했다.

c.seed: physical science — Catalytic converters palladium surface reactions reducing emissions

g.passage: Catalytic converters reduce harmful car exhaust by passing it over thin coatings of metals such as palladium. Molecules of carbon monoxide and unburned hydrocarbons stick briefly to the palladium surface, where they react with oxygen to form less harmful carbon dioxide and water. For decades, engineers assumed that the more palladium a converter contained, the cleaner its output would be. However, chemist Lena Ortiz and her colleagues found that this assumption breaks down when the engine is cold. In their tests, converters with heavy palladium loading performed no better during the first minutes after startup than converters with far less metal, because at low temperatures carbon monoxide molecules crowd the surface so densely that oxygen cannot reach the reactive sites. Ortiz's team concluded that how the palladium is arranged, such as spreading it into tiny, well-separated clusters, matters more for cold-start emissions than how much of it is used.
g.question: According to the text, what did Ortiz's team identify as the reason that extra palladium fails to lower emissions right after an engine is started?
options: Palladium does not react with oxygen until the converter has reached the temperature of a fully warmed engine.
One exhaust gas covers the metal so completely that a needed reactant is kept from the sites where reactions take place.
Heavy loading makes the palladium clump into large clusters that trap unburned hydrocarbons inside the converter.
Carbon dioxide and water produced in the first minutes build up on the metal and block further reactions.
g.explanation: 지문은 낮은 온도에서 일산화탄소 분자가 표면을 빽빽하게 덮어 산소가 반응 자리에 닿지 못한다고 설명하므로, 이를 바꿔 말한 B가 정답이다. A는 온도가 중요하다는 점은 맞지만, 원인을 일산화탄소의 표면 점유가 아니라 팔라듐 자체가 반응하지 않는 것으로 잘못 설명한다. C는 팔라듐 배열(클러스터)이라는 지문 요소를 쓰지만, 클러스터가 탄화수소를 가둔다는 내용은 지문에 없다. D는 표면이 막힌다는 생각은 맞지만, 막는 물질을 생성물(이산화탄소와 물)로 바꿔 놓았다.
g.explanation_en: The text says that at low temperatures, carbon monoxide molecules crowd the palladium surface so densely that oxygen can't reach the reactive sites, so B, which restates this, is correct. A is right that temperature matters, but it blames the palladium itself for not reacting instead of carbon monoxide covering the surface. C uses the text's idea of clusters, but the text never says clusters trap hydrocarbons. D gets the idea of a blocked surface right but swaps in the wrong blocker: the products, carbon dioxide and water, rather than carbon monoxide.
g.design: 정답은 '일산화탄소'·'산소'를 '한 배기가스'·'필요한 반응물'로 바꿔 써서 단어만 맞춰 보는 방식으로는 찾을 수 없게 했다. 오답 A, D는 원인의 일부(온도, 표면 막힘)만 맞게 담아 지문과 꼼꼼히 비교해야 배제된다.

c.seed: physical science — Quantum tunneling in scanning tunneling microscope tip-sample interactions

g.passage: A scanning tunneling microscope (STM) images surfaces by holding an extremely sharp metal tip a fraction of a nanometer above a conducting sample. Classical physics predicts that electrons should not cross the gap between tip and sample, since they lack the energy to pass through the empty space separating them. Quantum mechanics, however, allows electrons to "tunnel" through this barrier, producing a small but measurable current. Crucially, this tunneling current falls off exponentially as the gap widens: increasing the distance by roughly one tenth of a nanometer can reduce the current by about a factor of ten. Because of this steep dependence, nearly all of the current flows through the single atom at the very end of the tip, and even tiny variations in the height of the sample surface produce large changes in current. By scanning the tip across a surface and recording these changes, researchers can map the positions of individual atoms.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: The STM works by giving electrons enough energy to overcome the gap between the tip and the sample, which classical physics had wrongly considered impassable.
The STM's tip must be sharpened to a single atom because a blunter tip would prevent any tunneling current from flowing across the gap.
The STM can resolve individual atoms because the electron current it relies on is extremely sensitive to the distance between tip and sample.
The STM measures a tunneling current that is too small to detect directly, so researchers infer atomic positions from changes in the gap's width.
g.explanation: 지문은 터널링 전류가 간격에 지수적으로 민감하다는 점을 설명하고, 이 민감성 때문에 개별 원자를 지도화할 수 있다고 연결하므로 C가 중심 내용이다. A는 전자에게 에너지를 주어 장벽을 넘게 한다고 했지만, 지문은 에너지가 부족해도 터널링한다고 말한다. B는 팁 끝 원자를 언급하지만, 지문은 민감성 때문에 전류가 끝 원자로 집중된다고 했을 뿐 뭉툭한 팁이면 전류가 전혀 흐르지 않는다고 하지 않았다. D는 전류가 '작지만 측정 가능하다'는 지문 내용과 모순된다.
g.explanation_en: The text explains that tunneling current depends exponentially on the gap and then links that sensitivity to the ability to map individual atoms, so C states the main idea. A is wrong because the text says electrons tunnel even though they lack the energy to cross, not that they're given enough energy. B mentions the atom at the tip, but the text says current concentrates there because of the steep distance dependence; it never says a blunter tip would stop the current completely. D contradicts the text, which describes the current as small but measurable.
g.design: 이 문항은 두 정보, 즉 전류가 거리에 지수적으로 민감하다는 점과 그래서 원자를 분해할 수 있다는 점을 연결해야 풀린다. 오답 B와 D는 지문의 세부 내용(팁 끝 원자, 작은 전류)을 일부 그대로 쓰면서 그 내용을 왜곡하도록 만들었다. A는 그럴듯하게 들리지만 고전 물리학식으로 잘못 설명하는 선택지다.
