g.passage: Metal-organic frameworks, or MOFs, are crystals built from metal atoms linked by carbon-based molecules. Chemists often make them through hydrothermal synthesis, heating the ingredients in water inside a sealed container until the crystals form. The resulting structures are full of tiny pores, much like a sponge. In a recent series of tests, a research team made several MOFs this way and measured how much carbon dioxide each one could hold. The samples with the most internal pore space consistently stored the most gas, while denser samples with fewer open spaces stored far less. The team concluded that, for these materials, the amount of empty space inside the crystal is what mainly determines how much gas the material can capture.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Tests on several MOFs suggest that a crystal's internal openness largely controls how much carbon dioxide it can take up.
Tests on several MOFs suggest that heating ingredients in sealed water containers is the only way to produce such crystals.
Tests on several MOFs suggest that denser crystals are generally better than open ones at trapping carbon dioxide.
Tests on several MOFs suggest that the type of metal atom chosen matters more than the crystal's structure for storing gas.
g.explanation: 지문은 MOF의 제조 방식을 소개한 뒤, 내부 기공 공간이 많을수록 이산화탄소를 더 많이 저장한다는 실험 결과와 결론으로 마무리하므로 A가 중심 생각이다. B는 수열 합성을 언급한 세부 내용을 '유일한 방법'으로 과장한 것이다. C는 밀도가 높은 시료가 훨씬 적게 저장했다는 지문 내용과 반대이다. D의 금속 원자 종류는 지문에서 비교된 적이 없다.
g.explanation_en: The text introduces how MOFs are made, then reports that samples with more internal pore space stored more carbon dioxide and concludes that empty space mainly determines gas capture, so A is the main idea. B takes a background detail about hydrothermal synthesis and wrongly claims it is the only method. C reverses the finding, since the denser samples stored far less. D brings up the type of metal atom, which the text never compares.
g.design: 쉬운 난이도: 마지막 문장의 결론을 바꿔 말한 정답 하나만 고르면 되며, 오답은 세부 내용 과장, 결과 반대로 말하기, 언급되지 않은 요인 끌어오기라는 전형적 오류로 구성했다.

c.instruction:
- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: physical science — Dielectric constant manipulation in ferroelectric ceramics for capacitor energy storage applications

g.passage: Capacitors store electrical energy, and engineers often build them from ferroelectric ceramics such as barium titanate. These materials have a very high dielectric constant, a measure of how well a material can hold electric charge when voltage is applied. However, a high dielectric constant alone does not guarantee good energy storage. When a strong voltage is applied, the dielectric constant of many ferroelectric ceramics drops sharply, which limits how much energy the capacitor can actually hold. To address this problem, researchers add small amounts of other elements, such as strontium or bismuth, to the ceramic. These additions make the material's response to voltage more stable, so the dielectric constant stays higher under strong voltage, allowing the capacitor to store more energy.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Ferroelectric ceramics such as barium titanate are rarely used in capacitors because their dielectric constant is too low to store useful amounts of energy.
Adding certain elements to ferroelectric ceramics can keep their charge-holding ability from falling under strong voltage, which improves how much energy capacitors can store.
Strontium and bismuth are able to store more electrical energy on their own than any ferroelectric ceramic can.
Capacitors made from ferroelectric ceramics store the most energy when only a weak voltage is applied to them.
g.design: 문제(강한 전압에서 유전율 감소)와 해결책(원소 첨가)이라는 단순한 구조로, 한 단계 추론으로 중심 내용을 파악하게 했다. 오답은 지문 일부를 왜곡하거나 세부만 과장한 전형적 오개념이다.
g.explanation: 지문은 강유전성 세라믹의 유전율이 강한 전압에서 떨어지는 문제를 제시한 뒤, 다른 원소를 첨가하면 유전율이 높게 유지되어 에너지 저장량이 늘어난다고 설명하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 지문에서 이 세라믹들의 유전율이 매우 높다고 했으므로 틀렸다. C는 첨가 원소 자체가 에너지를 저장한다고 하지만, 지문은 그 원소들이 세라믹을 안정시킨다고만 말한다. D는 약한 전압에 대한 주장으로, 지문에서 다루지 않는 내용이며 해결책이라는 중심 내용을 놓친다.
g.explanation_en: The text first describes a problem, which is that the dielectric constant of ferroelectric ceramics drops under strong voltage. It then gives a solution: adding other elements keeps that value high so the capacitor stores more energy. That makes B the correct answer. A is wrong because the text says these ceramics have a very high dielectric constant, not a low one. C is wrong because the added elements stabilize the ceramic; the text never says they store energy on their own. D makes a claim about weak voltage that the text never makes, and it misses the main point about the solution.

c.instruction:
- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).
- 세부 기술 힌트: 수식어가 짧은 주어-동사 수 일치, 시제 일관성, 대명사 격/수 일치처럼 한 규칙을 묻는 문제.
c.seed: physical science — Creep deformation in concrete and time-dependent structural failure under sustained loading stress

g.passage: Concrete may look perfectly rigid, but under a heavy load that never lets up, it slowly changes shape over months or even years. This gradual deformation, known as creep, ______ engineers to plan carefully when designing bridges and tall buildings, since a beam that sags a little more each year can eventually crack.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: force
are forcing
forces
have forced
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 "deformation"이고, "known as creep"은 주어를 설명하는 삽입 수식어일 뿐이다. 따라서 단수 동사가 필요하며, 현재 시제로 일반적 사실을 서술하는 C의 "forces"가 정답이다. A의 "force", B의 "are forcing", D의 "have forced"는 모두 복수 주어에 맞는 형태이므로 단수 주어 "deformation"과 수가 일치하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "deformation"; the phrase "known as creep" is just a modifier describing it. So the sentence needs a singular verb, and C, "forces," correctly states a general fact in the present tense. A ("force"), B ("are forcing"), and D ("have forced") are all plural verb forms, so none of them agrees with the singular subject "deformation."
g.design: 짧은 삽입 수식어(known as creep) 뒤의 단수 주어와 동사의 수 일치라는 단일 규칙만 묻는다. 오답은 모두 복수형으로, 바로 앞의 "creep"이나 복수 명사 "engineers"에 이끌린 학생이 고를 만하다.

c.instruction:
- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).
- 세부 기술 힌트: 수식어가 짧은 주어-동사 수 일치, 시제 일관성, 대명사 격/수 일치처럼 한 규칙을 묻는 문제.
c.seed: physical science — Triboluminescence mechanical stress generating light in crystalline mineral fracture events

g.passage: When certain crystals, such as quartz or sugar, are crushed or split apart, they can give off brief flashes of light. This effect, known as triboluminescence, occurs because the breaking of a crystal separates electric charges along the newly formed surfaces. The rapid movement of these charges across the tiny gap between the surfaces ______ the surrounding air, causing it to glow for a fraction of a second.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: excite
have excited
are exciting
excites
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 "movement"이고, "of these charges across the tiny gap between the surfaces"는 주어를 꾸미는 수식어일 뿐이다. 따라서 단수 동사 "excites"가 필요하며, 현재 시제도 지문의 다른 동사(occurs, separates)와 맞으므로 D가 정답이다. A, B, C는 모두 복수 동사로, 주어 가까이에 있는 복수 명사 "charges"나 "surfaces"를 주어로 착각할 때 고르기 쉬운 오답이다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "movement." The phrase "of these charges across the tiny gap between the surfaces" just describes the subject. So the sentence needs a singular verb, "excites," and its present tense also matches the other verbs in the text (occurs, separates). That makes D correct. A, B, and C are all plural verbs, and they're easy to pick if you mistake a nearby plural noun like "charges" or "surfaces" for the subject.
g.design: 짧은 전치사구가 단수 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어 있는 주어-동사 수 일치 하나만을 묻는다. 오답은 모두 복수 동사로, 가까운 복수 명사에 끌리는 흔한 실수를 노렸다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: physical science — Nucleation rate control in protein crystallography determining crystal quality and size uniformity

g.passage: Protein crystallographers have long struggled to grow crystals that are both large and well ordered. In a typical supersaturated protein solution, many tiny nuclei form at once, and these nuclei then compete for the same dissolved protein, yielding a shower of small, unevenly sized crystals. Biophysicist Lena Haugland and colleagues propose that the problem lies chiefly in the timing of nucleation rather than in growth conditions themselves. They hypothesize that if nucleation is confined to a brief initial burst—for example, by holding a solution at high supersaturation for only a few minutes and then diluting it to a level where existing crystals can grow but new nuclei cannot form—the resulting crystals will be more uniform in size and of higher diffraction quality than crystals grown under constant conditions.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Haugland and colleagues' hypothesis?
options: Lysozyme samples exposed to high supersaturation for five minutes and then diluted produced crystals that varied little in size and diffracted to higher resolution than samples kept at a single constant supersaturation.
Lysozyme samples kept at constant high supersaturation produced more crystals per drop than samples kept at constant low supersaturation, though crystal quality was similar in both groups.
Lysozyme samples exposed to high supersaturation for five minutes and then diluted produced crystals that grew faster during the first hour than crystals in samples kept at constant conditions.
Lysozyme samples diluted after a brief period of high supersaturation produced crystals that diffracted no better than those from samples in which new nuclei continued to form throughout growth.
g.explanation: 가설은 핵생성을 짧은 초기 구간에 한정하면 일정 조건에서 키운 결정보다 크기가 균일하고 회절 품질이 높은 결정이 생긴다는 것이다. A는 바로 이 처리군과 일정 조건 대조군을 비교해 크기 균일성과 회절 품질이 모두 향상되었음을 보여 주므로 가설을 직접 지지한다. B는 과포화도에 따라 결정 수가 달라짐을 보여 주지만, 핵생성 시점을 조절하는 처리를 시험하지 않았다. C는 같은 처리를 사용하지만 초기 성장 속도만 보고하며, 가설이 다루는 크기 균일성이나 품질은 다루지 않는다. D는 회절 품질이 개선되지 않았음을 보여 주므로 오히려 가설을 약화한다.
g.explanation_en: The hypothesis says that limiting nucleation to a brief initial burst will produce crystals that are more uniform in size and diffract better than crystals grown under constant conditions. Choice A compares exactly that treatment with constant conditions and reports better size uniformity and better diffraction, so it directly supports the hypothesis. Choice B shows that supersaturation level affects how many crystals form, but it never tests the timed-burst approach. Choice C uses the right treatment but reports only early growth speed, not the size uniformity or quality the hypothesis predicts. Choice D shows no gain in diffraction quality, so it actually weakens the hypothesis.
g.design: 오답 B·C는 각각 핵생성과 같은 처리를 다루어 부분적으로 관련이 있어 보이지만 가설이 예측한 결과(균일성+품질)를 대조군과 비교하지 않는다. D는 같은 처리를 다루지만 반대 방향의 결과다. 따라서 정답을 고르려면 처리 방식과 결과 측정 항목을 함께 확인해야 한다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: physical science — Acoustic absorption coefficient of porous foam materials and sound wave energy dissipation mechanisms

g.passage: Open-cell polymer foams are widely used to absorb sound, but engineers disagree about which mechanism accounts for most of the energy they remove from an incoming wave. One view holds that the dominant loss comes from viscous friction: as air is forced back and forth through the narrow, interconnected pores, it rubs against the pore walls and its kinetic energy is converted to heat. Materials scientist Leena Okafor proposes an alternative. She argues that in foams with relatively flexible struts, the dominant loss instead comes from the solid skeleton itself, which flexes with each pressure cycle and dissipates energy internally, so that the stiffness of the foam's frame—not the size of its pores—chiefly determines how much sound it absorbs.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Okafor's hypothesis?
options: When two flexible-strut foams with identical frame stiffness but different pore sizes were tested, the foam with narrower pores absorbed noticeably more sound energy.
When two flexible-strut foams with identical pore sizes but different frame stiffness were tested, the foam with the softer frame absorbed noticeably more sound energy.
When a flexible-strut foam was heated slightly during testing, its temperature rose by a measurable amount, showing that absorbed sound energy had been converted to heat.
When flexible-strut foams were compared with rigid-strut foams of similar thickness, both types absorbed more sound at high frequencies than at low frequencies.
g.explanation: Okafor은 유연한 골격 폼에서 흡음량을 주로 결정하는 것이 기공 크기가 아니라 골격의 강성이라고 주장한다. B는 기공 크기를 같게 고정하고 강성만 바꿨을 때 흡음량이 달라졌음을 보여 주므로 이 주장을 가장 직접적으로 뒷받침한다. A는 기공 크기가 흡음을 좌우한다는 결과이므로 오히려 경쟁 견해인 점성 마찰 쪽을 지지한다. C의 열 변환은 두 메커니즘 모두에서 일어나므로 둘을 구별하지 못한다. D는 두 종류의 폼이 비슷하게 행동했다는 결과일 뿐 강성의 역할을 따로 떼어 보여 주지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: Okafor claims that in flexible-strut foams, the stiffness of the frame, not pore size, mainly determines how much sound is absorbed. B keeps pore size fixed and changes only stiffness, and absorption changes, so it most directly supports her claim. A shows pore size controlling absorption, which actually supports the competing viscous-friction view. C shows conversion to heat, but both mechanisms produce heat, so it can't tell them apart. D only shows the two foam types behaving similarly across frequencies, so it doesn't isolate the role of stiffness.
g.design: To answer, students must link Okafor's mechanism to the variable it predicts (frame stiffness) and then pick the finding that holds pore size constant. A uses the same sentence frame but supports the rival view, and C is a tempting partial match because it mentions heat.

c.instruction: 두 개의 짧은 텍스트(또는 텍스트와 연구 결과 요약)를 제시하고, 두 번째 텍스트의 저자나 연구자가 첫 번째 텍스트의 주장에 대해 보일 반응을 추론하는 문제를 만든다. 오답은 (1) 한쪽 텍스트 내용만으로 답한 경우, (2) 두 입장을 반대로 뒤바꾼 경우, (3) 두 텍스트 어디에도 없는 제3의 입장을 만든 경우로 구성한다.
c.seed: physical science — Ionic conductivity enhancement in solid-state electrolytes through doping strategy optimization

g.passage:
Text 1
Solid-state electrolytes could make lithium batteries safer, but most conduct lithium ions far more slowly than liquid electrolytes do. Materials scientist Rena Okafor argues that the remedy is aggressive doping: replacing as many host atoms as possible with ions of a different charge. Each substitution creates vacancies in the crystal lattice, she notes, and because lithium ions hop from vacancy to vacancy, more dopant should mean more open pathways and therefore steadily higher conductivity.

Text 2
In a study of a garnet-type electrolyte, Tomas Lindqvist and colleagues replaced increasing fractions of zirconium with tantalum. Conductivity rose as tantalum was added, but only up to a modest concentration. Beyond that point, conductivity fell: the researchers found that the excess vacancies began to cluster together and bind to nearby dopant ions, trapping lithium ions rather than freeing them to move. The team concluded that the useful effect of doping depends on keeping vacancies spread out, which happens only within a limited concentration range.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would Lindqvist and colleagues most likely respond to Okafor's proposal?
options: They would agree that creating vacancies through doping is the key to faster ion movement, since adding tantalum raised conductivity in their garnet electrolyte.
They would argue that doping fails to create vacancies at all, since the conductivity of their garnet electrolyte was ultimately determined by the zirconium remaining in the lattice.
They would argue that her reasoning holds only up to a point, since past a certain dopant level the extra vacancies they observed hindered rather than helped lithium movement.
They would argue that solid-state electrolytes should be abandoned in favor of liquid ones, since no doping level they tested raised conductivity to a liquid electrolyte's level.
g.explanation:
정답 C: Okafor는 도펀트가 많을수록 전도도가 계속 높아진다고 주장하지만, Text 2는 일정 농도까지만 증가하고 그 이상에서는 공공(vacancy)이 뭉쳐 리튬 이온을 가둬 전도도가 떨어졌다고 보고한다. 따라서 연구진은 '어느 지점까지만 맞다'고 반응할 것이다.
A: 낮은 농도에서 전도도가 오른 부분만 보고 전면 동의로 답한 경우로, 과도한 도핑이 역효과를 냈다는 핵심 결과를 무시한다.
B: 입장을 거꾸로 뒤집은 경우다. 연구진은 도핑이 공공을 만든다는 점을 부정하지 않았다. 오히려 공공이 너무 많아진 것이 문제였으며, 남은 지르코늄이 전도도를 결정했다는 언급도 없다.
D: 두 텍스트 어디에도 없는 제3의 입장이다. 액체 전해질과의 비교나 고체 전해질을 포기하자는 결론은 지문에 나오지 않는다.
g.explanation_en:
C is correct. Okafor claims that more dopant always means higher conductivity. Lindqvist's team found that conductivity rose only up to a modest dopant level. Past that level, the vacancies clustered and trapped lithium ions, so conductivity fell. They would therefore say her reasoning is valid only within a limited range.
A is wrong because it uses only the early rise in conductivity. It ignores the team's main finding that too much doping backfired.
B is wrong because it flips the team's position. They never said doping fails to create vacancies. Their problem was too many vacancies, and the text never says the remaining zirconium controlled conductivity.
D is wrong because it invents a position that neither text takes. Neither one compares the results to liquid electrolytes or suggests giving up on solid ones.
g.design: Text 1은 도핑 농도와 전도도가 단조 증가한다고 주장하고, Text 2는 최적점이 있다는 결과를 제시해 연구진의 반응을 추론하게 했다. 오답은 각각 한쪽 텍스트만 반영한 경우(A), 입장을 뒤바꾼 경우(B), 어느 텍스트에도 없는 제3의 입장(D)으로 구성했다. 네 선택지는 모두 같은 'They would ..., since ...' 틀로 썼다.

c.instruction: 인물의 행동이나 진술에 표면적으로 드러나지 않는 의도나 태도를 짧은 지문으로 제시하고, 겉으로 말한 것과 실제 상황(또는 결과) 사이의 어긋남으로부터 함의를 추론하게 한다. 오답은 (1) 지문에 명시된 문장을 그대로 가져온 오답, (2) 어긋남을 반대로 해석한 오답, (3) 지문과 무관한 일반적 상식을 답으로 만든 오답으로 구성한다.
c.seed: physical science — Hydration shell formation around dissolved ions and solvation thermodynamic energy contributions

g.passage: In a press interview, physical chemist Lena Okafor described her team's simulations of dissolved ions as "nothing that would surprise a first-year student": water molecules turn their oppositely charged ends toward each ion, forming a hydration shell, and this attraction releases energy. The paper's data, however, tell a more complicated story. For several large ions, the simulations showed that forming the hydration shell absorbed slightly more energy than it released. Dissolution happened only because the breakup of the orderly crystal raised entropy enough to make up the difference. Okafor's team gave this entropy analysis the longest section of the paper, and the paper's final figure sets its results directly beside the energy diagram printed in a widely used introductory chemistry textbook.
g.question: Based on the text, what can most reasonably be inferred about Okafor's remark in the interview?
options: It accurately sums up the paper's central conclusion that water molecules turn toward each ion to form an energy-releasing hydration shell.
It shows that Okafor viewed the entropy findings as a minor detail that the textbook's energy diagram already explains.
It reflects the well-established principle that dissolving any ionic substance in water releases energy into its surroundings.
It understates results that the paper itself presents as a challenge to a standard introductory explanation of why ions dissolve.
g.explanation:
정답 D: Okafor는 인터뷰에서 연구 결과가 "1학년 학생도 놀라지 않을 것"이라고 말했다. 그러나 논문을 보면 일부 큰 이온에서는 수화 껍질이 형성될 때 오히려 에너지가 흡수되었고, 용해는 엔트로피 증가 덕분에 일어났다. 또 논문은 이 엔트로피 분석에 가장 긴 절을 할애했고, 마지막 그림에서 결과를 입문 교과서의 에너지 도표와 바로 나란히 비교했다. 이런 구성은 논문 스스로 교과서 설명에 이의를 제기하고 있음을 보여 준다. 따라서 인터뷰 발언은 결과의 의미를 축소해 말한 것이다.
A(지문 문장 그대로 가져옴): 인터뷰에서 한 말을 그대로 옮겼을 뿐이다. 논문 데이터는 에너지를 방출한다는 그 설명과 어긋나므로 논문의 핵심 결론이라고 볼 수 없다.
B(어긋남을 반대로 해석): 논문은 엔트로피 분석을 가장 길게 다루고 교과서 도표와 직접 대조했다. 따라서 Okafor가 이를 사소한 세부로 여겼다거나 교과서가 이미 설명한다고 보았다는 추론은 근거가 반대 방향을 가리킨다.
C(지문과 무관한 일반 상식): 모든 용해가 에너지를 방출한다는 통념을 답으로 만든 것이다. 지문의 데이터는 오히려 이 통념에 맞는 반례를 제시한다.
g.explanation_en:
Correct answer, D: In the interview, Okafor says her results would not surprise a first-year student. But the paper shows something different. For some large ions, forming the hydration shell actually absorbed energy, and the ions dissolved only because entropy increased. The paper also gives this entropy analysis its longest section, and its final figure puts the results right beside a textbook energy diagram. That setup shows the paper is challenging the textbook explanation. So her interview remark plays down how significant the findings are.
A is wrong because it simply repeats what Okafor said in the interview. The paper's data contradict that energy-releasing account, so it can't be the paper's central conclusion.
B is wrong because it reads the mismatch backward. The paper gives the entropy findings the most space and compares them directly with the textbook. That doesn't suggest Okafor saw them as minor or as already explained by the textbook.
C is wrong because it turns a general belief into the answer. The passage's data actually contradict that belief: in some cases, dissolving absorbed energy.
g.design: The passage sets the chemist's modest interview remark against what the paper actually does: its data contradict the remark, and its structure targets the textbook explanation. Students must infer from that mismatch that she is downplaying her findings. The wrong answers are (1) a lifted quote of her remark, (2) the reverse reading of the mismatch, and (3) a general belief that the passage doesn't support. All four choices use the same "It + verb..." sentence frame.

c.instruction: 지문에 하나의 넓은 주장과 그를 뒷받침하는 좁은 세부사실을 함께 제시하고, 지문 전체의 핵심 요지로 가장 적절한 범위의 진술을 고르게 한다. 오답은 (1) 세부사실 하나만을 전체 요지인 것처럼 과잉축소한 것, (2) 지문이 다루지 않은 범위까지 과잉확장한 것, (3) 넓은 주장과 세부사실을 뒤섞어 범위가 어긋난 것으로 구성한다.
c.seed: physical science — Photodegradation of organic pollutants using semiconductor photocatalyst quantum efficiency measurement

g.passage: Researchers testing semiconductor photocatalysts, such as titanium dioxide particles that break down organic pollutants in water when exposed to light, often compare materials by reporting how much of a dye disappears in a fixed time. Chemist Lena Okafor argues that such comparisons can be misleading unless they are based on quantum efficiency: the number of pollutant molecules degraded per photon actually absorbed by the catalyst. A slurry that scatters much of the incoming light, for example, may appear sluggish simply because fewer photons are absorbed, not because the material is chemically inferior. In Okafor's experiments, two catalysts that differed nearly threefold in dye removal per hour turned out to have almost identical quantum efficiencies once the absorbed light in each reactor was measured with chemical actinometry.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Judging photocatalysts by how quickly they remove pollutants can misrepresent their performance, so their activity should instead be evaluated relative to the light they actually absorb.
When two photocatalysts differ in how quickly they remove dye, the slower one typically scatters more light than it absorbs.
Removal rates are unreliable for comparing any chemical process, so measurements of quantum efficiency should replace them across chemistry.
Photocatalysts that scatter light degrade pollutants more slowly per absorbed photon, which is why quantum efficiency is a better standard than removal rate.
g.explanation:
정답 A: 지문의 넓은 주장(제거 속도 비교는 오해를 낳을 수 있으니 흡수된 광자 기준의 양자효율로 비교해야 한다)을 적절한 범위로 진술하며, 산란 예시와 실험은 이를 뒷받침하는 세부이다.
B(과잉축소·과잉일반화): 산란 예시라는 하나의 세부를 전체 요지로 삼고, 느린 촉매가 '대체로' 산란이 많다는 지문에 없는 일반화까지 한다.
C(과잉확장): 지문은 광촉매 비교만 다루며 화학 전반의 모든 공정으로 확장하지 않는다.
D(범위 혼합·왜곡): 넓은 주장과 세부를 뒤섞으면서, 산란이 흡수 광자당 효율을 낮춘다고 잘못 진술한다. 지문은 산란 때문에 흡수되는 광자 수가 줄어 느려 '보일' 뿐이며, 화학적으로 열등한 것은 아니라고 한다.
g.explanation_en:
A is correct because it states the text's broad claim at the right scope: comparing photocatalysts by how fast they remove pollutants can be misleading, so they should be compared by quantum efficiency, which is measured per absorbed photon. The scattering example and Okafor's experiment are details that support this claim.
B is too narrow. It treats the scattering example as if it were the whole point. It also adds a generalization the text never makes: that slower catalysts usually scatter more light.
C goes too far. The text is only about comparing photocatalysts, not about every chemical process in chemistry.
D mixes the claim with a detail and gets the detail wrong. According to the text, scattering lowers the number of photons absorbed, which makes a catalyst look slow. It does not lower the efficiency per absorbed photon.
g.design: 넓은 주장(양자효율 기준 비교)과 좁은 세부(산란 예시, 3배 차이 실험)를 함께 제시했다. 오답은 과잉축소(B), 과잉확장(C), 범위를 뒤섞으면서 세부를 왜곡한 진술(D)로 구성했다.

c.instruction: 지문에 '한때 ~라고 여겨졌으나(통념)' 다음 'however/but/실제로는' 류의 전환어와 함께 이를 뒤집는 새 증거나 반박 문장을 제시하고, 빈칸이 그 반박된 결과를 표현하도록 한다. 정답은 통념과 정반대 방향의 의미를 가진 어휘로 하고, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 통념 쪽 단어를 그대로 쓴 것, (2) 전환어를 못 읽고 통념과 같은 방향이지만 강도만 다른 단어, (3) 반박 대상과 무관한 제3의 의미 단어로 구성한다. 전환 지점 앞뒤 문장만으로 답이 결정되게 하고 문장 길이나 어휘 난이도는 중간 수준을 유지한다.
c.seed: physical science — Critical angle total internal reflection optical fiber design preventing signal escape loss

g.passage: Early designers of optical fibers assumed that some light would inevitably leak through the sides of a glass strand, and they regarded the thin outer layer, or cladding, as merely protective: the real work of carrying a signal, they believed, depended on the purity of the inner core alone. Later experiments, however, showed that when the cladding's refractive index is set slightly below the core's, light striking the boundary at more than the critical angle is totally reflected back inward rather than escaping. Far from being a minor addition, then, the cladding is ______ to keeping a signal confined over long distances.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: incidental
indispensable
superfluous
decorative
g.explanation:
정답 B(indispensable). 지문은 먼저 클래딩이 '보호용'일 뿐이고 신호 전달은 코어에만 달려 있다는 통념을 제시한다. 이어 'however'로 그 통념을 뒤집는다. 클래딩의 굴절률을 코어보다 약간 낮게 맞추면 임계각을 넘어 경계에 닿은 빛이 전반사되어 빠져나가지 않는다는 것이다. 'Far from being a minor addition'도 빈칸이 통념과 반대 방향, 즉 '필수적'이라는 뜻이어야 함을 확인해 준다.
A(incidental, 부수적인): 반박당한 통념을 그대로 담은 단어다.
C(superfluous, 불필요한): 전환어를 놓쳐 통념과 같은 방향으로 읽고 강도만 더 세게 만든 단어다.
D(decorative, 장식적인): 신호 손실을 막는 기능이라는 논점과 상관없는 제3의 의미다.
g.explanation_en:
The answer is B, indispensable. The text first gives the old belief: the cladding was thought to be merely protective, with signal transmission depending on the core alone. "However" then reverses that belief. When the cladding's refractive index is slightly lower than the core's, light hitting the boundary beyond the critical angle is totally reflected inward instead of escaping. The phrase "Far from being a minor addition" confirms that the blank must mean the opposite of the old view, which is "essential."
A (incidental) simply repeats the old belief that the text rejects.
C (superfluous) ignores the reversal and pushes the old view further in the same direction.
D (decorative) brings in an unrelated idea, appearance, which has nothing to do with stopping signal loss.
g.design: 'However' 앞에는 클래딩이 부차적이라는 통념을, 뒤에는 전반사를 근거로 한 반박을 두었다. 정답은 통념과 정반대인 indispensable로 했다. 오답은 각각 통념 그대로(incidental), 같은 방향에 강도만 센 단어(superfluous), 무관한 의미(decorative)로 구성했다.

c.instruction: 지문에 'is not X, but rather Y' 또는 'it isn't that A; instead B' 형태로 부정어 뒤에 대조 표현이 이어지는 문장을 만들고, 빈칸이 그 대조 표현(B) 자리에 오게 한다. 정답은 부정된 개념(X)과 반대 극성을 가진 어휘로 하고, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 부정어를 무시하고 X와 같은 의미 단어, (2) 부정 구조를 이중으로 잘못 해석해 극성을 다시 뒤집은 단어, (3) 대조 구조와 무관한 유사 발음/철자 단어로 구성한다.
c.seed: physical science — Swelling behavior of clay minerals upon water absorption affecting soil mechanical properties

g.passage: Geotechnical engineers once judged soils mainly by how much weight they could bear. Smectite-rich clays forced a change in that thinking. The danger these clays pose to buildings is not that they stay passive as moisture conditions shift, but rather that they are ______: after rain, water molecules slip between the mineral's stacked sheets and push them apart, swelling the soil enough to lift concrete slabs, and in drought the same soil shrinks back, opening cracks in foundations and walls.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: inert
stable
volatile
voluble
g.explanation: 'not ~ passive, but rather ______' 구조에서 빈칸에는 '수동적·변화 없음'과 반대되는 말이 와야 합니다. 뒤 문장도 점토가 비가 오면 부풀고 가뭄에는 줄어든다고 설명하므로, '급격하고 예측하기 어렵게 변한다'는 뜻의 volatile(C)이 정답입니다. A inert(비활성의)는 부정어를 무시하고 부정된 개념 passive와 같은 뜻의 단어를 고른 경우입니다. B stable(안정적인)은 부정 구조를 이중으로 잘못 읽어 극성을 다시 뒤집은 경우로, 부피가 크게 변한다는 설명과 맞지 않습니다. D voluble(말이 많은)은 volatile과 철자·발음이 비슷할 뿐 사람의 말하는 태도를 가리키는 단어라 점토를 묘사하는 맥락과 관계가 없습니다.
g.explanation_en: The sentence uses the frame "not that they stay passive..., but rather that they are ______," so the blank needs a word that means the opposite of passive and unchanging. The next part confirms this: the clay swells after rain and shrinks in drought. "Volatile" (C) fits, because it means prone to sudden, large changes. "Inert" (A) ignores the negation. It means the same thing as "passive," which is exactly the idea the sentence rejects. "Stable" (B) comes from misreading the negative structure twice and flipping the meaning back. It contradicts the dramatic swelling and shrinking described. "Voluble" (D) only looks and sounds like "volatile." It means talkative, so it has nothing to do with how soil behaves.
g.design: 빈칸을 'is not passive, but rather ___'의 대조 자리에 두었습니다. 정답은 반대 극성인 volatile입니다. 오답은 부정어를 무시한 동의어(inert), 극성을 다시 뒤집은 단어(stable), 철자·발음만 비슷한 단어(voluble)로 구성했습니다.

c.instruction: 지문을 두 단계(예: 상황 묘사 후 화자의 숙고, 또는 기존 주장 소개 후 저자의 반박/선언)로 구성하고, 빈칸을 두 번째 단계의 시작 지점에 배치해 앞 단계와 다른 서술 기능을 하도록 한다. 정답은 두 번째 단계의 기능(숙고, 반박, 선언 등)에 맞는 어휘로 하고, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 첫 번째 단계에 어울리는 단어, (2) 두 단계 어디에도 맞지 않는 중립적 단어, (3) 의미는 비슷하나 문장이 요구하는 품사/기능이 다른 단어로 구성한다.
c.seed: physical science — Electrode potential difference in galvanic cells predicting spontaneous redox reaction direction

g.passage: Introductory chemistry textbooks often present the standard electrode potential difference of a galvanic cell as a straightforward forecast: if the cathode's reduction potential exceeds the anode's, the cell's redox reaction proceeds spontaneously in that direction, and the larger the gap, the more vigorously it runs. Electrochemist Lena Ostrowski ______ this framing, arguing that standard potentials describe only idealized conditions; in real cells, shifts in ion concentration or temperature can shrink or even reverse the potential difference, so the tabulated values indicate a tendency rather than guarantee an outcome.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: endorses
describes
skeptical of
qualifies
g.explanation: 지문은 두 단계로 되어 있다. 앞부분은 교과서의 통념(표준 전위차가 반응 방향을 그대로 예측한다)을 소개하고, 빈칸부터 Ostrowski의 반응이 시작된다. 그녀는 이 틀을 완전히 버리지 않는다. 표준 전위가 '경향'을 나타낸다는 점은 인정하면서, 실제 조건에서는 결과가 달라질 수 있다는 제한을 덧붙인다. 따라서 '조건을 달아 범위를 제한하다'라는 뜻의 qualifies(D)가 정답이다. A의 endorses(지지하다)는 첫 단계의 통념을 그대로 받아들이는 태도에 어울리는 단어라서, 뒤따르는 반론 내용과 맞지 않는다. B의 describes(서술하다)는 중립적인 단어로, 그녀가 이 틀에 대해 평가적인 논증을 펼친다는 점을 담아내지 못한다. C의 skeptical of는 의심한다는 뜻이라 의미상 비슷해 보이지만 형용사구다. 주어 다음에 동사가 와야 하는 자리에 들어갈 수 없고, 'is'가 없어서 문법적으로 성립하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The text has two stages. First it presents the textbook view that a standard potential difference simply predicts which way a reaction will go. Then, starting at the blank, Ostrowski responds. She doesn't throw the framing out. She accepts that standard potentials show a "tendency," but she adds limits: under real conditions, the outcome can change. To qualify a claim means to restrict it with conditions, so "qualifies" (D) is correct. "Endorses" (A) fits the first stage's textbook view, not the counterargument that follows. "Describes" (B) is too neutral and misses the fact that she is evaluating the framing and arguing about it. "Skeptical of" (C) has a similar meaning, but it's an adjective phrase. The sentence needs a verb after the subject, and without "is" the sentence doesn't work grammatically.
g.design: The first stage presents the textbook claim, and the blank opens the second stage, where the author pushes back. The correct answer (qualifies) fits that rebuttal role. The wrong answers are: endorses (fits the first stage), describes (neutral, fits neither stage), and skeptical of (similar meaning, but the wrong part of speech).

c.instruction: 짧은 지문에 '주장→근거→결론' 또는 순서가 있는 2~3개 사건을 넣고, 특정 문장 하나가 전체 흐름에서 어떤 논리적 역할(예: 결론을 예비하는 전환, 앞선 주장을 제한하는 단서)을 하는지 묻는다. 정답은 두 단계 이상을 연결해야 나오도록 만들고, 오답 3개는 각각 '한 단계만 본 역할', '역할을 인접 문장과 혼동', '전체 목적과 개별 문장 기능을 뒤바꾼 것'으로 구성한다.
c.seed: physical science — Thermal shock resistance in ceramics and rapid temperature cycling failure mechanisms analysis

g.passage: Engineers have long ranked ceramics for thermal shock resistance by a single test: heat a sample, plunge it into cold water, and record the temperature difference at which it first cracks. By this measure, dense alumina outperforms many porous ceramics, since its high strength lets it survive larger sudden drops. __Yet a material that survives one severe quench may still fail after hundreds of milder ones, because each cycle can extend microscopic flaws without producing any visible crack.__ Porous ceramics, whose pores blunt the tips of growing cracks, often outlast dense alumina in furnace linings that are heated and cooled daily. For such applications, then, a ranking based on a single quench may point engineers toward precisely the wrong material.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It identifies a limitation of the single-quench test that the following evidence about porous ceramics illustrates and that leads to the text's closing judgment.
It explains why dense alumina performs well in the single-quench test that the text describes in its opening sentences.
It presents evidence that porous ceramics blunt crack tips, a property that allows them to last longer in furnace linings.
It states the text's main purpose, which is to recommend porous ceramics over dense alumina for all high-temperature uses.
g.explanation:
정답 A: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 단일 급랭 시험의 한계(반복 사이클에서 미세 결함 누적)를 제기하고, 이어지는 다공성 세라믹 사례가 이를 구체화하며, 마지막 문장의 결론(단일 급랭 순위는 잘못된 재료를 고르게 할 수 있음)으로 이어진다. 두 단계 이상을 연결해야 하는 역할이다.
B(한 단계만 본 역할): 알루미나가 급랭 시험에 강한 이유는 앞 문장(높은 강도)에서 설명되며, 밑줄 문장은 오히려 그 평가를 제한한다.
C(인접 문장과 혼동): 기공이 균열 끝을 무디게 한다는 근거는 다음 문장의 내용이다.
D(전체 목적과 문장 기능 뒤바꿈/과장): 밑줄 문장은 전체 결론 자체가 아니며, 지문은 '모든' 고온 용도가 아니라 매일 가열·냉각되는 용도에 한정해 말한다.
g.explanation_en:
A is correct. The underlined sentence starts with "Yet" and points out a limitation of the single-quench test: repeated mild cycles can slowly extend flaws even when a sample survives one severe quench. The next sentence about porous ceramics gives a concrete example of this, and the final sentence draws the conclusion that a single-quench ranking can point engineers to the wrong material. To see the sentence's role, you have to connect all three steps.
B is wrong because the reason alumina does well on the test (its high strength) appears in the sentence before. The underlined sentence actually limits how much that result should count.
C is wrong because the evidence that pores blunt crack tips comes in the sentence after the underlined one.
D is wrong because the underlined sentence is not the text's overall conclusion. The text also never recommends porous ceramics for all uses. It only discusses applications like furnace linings that are heated and cooled daily.
g.design: The text runs from the accepted test, to a limitation (the underlined sentence), to evidence, to a conclusion, so the answer only becomes clear when you link the limitation to both the example and the conclusion. Each wrong answer matches one assigned type: B looks at only one step, C swaps in the neighboring sentence's role, and D confuses the whole text's purpose with this one sentence's function.

c.instruction: 두 인물 또는 두 텍스트의 입장을 짧게 제시하고, 한쪽이 다른 쪽의 특정 주장에 대해 보일 반응(동의/반박/보완)을 직접 언급하지 않은 채 추론하도록 묻는다. 정답은 두 입장의 차이를 바탕으로 간접 추론해야 나오게 하고, 오답 3개는 '두 입장을 뒤바꿔 반응을 반대로 서술', '한쪽 입장만 근거로 사용', '텍스트에 없는 새로운 반응을 지어낸 것'으로 만든다.
c.seed: physical science — Diffusion in metals creating Kirkendall void formation at dissimilar alloy interfaces

g.passage: When two different metals are bonded and heated, their atoms migrate across the interface, and they rarely do so at equal rates. In copper–zinc couples, for example, zinc atoms diffuse into copper faster than copper atoms diffuse into zinc, so vacancies pile up on the zinc-rich side and can merge into tiny pores known as Kirkendall voids. Materials engineer Priya Raman treats these voids strictly as defects: in solder joints for electronics, she argues, they concentrate stress and cause cracks, so alloy pairs should be chosen to keep diffusion rates as balanced as possible. Chemist Tomás Ibarra studies the same imbalance for a different purpose. By deliberately heating metal nanoparticles coated with a second element, his team lets the faster-moving core atoms escape outward, leaving behind hollow nanospheres whose large interior surfaces are useful in catalysis. __For Ibarra, then, an unequal diffusion rate is not a mismatch to be engineered away but a parameter to be tuned.__
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It suggests that Ibarra would agree with Raman's recommendation to balance diffusion rates, since hollow nanospheres also form most reliably when atoms migrate evenly.
It implies that Ibarra would reject Raman's recommendation as a general rule, since the very imbalance she seeks to minimize is what his technique depends on.
It indicates that Raman's concern about stress in solder joints is the main reason Ibarra began controlling diffusion in nanoparticles.
It proposes that Raman and Ibarra should collaborate to develop solder joints containing hollow nanospheres that resist cracking.
g.explanation:
정답 B: Raman은 확산 속도 불균형을 결함 원인으로 보고 균형을 맞추라고 권하지만, 밑줄 문장은 Ibarra에게 그 불균형이 '제거할 것'이 아니라 '조절할 변수'임을 밝힌다. 따라서 Ibarra는 Raman의 권고를 보편 원칙으로 받아들이지 않을 것임을 간접적으로 드러낸다.
A(입장 뒤바꿈): Ibarra의 기법은 불균형에 의존하므로 균등 확산에 동의한다는 것은 반대 서술이다.
C(한쪽 입장만 사용): Raman의 응력 우려만 근거로 삼아 Ibarra 연구의 동기를 꾸며냈으며, 지문은 두 연구의 인과관계를 말하지 않는다.
D(새 반응 날조): 협업이나 나노구체 솔더 개발은 지문에 없다.
g.explanation_en:
Correct answer B: Raman sees unequal diffusion rates as a cause of defects and recommends balancing them. The underlined sentence shows that, for Ibarra, the imbalance is a variable to adjust, not something to eliminate. So it indirectly signals that Ibarra would not accept Raman's recommendation as a universal rule, because his hollow nanospheres depend on that imbalance.
A reverses the stances. Ibarra's method requires uneven migration, so he wouldn't endorse even diffusion for his own work.
C relies only on Raman's position to invent a reason for Ibarra's research. The text never links the two lines of work causally.
D makes up a new response. The text says nothing about collaboration or solder joints containing nanospheres.
g.design: Two researchers' views of the same diffusion imbalance are placed side by side. The underlined sentence implies Ibarra's response to Raman's recommendation without stating it directly. The wrong answers are built from a reversal, a one-sided basis, and an invented response, in that order.

c.instruction: 실험 결과나 비용-효과 같은 구체적 근거 하나를 지문에 제시하고, 이 근거가 특정 결론을 뒷받침하는 정확한 논리적 역할(전면 입증/부분 입증/반증/조건부 지지)을 고르게 한다. 정답은 근거의 범위와 결론의 범위가 정확히 일치하는 것으로 하고, 오답 3개는 각각 '근거가 실제보다 넓은 결론을 지지한다고 과장', '근거의 일부만 반영해 좁게 해석', '근거와 결론의 인과 방향을 뒤바꾼 것'으로 만든다.
c.seed: physical science — Surface roughness effect on contact angle measurement and wettability behavior characterization

g.passage: Materials scientists often report a liquid's contact angle—the angle a droplet forms where it meets a solid—as if it were a fixed property of the solid's chemistry. Yet the same chemistry can produce very different angles depending on surface texture. Physicist Lena Okafor and colleagues tested how far texture matters by coating silicon wafers with an identical fluoropolymer and then etching them to different roughness levels. __On the smoothest wafers, water beaded at about 110 degrees, but on wafers etched to the highest roughness, the angle climbed above 150 degrees, even though the coating's chemistry was unchanged across all samples.__ The team cautions that this finding concerns water-repelling coatings specifically; for surfaces whose chemistry attracts water, theory predicts that roughness should instead lower the angle. Still, the researchers argue, any contact angle reported without a description of surface texture cannot be taken as a reliable measure of a coating's chemistry alone.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents a result showing that roughness raises contact angles on every kind of surface, regardless of whether the coating attracts or repels water.
It presents a result showing only that the fluoropolymer coating produced a high contact angle, leaving the role of etching unaddressed.
It presents a result showing that texture alone can substantially alter a measured contact angle, which supports the researchers' warning that unreported texture undermines such measurements.
It presents a result showing that a coating's chemistry determines how rough the wafer becomes during etching, which explains the changes in contact angle.
g.explanation: 정답 C: 밑줄 문장은 화학 조성을 고정하고 거칠기만 바꿨을 때 접촉각이 약 110°에서 150° 이상으로 달라졌다는 결과를 보여 준다. 따라서 질감만으로도 측정값이 크게 바뀔 수 있음을 보여 주며, 마지막 문장의 결론(질감 정보 없이 보고된 접촉각은 화학적 특성의 신뢰할 만한 척도가 아니다)과 범위가 정확히 일치한다. A(과장): 지문은 이 결과가 발수 코팅에만 해당한다고 명시하고, 친수 표면에서는 거칠기가 접촉각을 오히려 낮춘다고 예측하므로 '모든 표면'으로 일반화할 수 없다. B(좁은 해석): 이 문장의 핵심은 매끈한 웨이퍼와 거친 웨이퍼의 비교인데, B는 코팅이 높은 각도를 만들었다는 점만 보고 거칠기의 역할을 빠뜨린다. D(인과 역전): 실험은 거칠기를 독립적으로 조절했고 화학 조성은 고정했다. 화학 조성이 거칠기를 결정한다는 설명은 지문에 없으며 인과 관계를 잘못 설정한 것이다.
g.explanation_en: C is correct. The underlined sentence describes an experiment in which the chemistry stayed fixed and only the roughness changed. The contact angle still rose from about 110 degrees to above 150 degrees. This shows that texture alone can shift the measurement substantially, which is exactly what supports the final claim: a contact angle reported without texture information can't be trusted as a measure of chemistry alone. The scope of the evidence matches the scope of the conclusion. A is wrong because it overstates the result. The text limits the finding to water-repelling coatings and notes that roughness should lower the angle on water-attracting surfaces. B is wrong because it reads the evidence too narrowly. The key point is the comparison between smooth and rough wafers, and B ignores the role of etching. D is wrong because it reverses the cause and effect. The researchers controlled roughness directly while keeping the chemistry constant, and nothing in the text suggests that chemistry determines roughness.
g.design: I gave one controlled experimental result plus explicit limits on its scope (it applies only to water-repelling coatings). The correct answer matches the result's scope to the conclusion exactly. The wrong answers are built on three distinct errors: overstating the result (A), reading it too narrowly (B), and reversing cause and effect (D). All four options share the same sentence frame.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: economics and business — Venetian silk monopoly and guild regulation of luxury textile production fifteenth to seventeenth centuries

g.passage: From the fifteenth to the seventeenth century, Venice's silk guild imposed strict rules on its members: weavers had to use a fixed number of warp threads per cloth, dye only with approved materials, and submit finished pieces to inspectors who stamped those that met the standard. Historians once treated these regulations mainly as tools for shutting out competitors and keeping prices high. Economic historian Luca Molà, however, argues that the rules served a different purpose. Because buyers in distant markets such as Constantinople and Antwerp could not examine every bolt before purchase, the guild's stamp functioned as a guarantee of quality, allowing Venetian silk to command trust—and premium prices—far from the city where it was made. In Molà's view, the restrictions that seem to limit producers actually created the reputation on which their foreign sales depended.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Venetian silk guild regulations mainly kept outside competitors from entering the luxury textile trade, which allowed members to keep prices high.
Venetian silk guild regulations required weavers to follow detailed technical rules, which made production slower and more costly than in rival cities.
Venetian silk guild regulations were enforced most strictly on goods bound for Constantinople and Antwerp, which were the city's most demanding markets.
Venetian silk guild regulations, though they restricted weavers, gave distant buyers a reliable signal of quality that supported the city's export trade.
g.explanation: 지문은 길드 규제를 경쟁 차단 수단으로 보던 기존 견해를 소개한 뒤, 몰라가 이 규제와 검사 도장이 먼 시장의 구매자에게 품질 보증 역할을 하여 수출을 뒷받침했다고 주장한다고 설명하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 지문이 반박하는 과거 역사가들의 견해일 뿐 글의 중심 생각이 아니다. B는 세부 기술 규칙은 맞게 언급하지만 생산이 느려지고 비용이 늘었다는 내용은 지문에 없다. C는 지문에 나온 시장 이름을 쓰지만 그 시장으로 가는 물품에 규제가 더 엄격했다는 내용은 지문에 없다.
g.explanation_en: The text introduces an older view that the guild's rules were meant to shut out competitors, then presents Molà's argument that the rules and inspection stamps assured distant buyers of quality and so supported Venice's export trade, which makes D correct. A just restates the earlier historians' view, which the text sets up in order to challenge it, so it isn't the main idea. B correctly mentions the technical rules, but the text never says they made production slower or more costly. C names markets that appear in the text, but nothing suggests the rules were enforced more strictly for goods headed there.
g.design: Distractor A matches the old view stated in the text, so a reader who skims picks it. B and C reuse real details from the passage but add claims the text doesn't support. To get the answer, the reader has to connect the shift to Molà's view with what the stamp did.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: economics and business — Japanese zaibatsu conglomerate structure and its role in postwar economic recovery and growth

g.passage:
Before World War II, Japan's economy was dominated by zaibatsu, family-controlled conglomerates such as Mitsui and Mitsubishi in which a central holding company owned stakes in banks, trading firms, and manufacturers. After the war, occupation authorities dissolved these holding companies and sold off the families' shares, intending to break up concentrated economic power. Yet many of the former member firms soon regrouped into looser networks known as keiretsu. Instead of answering to a single family, these firms held small amounts of one another's stock and relied on a shared "main bank" for long-term loans.

Some economists have treated the keiretsu simply as the zaibatsu under a new name, but this view overlooks how the changed structure shaped postwar growth. Because no single owner could demand quick returns, and because the main bank monitored borrowers closely and stood ready to rescue them in hard times, keiretsu managers could commit to costly, slow-paying investments in new factories and technology. Such long-horizon investment, made possible by the reorganized networks rather than by the old family-centered model, helped fuel Japan's rapid expansion in the 1950s and 1960s.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Although keiretsu grew out of the dismantled zaibatsu, their distinct ownership and lending arrangements encouraged the patient investment that supported Japan's postwar boom.
Although occupation authorities dissolved the zaibatsu, the same founding families quietly regained control of Japan's largest firms and directed its postwar boom.
Although keiretsu resembled the zaibatsu in name only, their main banks discouraged risky investment and thereby slowed Japan's recovery until the 1960s.
Although economists disagree about the keiretsu, most now conclude that breaking up the zaibatsu was the main reason Japan's economy grew after the war.
g.explanation: 지문은 keiretsu가 해체된 zaibatsu에서 나왔지만 상호 소량 지분과 main bank 구조 덕분에 장기 투자가 가능해져 전후 성장에 기여했다고 주장하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 가문이 통제권을 되찾았다고 하나 지문은 keiretsu가 단일 가문에 응답하지 않았다고 말한다. C는 main bank가 장기 투자를 가능하게 했다는 지문 내용과 정반대이다. D는 경제학자들의 이견을 언급하는 점은 부분적으로 맞지만, 성장의 원인을 해체 자체로 돌리고 지문이 다루지 않는 '대부분의 결론'을 주장한다.
g.explanation_en: The text argues that keiretsu emerged from the dissolved zaibatsu, but their cross-shareholding and main-bank structure allowed long-term investment that fueled postwar growth, so A is correct. B claims the families regained control, yet the text says keiretsu firms did not answer to a single family. C contradicts the text, which says main banks made costly, slow-paying investments possible rather than discouraging them. D correctly notes economists' disagreement but credits the breakup itself for growth and invents a "most economists" consensus the text never states.
g.design: 두 단락(구조 변화 + 성장 메커니즘)을 연결해야 하며, 오답들은 해체·경제학자 이견·main bank 등 지문 요소를 부분 차용해 훑어 읽기를 유도했다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: economics and business — Scottish banking innovation: free banking era and competitive note issue without central authority

g.passage: From 1716 to 1845, Scotland had no central bank and no single authority controlling the supply of paper money. Instead, dozens of private banks issued their own notes, which circulated side by side. Some economists have assumed that such an arrangement would invite reckless overissue, since each bank could profit by printing more notes. Historian Lawrence H. White argues, however, that the Scottish system largely policed itself. Banks routinely accepted one another's notes and then, through a regular note exchange, presented them back to the issuing bank for payment in gold or silver. A bank that issued too many notes therefore quickly found its reserves drained by its rivals, giving every bank a strong incentive to issue cautiously. White points out that Scottish bank failures in this period imposed relatively small losses on noteholders compared with failures in England, where note issue was more tightly restricted.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Although Scottish banks during the free banking era issued notes without central oversight, they frequently overissued them, leading to more failures than occurred in England.

Although Scottish banks during the free banking era faced no central regulator, competition among them, especially the practice of returning rivals' notes for redemption, helped restrain excessive note issue.
Although Scottish banks during the free banking era accepted one another's notes, they did so mainly to drain their rivals' reserves and drive competitors out of business.
Although Scottish banks during the free banking era operated without a central bank, England's tighter restrictions on note issue ultimately proved to be the more stable approach.
g.explanation: 이 지문은 중앙 권한 없이도 경쟁 은행들이 서로의 지폐를 상환 요구하며 과잉 발행을 억제했다는 White의 주장이 핵심이므로 B가 정답이다. A는 '경제학자들의 추정'을 사실로 오인했고, 지문은 오히려 손실이 더 작았다고 말한다. C는 상환 관행이 언급되지만 그 목적을 경쟁자 퇴출로 왜곡했으며, 지문에서 그것은 신중한 발행의 유인으로 제시된다. D는 잉글랜드와의 비교를 거꾸로 해석했는데, 지문은 스코틀랜드의 손실이 더 작았다고 한다.
g.explanation_en: The text's central point is White's argument that, even without a central authority, competition among Scottish banks, especially returning one another's notes for redemption, kept note issue in check, so B is correct. A takes the economists' assumption as fact, but the text says Scottish failures actually caused smaller losses. C mentions the redemption practice but misstates its purpose. In the text, this practice gives banks a reason to issue cautiously, not a way to drive competitors out of business. D reverses the comparison with England: the text says noteholders lost less in Scotland.
g.design: Each option uses the same "Although... free banking era..." frame and refers to real details from the text (overissue, note exchange, comparison with England). Students need to separate White's view from the assumption he rejects and link the note-exchange mechanism to its effect.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

c.seed: economics and business — Hanseatic League merchant practices and standardized contracts for Baltic grain trade networks

g.passage: By the fourteenth century, merchants of the Hanseatic League shipped large quantities of rye and wheat from Baltic ports such as Danzig and Riga to buyers in Flanders and England. Historians once assumed that this trade depended chiefly on personal trust among relatives and close associates, since merchants rarely traveled with their cargo. Economic historian Ulla Brenner argues that a less visible factor mattered more: by the 1380s, contracts used in several Hanseatic towns followed a shared format that fixed how grain would be measured, when payment was due, and which town court would settle disputes. Because these terms no longer had to be negotiated anew for each shipment, Brenner contends, merchants could deal with unfamiliar partners in distant ports almost as confidently as with kin, allowing the grain network to expand well beyond family circles.
g.question: According to the text, what does Brenner claim made it possible for the Baltic grain network to grow?
options: Merchants began accompanying their shipments personally so that they could inspect grain before payment was made.
Merchants relied more heavily on relatives stationed in distant ports to vouch for the honesty of new partners.
Merchants used agreements with uniform terms, which reduced the risk of trading with people they did not know.
Merchants persuaded town courts in Flanders and England to adopt the measurement standards used in Danzig and Riga.
g.explanation: 브레너는 1380년대 여러 한자 도시의 계약이 측정 방식, 지불 시기, 분쟁 관할 법원을 고정한 공통 양식을 따랐고, 이 덕분에 낯선 상대와도 거래할 수 있어 네트워크가 가족 범위를 넘어 확장되었다고 주장하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 상인들이 화물과 함께 거의 이동하지 않았다는 지문 내용과 반대된다. B는 역사가들이 예전에 가정한 '친족 신뢰'를 브레너의 주장으로 혼동한 오답이다. D는 측정·법원이라는 지문 요소를 섞었지만, 플랑드르·영국 법원이 기준을 채택했다는 내용은 지문에 없다.
g.explanation_en: C is correct. Brenner argues that contracts in several Hanseatic towns followed a shared format that fixed measurement, payment timing, and the court for disputes, so merchants could trust unfamiliar partners and the network grew beyond family circles. A contradicts the text, which says merchants rarely traveled with their cargo. B describes the older view that historians held about trust among relatives, not Brenner's claim. D mixes in details from the text (measurement, courts), but the text never says that courts in Flanders or England adopted Baltic standards.
g.design: 정답은 '표준화된 계약→낯선 상대와 거래→확장'의 두 정보 연결로 도출되며, B는 이전 학설, D는 지문 어휘 재조합으로 부분 근거를 갖도록 했다.

c.instruction:

c.seed: economics and business — Argentine beef export industry and refrigerated shipping technology reshaping global meat markets

g.passage: In the mid-nineteenth century, Argentina's vast herds of cattle were valued mainly for their hides and tallow, since fresh meat could not survive the weeks-long voyage across the Atlantic. Much of the beef itself was either salted into a cheap product called tasajo, sold largely to feed enslaved laborers in Brazil and Cuba, or simply discarded. The arrival of refrigerated steamships in the late 1870s and, more decisively, the spread of chilling plants called frigoríficos in the 1880s and 1890s changed this calculation. Once chilled carcasses could reach British ports in edible condition, Argentine ranchers began crossing their herds with Shorthorn and Hereford bulls to produce the tender, fatty meat that British consumers preferred. By the early twentieth century, Argentina had become one of the world's leading beef exporters, and the animal that had once been worth little more than its skin had become the foundation of the nation's export economy.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Argentine cattle ranchers began crossbreeding their herds with British bulls mainly to improve the quality of the hides and tallow they sold abroad.
Argentina's beef industry grew mainly because the market for salted tasajo in Brazil and Cuba expanded rapidly in the late nineteenth century.
Refrigerated steamships allowed Argentina to replace Britain as the world's largest consumer of fresh beef by the early twentieth century.
Refrigeration technology turned Argentine beef from a low-value by-product into a major export, prompting ranchers to reshape their herds for a foreign market.
g.explanation: 지문은 냉장 운송 이전에는 아르헨티나 소가 주로 가죽과 수지 때문에 가치가 있었으나, 냉장선과 냉장 공장 이후 쇠고기가 핵심 수출품이 되었고 목장주들이 영국 시장에 맞게 품종을 개량했다고 설명하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 교배를 언급하지만 목적이 영국 소비자가 선호하는 고기 생산이었지 가죽 품질 향상이 아니었다. B는 타사호를 언급하지만 지문에서 타사호는 값싼 과거 제품일 뿐 산업 성장의 원인이 아니다. C는 냉장선을 언급하지만 아르헨티나는 소비국이 아니라 영국으로 수출한 나라였다.
g.explanation_en: The text explains that before refrigeration, Argentine cattle were valued mainly for hides and tallow, but refrigerated ships and chilling plants turned beef into a leading export, and ranchers crossbred their herds to suit British tastes. That makes D the answer. A does mention crossbreeding, but the text says ranchers did it to produce meat British consumers preferred, not to improve hides. B mentions tasajo, but the text presents it as a cheap older product, not the reason the industry grew. C mentions refrigerated ships, but Argentina exported beef to Britain; it didn't replace Britain as a consumer.
g.design: 각 오답이 지문의 실제 세부(교배, 타사호, 냉장선)를 빌려오되 인과·역할을 뒤틀어, 두 정보(기술→가치 변화→품종 개량)를 연결해야 정답 D를 고를 수 있게 했다.

c.instruction:

c.seed: economics and business — Champagne wine region collective branding and appellation origin protection mechanisms eighteenth century

g.passage: Historians often credit nineteenth-century courts and twentieth-century laws with creating the protected identity of Champagne, but the region's merchants had begun building that identity much earlier. In the 1700s, wine houses in Reims and Épernay faced a practical problem: sparkling wine was costly to make, and bottles shipped to distant buyers could easily be refilled or relabeled by intermediaries. To guard their reputation, local producers lobbied for a 1728 royal decree permitting wine to be transported in bottles rather than barrels, which allowed them to control the product until it reached the customer. They also began marking corks and bottles with house names and the word "Champagne." These steps were driven less by a desire to honor tradition than by commercial calculation: by tying a recognizable name to a guaranteed place of origin, merchants could charge prices that unnamed wines from elsewhere could not command.
g.question: According to the text, what was the primary motivation behind the efforts of eighteenth-century Champagne producers?
options: Producers wanted to secure higher prices by linking their wine's name to its verified source.
Producers wanted to preserve the region's winemaking traditions against outside influence.
Producers wanted to lower shipping costs by moving wine in bottles rather than barrels.
Producers wanted to persuade courts to grant legal protection to the name "Champagne."
g.design: 정답은 마지막 문장의 'commercial calculation…charge prices'를 바꿔 말한 것이고, 오답은 지문에 나오는 전통·병 운송·법원 같은 세부를 동기로 잘못 엮었다.
g.explanation: 지문 마지막 문장에 따르면 생산자들의 노력은 상업적 계산에서 나왔다. 알아볼 수 있는 이름을 보장된 원산지와 묶어 더 높은 가격을 받으려 했다는 것이므로 A가 정답이다. B는 지문이 '전통을 기리려는 욕구보다는'이라고 명시적으로 부정한 내용이다. C의 병 운송은 지문에 나오지만, 목적은 비용 절감이 아니라 고객에게 닿을 때까지 제품을 통제하는 것이었다. D의 법원 보호는 19세기 이후의 일로 언급될 뿐, 18세기 생산자들의 동기로 제시되지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The last sentence says the producers acted out of commercial calculation: by tying a recognizable name to a guaranteed place of origin, they could charge higher prices. That makes A correct. B is wrong because the text directly sets aside honoring tradition as the main driver. C picks up the detail about shipping in bottles, but the text says the goal was to control the product until it reached the customer, not to cut costs. D is wrong because the text links court protection to the nineteenth century and later, not to what drove eighteenth-century producers.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

c.seed: economics and business — Rhodesian tobacco farming and export markets under international sanctions economic adaptation strategies

g.passage: When the United Nations imposed sanctions on Rhodesia in the late 1960s, the country's tobacco growers lost open access to their largest buyers almost overnight. Many observers predicted that the industry would collapse, since tobacco had been the colony's leading export. Instead, production continued for more than a decade. The government created a state agency that bought the entire crop each season at guaranteed prices and then sold it abroad through intermediaries who disguised its origin, often relabeling it as tobacco from neighboring countries. At the same time, the agency paid some farmers to plant maize, cotton, and wheat instead of tobacco, shrinking a surplus that could no longer be sold easily. These measures kept farms operating, but they came at a cost: secret sales typically fetched well below prewar prices, and the industry survived largely because the state absorbed the losses.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Rhodesian tobacco farming collapsed under sanctions because growers could no longer reach their largest buyers abroad.
Rhodesian tobacco farming endured under sanctions through state-managed strategies, though at reduced earnings supported by government spending.
Rhodesian tobacco farming was replaced under sanctions by maize, cotton, and wheat, which became the colony's leading exports.
Rhodesian tobacco farming prospered under sanctions because disguised sales through intermediaries earned higher prices than before.
g.explanation: 지문은 붕괴 예측과 달리 국가 기관의 일괄 매입·원산지 위장 판매·작물 전환으로 산업이 유지되었지만, 낮은 가격과 국가의 손실 부담이라는 대가가 있었다고 말하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 관찰자들의 예측일 뿐 실제로는 생산이 지속되었다. C는 일부 농민의 작물 전환이라는 세부 내용을 과장했으며, 이 작물들이 주요 수출품이 되었다는 언급은 없다. D는 위장 판매라는 사실은 맞지만 가격이 전쟁 전보다 훨씬 낮았다는 진술과 반대된다.
g.explanation_en: The text says that, contrary to predictions of collapse, the industry kept going thanks to a state agency that bought the whole crop, sold it secretly, and paid some farmers to switch crops. It also notes the cost: lower prices and losses covered by the state. B captures both parts, so it is correct. A repeats the observers' prediction, but the text says production actually continued. C stretches a detail about some farmers switching crops, and the text never says those crops became leading exports. D gets the disguised sales right, but the text says those sales earned well below prewar prices, not more.
g.design: To get this right, you have to connect two ideas: the industry survived through adaptation, and that survival came at a cost. Each wrong answer uses a real detail from the text (the prediction, the crop switching, the disguised sales) but twists it, and all four choices use the same sentence frame.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

c.seed: economics and business — Belgian diamond cutting industry clustering in Antwerp and vertical integration of supply chains

g.passage:
For much of the twentieth century, Antwerp dominated the world's diamond trade not because any single firm controlled the business but because thousands of small, specialized firms operated within a few city blocks. Cutters, polishers, brokers, and dealers worked within walking distance of one another, so a rough stone could pass through several independent hands in a single day, and reputations built through repeated face-to-face dealings allowed deals worth millions to be sealed with a handshake. Economists have often cited this arrangement as a textbook example of how geographic clustering can substitute for the coordination that a large, vertically integrated company would otherwise provide internally.

Since the 1990s, however, that model has come under strain. Major mining companies have increasingly sought to control their stones from mine to retail counter, sending rough diamonds directly to their own cutting facilities, many of them in India, where labor costs are lower. As a result, the advantages that Antwerp's dense network once offered have mattered less, and the city's role has shifted toward trading and certification rather than cutting itself.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Antwerp's diamond trade succeeded because its small firms relied on handshake agreements, a practice that economists consider more efficient than formal contracts.
Antwerp's diamond cutters lost business in the 1990s mainly because Indian workshops developed polishing techniques superior to those used in Belgium.

Antwerp's network of nearby specialized firms once performed the coordinating role of a single integrated company, but mining firms' move toward controlling the whole supply chain has weakened that advantage.
Antwerp's diamond industry remains the world's leading center for cutting stones because its dense cluster of firms continues to outcompete vertically integrated companies.
g.design: 두 단락(클러스터가 통합 기업의 조정 기능을 대신함 → 수직 통합으로 그 이점 약화)을 연결해야 정답을 고를 수 있다. 오답은 같은 'Antwerp's ...' 문장 틀로 쓰고, 한 단락만 다루거나 지문에 없는 인과를 끼워 넣었다.
g.explanation: C가 정답이다. 첫 단락에서는 앤트워프에 밀집한 소규모 전문 업체들이 수직 통합 기업이 내부에서 하던 조정 역할을 대신했다고 하고, 둘째 단락에서는 광산 기업들이 공급망 전체를 직접 통제하게 되면서 그 이점이 약해졌다고 한다. C는 이 두 단락을 모두 담고 있다. A는 악수 거래라는 세부 사항만 다루고, 경제학자들이 이를 정식 계약보다 효율적이라고 봤다는 비교는 지문에 없다. B는 인도로 일이 옮겨 간 이유를 우수한 기술 때문이라고 하지만, 지문이 든 이유는 수직 통합과 낮은 인건비이다. D는 앤트워프의 역할이 연마에서 거래·감정 쪽으로 바뀌었다는 둘째 단락 내용과 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: C is correct. In the first paragraph, Antwerp's cluster of small, specialized firms does the coordinating work that a vertically integrated company would normally handle internally. The second paragraph explains that mining companies started controlling their stones from mine to retail, which weakened that advantage. C is the only choice that covers both paragraphs. A focuses only on the handshake detail, and the text never says economists found handshakes more efficient than formal contracts. B claims Indian workshops won business through better techniques, but the text gives vertical integration and lower labor costs as the reasons. D contradicts the second paragraph, which says Antwerp's role has shifted away from cutting toward trading and certification.
