c.seed: economics and business — Colombian coffee federation and geographic indication strategy for specialty bean market positioning

g.passage: In the early 2000s, Colombia's National Federation of Coffee Growers sought legal protection for "Café de Colombia" as a geographic indication, a label reserved for beans grown in specific regions under defined standards. Federation officials argued that the designation would not merely describe where the coffee came from; rather, it would ______ the beans from the cheaper blends that mixed origins, giving roasters and buyers a reliable reason to pay premium prices for certified Colombian lots.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: derive
distinguish
release
remove
g.design: The wrong answers each fit part of the "from" structure (derive from origins, remove from blends, release from competition). To rule them out, students have to connect the "not merely describe" contrast with the goal of getting premium prices.
g.explanation: 지문은 이 표시가 원산지를 '설명하는 것' 이상의 역할을 한다고 말한다. 그 역할은 원산지를 섞은 값싼 블렌드와 구별해 프리미엄 가격의 근거를 주는 것이므로 B가 정답이다. A는 'derive from'이 '~에서 유래하다'라는 뜻이다. 원두가 값싼 블렌드에서 나왔다는 말이 되어 지문의 논리와 반대가 된다. C는 경쟁에서 '풀어준다'는 느낌이 있다. 하지만 표시는 원두를 블렌드로부터 해방시키는 것이 아니라 차별화하는 것이다. D는 원두를 블렌드에서 물리적으로 '빼낸다'는 뜻이다. 그래서 시장에서의 인식을 차별화한다는 의도와 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The passage says the label would do more than describe where the coffee came from. Its job is to set certified beans apart from cheaper mixed-origin blends so buyers have a reason to pay more, which is why B is correct. A, "derive from," means "come from," so it would say the beans originate in the cheap blends. That is the opposite of the passage's logic. C hints at freeing the beans from competition, but the label isn't liberating the beans from blends; it's setting them apart. D means physically taking the beans out of blends, which doesn't fit the goal of making buyers see them differently in the market.

c.instruction:
- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: economics and business — Austrian crystal manufacturer Swarovski and vertical integration from raw materials to retail

g.passage: Many companies buy their materials from one business, have another business make their products, and use stores owned by others to sell them. The Austrian crystal maker Swarovski, founded in 1895, took a different path for much of its history. It controlled nearly every step of its business itself, a strategy called vertical integration. __For example, the company mixed its own glass, designed and ran the machines that cut the crystals, and sold finished pieces in shops that carried its own name.__ By handling each stage, Swarovski could keep close watch on the quality of its crystals from start to finish.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents a problem that Swarovski faced because it relied on other businesses for materials.
It describes the approach most companies use, which the text then contrasts with Swarovski's.
It gives specific cases showing how Swarovski carried out the strategy introduced in the previous sentence.
It explains a result of Swarovski's strategy that the text goes on to question.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 "For example"로 시작해 바로 앞 문장에서 소개한 수직 계열화가 실제로 어떻게 이루어졌는지(유리 제조, 커팅 기계, 자체 매장) 구체적 사례를 든다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 틀렸다. 이 문장은 문제점이 아니라 스와로브스키가 모든 단계를 직접 맡았다는 내용이다. B는 틀렸다. 대부분 회사의 방식은 첫 문장에서 설명되며, 밑줄 문장은 스와로브스키에 관한 것이다. D는 틀렸다. 지문은 이 전략에 의문을 제기하지 않고, 결과(품질 관리)는 마지막 문장에 나온다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence begins with "For example" and lists concrete cases (making its own glass, running its own cutting machines, selling in its own shops) of the vertical integration strategy named in the sentence right before it. So C is correct. A is wrong because the sentence describes no problem; it shows Swarovski doing every step itself instead of relying on others. B is wrong because the first sentence is the one that describes what most companies do, while the underlined sentence is about Swarovski. D is wrong because the text never questions the strategy, and the result (quality control) comes up in the last sentence, not this one.
g.design: "For example"라는 명시적 단서 하나로 앞 문장 개념의 사례 제시 기능을 파악하게 했다. 오답은 같은 "It ..." 문장 틀로 쓰고, 문제 제시·대조·결과 비판처럼 흔한 오개념을 담았다.

c.instruction:
- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: economics and business — Kenyan tea auction system and smallholder farmer participation in commodity price discovery mechanisms

g.passage: Every week in Mombasa, Kenya, buyers gather to bid on tea grown across East Africa. Much of this tea comes from smallholder farmers, who each tend only a small plot of land. Many people assume that such small growers have little say in what their crop is worth. __In fact, because smallholders sell their leaves through factories they jointly own, the prices set at the auction flow back to them as monthly and yearly payments.__ This arrangement links even a farmer with a few hundred tea bushes directly to the price that global buyers are willing to pay.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It describes how buyers at the Mombasa auction decide which tea to bid on each week.
It presents evidence that smallholder farmers grow more tea than large estates do.
It explains why the Mombasa auction meets only once a week rather than every day.
It challenges a common assumption by showing how small growers are connected to auction prices.
g.explanation: 바로 앞 문장은 소규모 농민이 작물 가격에 거의 영향력이 없다는 흔한 가정을 제시하고, 밑줄 문장은 "In fact"로 시작해 공동 소유 공장을 통해 경매 가격이 농민에게 돌아온다고 설명하며 그 가정을 반박한다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 구매자의 입찰 결정 방식을 다루지 않으므로 틀리다. B는 소농과 대농장의 생산량 비교가 지문에 없으므로 틀리다. C는 경매가 주 1회 열리는 이유를 설명하지 않으므로 틀리다.
g.explanation_en: The sentence before the underlined one states a common assumption: small growers have little say in what their crop is worth. The underlined sentence begins with "In fact" and explains that auction prices flow back to smallholders through factories they jointly own, which pushes back on that assumption. So D is correct. A is wrong because the sentence doesn't explain how buyers choose which tea to bid on. B is wrong because the text never compares how much tea smallholders and large estates produce. C is wrong because the sentence doesn't explain why the auction is held weekly.
g.design: This item relies on one explicit cue: "In fact" right after a stated assumption marks a counterclaim. The wrong answers mention real details from the passage (buyers, smallholders, weekly auction) and are written in the same sentence pattern as the correct answer.

c.instruction:
- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: economics and business — Dominican cocoa farmer networks and supply chain transparency initiatives for direct roasters

g.passage: For years, small cocoa farmers in the Dominican Republic sold their beans to middlemen who mixed harvests from many farms, so buyers rarely knew where any single bag came from. Recently, several farmer cooperatives have begun recording each farm's harvest dates, fermentation methods, and prices paid, then sharing those records directly with small chocolate makers abroad. __For example, one cooperative in the province of Duarte now gives each sack a code that lets a roaster in Oregon look up the exact family farm that grew the beans.__ Supporters say this kind of transparency helps farmers earn higher prices for carefully grown cocoa.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It gives a specific instance of the record-sharing practice described in the previous sentence.
It gives a specific reason why middlemen mixed harvests from many farms in the past.
It gives a specific objection to the claim that transparency helps farmers earn more.
It gives a specific conclusion that summarizes the overall argument of the text.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 "For example"로 시작하며, 앞 문장에서 설명한 협동조합의 기록 공유 관행을 Duarte 협동조합의 자루 코드라는 구체적 사례로 보여 준다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 틀렸다. 밑줄 문장은 과거에 중개상이 수확물을 섞은 이유를 설명하지 않는다. C는 틀렸다. 이 문장은 투명성의 이점을 반박하지 않고 오히려 뒷받침한다. D는 틀렸다. 이 문장은 결론이 아니며, 주장을 요약하는 역할은 마지막 문장에 가깝다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence begins with "For example." It shows the record-sharing practice described in the sentence before it through one concrete case: a cooperative in Duarte that puts a code on each sack. That makes A the correct answer. B is wrong because the sentence doesn't explain why middlemen used to mix harvests. C is wrong because the sentence supports the benefits of transparency instead of arguing against them. D is wrong because the sentence isn't a conclusion; the last sentence comes closer to summing up the text.
g.design: "For example"라는 명시적 단서 하나로 예시 기능을 알아보게 해 easy 난이도를 유지했다. 오답은 원인, 반론, 결론처럼 흔히 헷갈리는 기능으로 만들고, 네 선택지 모두 같은 문장 틀을 쓰게 했다.

c.instruction: 문장이 분사구문(-ing/-ed로 시작)이나 비교구문(Unlike/Like/As)으로 시작하고, 그 뒤에 콤마와 함께 주절이 이어지는 문법 문제를 만들어라. 정답은 수식어구가 의미적으로 가리키는 대상과 정확히 일치하는 주절 주어를 가져야 하며, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 수식어와 무관한 엉뚱한 명사를 주어로 둔 경우, (2) 수식 대상과 비슷하지만 다른 범주의 명사(예: 사람 대신 그 사람의 저작물)를 주어로 둔 경우, (3) 수일치는 맞지만 의미상 수식어가 가리킬 수 없는 대상을 주어로 둔 경우로 구성하라. 정답과 오답 모두 문법적으로는 완전한 문장이 되도록 만들어 순수하게 의미적 연결 판단만으로 정답을 가려내게 하라.
c.seed: economics and business — Tamil Nadu textile cluster and subcontracting networks in southern India manufacturing belt

g.passage: In the southern Indian city of Tiruppur, often called the knitwear capital of Tamil Nadu, few firms handle every stage of production under one roof. Instead, work moves among hundreds of specialized workshops. Relying on dense networks of small subcontractors for dyeing, printing, and stitching, ______ able to fill large overseas orders far faster than a single vertically integrated factory could.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: Tiruppur's knitwear exports are
Tiruppur's garment exporters are
the subcontracting networks themselves are
European fashion retailers are
g.explanation:
정답 B. 분사구 "Relying on dense networks of small subcontractors..."의 의미상 주어는 하청 네트워크에 의존해 주문을 처리하는 행위자여야 하므로 '의류 수출업체(exporters)'가 맞다. 
A: 수출업체 대신 그들의 산출물인 '수출품(exports)'을 주어로 둔 범주 혼동. 상품은 하청업체에 의존하거나 주문을 처리할 수 없다. 
C: 복수형이라 are와 수일치는 맞지만, 네트워크가 '하청업체 네트워크에 의존한다'는 것은 자기 자신에 의존하는 셈이 되어 논리적으로 맞지 않는다. 
D: 유럽 소매업체는 주문을 하는 쪽이지 Tiruppur의 하청업체에 의존해 주문을 처리하는 주체가 아니다. 문맥과 무관한 명사다.
g.explanation_en:
B is correct. The introductory phrase "Relying on dense networks of small subcontractors..." needs a subject that can actually do the relying and fill the orders. That subject is the garment exporters, so B gives the modifier the right subject.
A is wrong because it uses the exporters' product, their exports, instead of the exporters. Products can't rely on subcontractors or fill orders.
C is wrong even though "networks are" agrees in number. The networks can't be the ones relying on networks of subcontractors, because that would mean they rely on themselves.
D is wrong because European retailers place the orders. They aren't the ones who use Tiruppur's subcontractors to fill them.
g.design: This item opens with a participial phrase. All four choices follow the same "noun phrase + are" pattern and form complete sentences. The wrong answers use (1) an unrelated noun (retailers), (2) a related noun in a different category (exports instead of exporters), and (3) a noun that agrees in number but can't logically be the subject (networks).

c.instruction: 완전한 독립절 두 개가 이어지는 문장을 만들되, 두 절 사이의 논리적 관계(대조, 인과, 부연설명 중 하나)를 분명히 드러내라. 정답은 그 관계에 어울리는 구두점 전략(등위접속사+쉼표, 세미콜론, 또는 마침표) 하나이며, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 구두점 종류는 맞지만 절 관계와 안 맞는 접속사를 쓴 경우, (2) 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이은 콤마 스플라이스, (3) 절 경계가 아닌 곳에 세미콜론을 넣어 절을 어색하게 쪼갠 경우로 만들어라. 정답 선택 시 단순히 구두점 유무가 아니라 절 간 의미 관계까지 고려해야 정답을 고를 수 있도록 하라.
c.seed: economics and business — Croatian shipbuilding industry government subsidies and maritime employment concentration regional economy

g.passage: For decades, the Croatian government poured subsidies into shipyards such as Uljanik in Pula and 3. Maj in Rijeka, hoping to protect the thousands of maritime jobs concentrated in a few Adriatic port towns. The payments kept the yards operating through repeated financial ______ to make the yards competitive with lower-cost builders in Asia, and several of them collapsed into bankruptcy once European Union rules limited further state aid.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: crises, so they did little
crises, they did little
crises, but they did little
crises but they did; little
g.explanation:
빈칸 앞 "The payments kept the yards operating through repeated financial crises"와 뒤 "they did little to make the yards competitive..."는 둘 다 독립절이다. 앞 절은 보조금 덕분에 조선소가 계속 돌아갔다는 성과이고, 뒤 절은 경쟁력은 거의 높이지 못했다는 한계이므로 둘은 대조 관계다. 따라서 쉼표와 등위접속사 but을 쓴 C가 정답이다.
A: 쉼표+등위접속사라는 구두점 형식은 맞다. 하지만 so는 인과를 나타내므로 '조선소를 유지시켰기 때문에 경쟁력을 높이지 못했다'는 뜻이 되어 논리가 맞지 않는다.
B: 독립절 두 개를 쉼표만으로 이었으므로 콤마 스플라이스다.
D: 세미콜론이 절 경계가 아니라 "did"와 목적어 "little" 사이에 들어가 동사와 목적어를 갈라 놓는다. 또 세미콜론 뒤 "little to make..."는 독립절이 아니다.
g.explanation_en:
The text before the blank ("The payments kept the yards operating through repeated financial crises") and the text after it ("they did little to make the yards competitive...") are both independent clauses. The first clause gives what the subsidies achieved: they kept the yards running. The second gives their limit: they barely made the yards more competitive. That's a contrast, so the best way to join the clauses is a comma plus "but," which is choice C.
A: The comma plus a coordinating conjunction is the right punctuation, but "so" signals cause and effect. It would mean the yards failed to become competitive *because* the subsidies kept them running, and that's not the logic of the text.
B: This joins two independent clauses with only a comma, so it's a comma splice.
D: The semicolon doesn't fall at the boundary between the clauses. Instead, it splits the verb "did" from its object "little," and what follows the semicolon isn't an independent clause.
g.design: The answer depends on seeing the contrast between the two clauses (the subsidies kept the yards running, but they barely improved competitiveness). The wrong choices are a mismatched conjunction (so), a comma splice, and a semicolon placed where there's no clause boundary.

c.instruction: 짧은 부사적 삽입어구(however, for example, in fact 등)가 문장 중간에 등장하되, 이것이 두 독립절 사이에 낀 것인지 아니면 한 절 내부의 단순 삽입인지 헷갈리게 설계하라. 정답은 실제 절 구조(삽입어 앞뒤가 독립절인지 아닌지)에 맞는 구두점이며, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 삽입어를 절 경계로 착각해 불필요하게 세미콜론/마침표를 쓴 경우, (2) 실제 절 경계인데 쉼표만 찍어 콤마 스플라이스를 만든 경우, (3) 삽입어 앞뒤 쉼표를 하나만 찍어 비대칭으로 만든 경우로 구성하라. 문장을 읽고 삽입어 앞뒤가 각각 완전한 절인지 아닌지를 판별해야만 정답을 고를 수 있게 하라.
c.seed: economics and business — Estonian e-commerce platform Wise and cross-border payment system disrupting traditional banking fees

g.passage: Founded in 2011 by two Estonian entrepreneurs, the money-transfer company Wise undercut traditional banks by avoiding the international wire networks that banks rely on. When a customer in Germany sends euros to a relative in Mexico, the euros remain in Wise's German account______ pesos are paid out to the relative from a reserve that Wise already holds in Mexico.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , in effect,
; in effect
; in effect;
; in effect,
g.explanation:
정답 D. 빈칸 앞 "the euros remain in Wise's German account"와 뒤 "pesos are paid out ... in Mexico"는 각각 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 따라서 두 절 사이에 경계(세미콜론)가 필요하고, 삽입어 "in effect"는 뒤 절을 이끄는 도입어이므로 그 뒤에 쉼표를 둔다. "; in effect,"가 맞다.
A: 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어서 콤마 스플라이스가 된다. "in effect"를 단순 삽입어로 보고 양쪽에 쉼표를 찍으면 맞다고 착각하기 쉽지만, 앞뒤가 모두 완전한 절이다.
B: 세미콜론으로 경계는 맞게 두었지만, 도입어 "in effect" 뒤에 쉼표가 없어 삽입어와 절이 구분되지 않는다(삽입어 구두점 비대칭).
C: 삽입어 자체를 또 하나의 절 경계로 오인해 뒤에 불필요한 세미콜론을 넣었다. 세미콜론 뒤의 "in effect"는 혼자서 독립절이 될 수 없다.
g.explanation_en:
The answer is D. "The euros remain in Wise's German account" is an independent clause, and so is "pesos are paid out to the relative from a reserve that Wise already holds in Mexico." Two independent clauses need a strong boundary, such as a semicolon. "In effect" is an introductory phrase that belongs to the second clause, so it should be followed by a comma: "; in effect,".
A is wrong because it joins two independent clauses with only commas, which creates a comma splice. It can look correct if you read "in effect" as a simple interruption inside a single clause, but the words on both sides of it are complete clauses.
B is wrong because it places the semicolon correctly but leaves out the comma after the introductory phrase "in effect," so the punctuation around the phrase is unbalanced.
C is wrong because it treats the phrase itself as a clause boundary and adds a second semicolon. "In effect" can't stand alone as an independent clause, so that second semicolon is unnecessary.
g.design: "in effect"는 겉보기에 한 절 안의 단순 삽입어처럼 보이지만, 실제로는 두 독립절 사이에 놓여 있다. 그래서 앞뒤가 각각 완전한 절인지 따져 봐야만 고를 수 있다. 오답은 콤마 스플라이스, 삽입어 뒤 쉼표 누락(비대칭), 삽입어를 절 경계로 오인한 불필요한 세미콜론으로 구성했다.

c.instruction: 노트에 제시된 서로 다른 두 개의 사실(예: 각각 다른 대상/사건/수치에 대한 독립된 정보)을 하나의 문장으로 자연스럽게 결합하여 주어진 목표(예: 두 대상을 비교하거나 관계를 설명)를 달성하는 문제를 만들어라. 오답은 각각 (1) 한쪽 사실만 담아 목표를 절반만 달성, (2) 두 사실을 결합했지만 목표와 무관한 조합, (3) 노트에 없는 내용을 추가해 사실을 왜곡한 문장으로 구성하라.
c.seed: economics and business — Tanzanian cashew nut processing and value-added production shifting from raw export dependency

g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Tanzania is one of Africa's largest producers of raw cashew nuts.
- In the 2017–2018 season, Tanzania exported most of its cashew harvest unprocessed, largely to India and Vietnam for shelling.
- In that season, only about 10 percent of Tanzania's cashew crop was processed domestically.
- Processing cashews (shelling, peeling, and grading kernels) can multiply the export value of each ton several times over.
- The Tanzanian government has announced a target of processing 60 percent of the national cashew crop within the country by 2025.
g.question: The student wants to emphasize how far Tanzania's cashew industry would need to change to meet its stated ambition. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Although only about 10 percent of Tanzania's cashew crop was processed domestically in the 2017–2018 season, the government aims to process 60 percent of it within the country by 2025.
Tanzania, one of Africa's largest producers of raw cashew nuts, has set a goal of processing 60 percent of its national cashew crop domestically by 2025.
Although Tanzania is one of Africa's largest producers of raw cashew nuts, it sent most of its 2017–2018 harvest unprocessed to India and Vietnam for shelling.
Although only about 10 percent of Tanzania's cashew crop was processed domestically in the 2017–2018 season, a government ban on raw exports is expected to raise that share to 60 percent by 2025.
g.explanation:
정답 A: 목표는 야심(목표치)과 현재 상황 사이의 격차를 강조하는 것이다. A는 2017–2018년 국내 가공률 약 10%와 2025년 목표 60%라는 서로 다른 두 사실을 하나로 묶어 격차를 직접 보여 준다.
B: 60% 목표만 담고 출발점이 되는 현재 가공률이 없다. 그래서 얼마나 바뀌어야 하는지 알 수 없어 목표의 절반만 달성한다.
C: 두 사실(주요 생산국이라는 점, 원물 수출)을 결합했지만 정부 목표를 언급하지 않아 '야심'과의 격차라는 목표와 관련이 없다.
D: 10%와 60%는 노트와 맞지만, 노트에 없는 '원물 수출 금지'를 추가하고 목표를 예상 결과처럼 바꿔 사실을 왜곡한다.
g.explanation_en:
Choice A is correct. The goal is to show how big the gap is between where the industry stands now and what Tanzania is aiming for. Choice A puts two separate facts side by side: only about 10 percent of the crop was processed at home in 2017–2018, and the target is 60 percent by 2025. Seeing both numbers together makes the size of the change clear.
Choice B gives only the 60 percent target. Without the starting point, you can't tell how much has to change, so it only does half the job.
Choice C combines two facts from the notes (Tanzania is a major producer, and it exports most of its cashews raw), but it never mentions the government's target. Without the target, there is no ambition to compare against.
Choice D adds a ban on raw exports, which does not appear in the notes. It also presents the target as an expected outcome, which changes what the notes actually say.
g.design: This item asks the student to combine two independent facts, the current rate and the target, to show a gap. Each wrong answer matches one assigned pattern: B states only one fact, C combines two facts that don't serve the goal, and D adds information not in the notes. All four choices use similar sentence frames, and the question avoids key words from the correct answer.

c.instruction: 학생이 주어진 하나의 수사적 목표(강조하기, 개관하기, 소개하기 중 하나)를 달성하기 위해 노트의 여러 항목 중 어느 것을 포함해야 하는지 판단하는 문제를 만들어라. 오답은 각각 (1) 목표보다 지나치게 세부적인 정보만 담은 문장, (2) 목표보다 지나치게 포괄적이라 초점을 잃은 문장, (3) 목표와 무관한 다른 항목을 강조한 문장으로 구성하라.
c.seed: economics and business — Hanseatic League's standardized wool and linen grading systems enabling quality assurance in Northern European trade

g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Hanseatic League was a network of merchant guilds and towns that dominated trade in Northern Europe from the 1200s to the 1600s.
- In Hanseatic trading centers such as Bruges and London, sworn inspectors examined bolts of cloth before the cloth could be sold.
- Inspectors checked each bolt's length, weave density, and dye, then attached a lead seal marking its grade.
- A seal from a recognized town let a buyer in a distant port judge a cloth's quality without unrolling and examining it.
- Cloth that failed inspection could be cut up or burned, and the weaver could be fined.
- The League also negotiated trading privileges, such as reduced tolls, with foreign rulers.
g.question: The student wants to emphasize why the League's grading practice mattered to merchants trading across long distances. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Hanseatic inspectors measured each bolt's length, weave density, and dye before attaching a lead seal that marked its grade.
Because a recognized town's seal certified a bolt's grade, a buyer in a faraway port could trust the cloth's quality without having to unroll and examine it.
From the 1200s to the 1600s, the Hanseatic League, a network of guilds and towns, dominated Northern European trade through cloth inspection, trading privileges, and other practices.
In addition to inspecting cloth, the Hanseatic League gained trading privileges, such as reduced tolls, from foreign rulers, which made long-distance trade cheaper for its merchants.
g.explanation:
정답 B: 목표는 등급 판정 관행이 원거리 상인에게 왜 중요했는지 강조하는 것이다. B는 봉인이 품질을 보증했다는 점과, 그 덕분에 멀리 있는 구매자가 직접 펼쳐 보지 않고도 품질을 믿을 수 있었다는 결과를 함께 제시하므로 '왜 중요했는가'에 답한다.
A(지나치게 세부적): 검사 절차만 자세히 설명할 뿐, 그 관행이 원거리 거래에 왜 중요했는지는 말하지 않는다.
C(지나치게 포괄적): 동맹 전체를 개관하며 등급 판정을 여러 관행 중 하나로만 언급해 초점이 흐려진다.
D(다른 항목 강조): 원거리 교역을 언급해 그럴듯하지만, 등급 판정이 아니라 통행세 감면이라는 다른 관행의 이점을 강조한다.
g.explanation_en:
Correct answer B: Your goal is to emphasize why the grading practice mattered to long-distance merchants. B links the seal, which certified a bolt's grade, to the payoff: a buyer in a faraway port could trust the cloth's quality without examining it. That answers the "why it mattered" part.
A (too detailed): It lays out the inspection steps but never explains why the practice mattered for long-distance trade.
C (too broad): It gives an overview of the whole League and mentions cloth inspection only as one practice in a list, so the focus is lost.
D (wrong item): It mentions long-distance trade, which sounds relevant, but it emphasizes a different practice, toll privileges, instead of the grading system.
g.design: Rhetorical goal is "emphasize significance." Each distractor fails in its own way: A gives only procedural detail, C is a broad overview, and D picks the wrong note (privileges) while borrowing "long-distance" wording. All options share the same declarative sentence frame, and the question avoids the key words of the answer (seal, trust, unroll).

c.instruction: 노트에 연구 결과를 설명하는 확정적 진술과 통계적/잠정적 진술이 함께 제시된 상황에서, 주어진 목표에 맞는 확실성 수준의 문장을 선택하는 문제를 만들어라. 오답은 각각 (1) 잠정적 결과를 확정적으로 과장한 문장, (2) 확정적 사실을 불필요하게 잠정적으로 축소한 문장, (3) 확실성 수준은 맞지만 다른 연구 내용과 혼동한 문장으로 구성하라.
c.seed: economics and business — Venetian glass monopoly on Murano Island and guild restrictions preventing artisan knowledge emigration fifteenth century

g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- In 1291, Venice ordered its glass furnaces moved to the island of Murano.
- Venetian law barred Murano glassmakers from leaving the republic without permission; archival records show that the punishment for leaving could include seizure of the artisan's property.
- Historian Francesca Trivellato examined guild records from the fifteenth century.
- Her analysis suggests that fewer than one in ten trained Murano glassmakers left Venice during that century, though she cautions that the records are incomplete.
- A separate study by economist Paolo Rossi estimates that Murano glass made up roughly a quarter of Venice's luxury exports by value around 1500.
g.question: The student wants to present Trivellato's finding about artisan departures while accurately reflecting how strongly the evidence supports it. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Trivellato's analysis of guild records proves that fewer than one in ten trained Murano glassmakers left Venice in the fifteenth century, showing that the republic's restrictions fully stopped the emigration of artisan knowledge.

Trivellato's analysis of guild records indicates that Venetian law may possibly have discouraged glassmakers from leaving, since the punishment for leaving could perhaps have included the seizure of an artisan's property.

Trivellato's analysis of incomplete guild records indicates that fewer than one in ten trained Murano glassmakers likely left Venice in the fifteenth century, despite the incentives that skilled artisans had to seek work abroad.
Trivellato's analysis of incomplete guild records suggests that Murano glass likely made up roughly a quarter of Venice's luxury exports by value around 1500.
g.explanation:
정답 C: Trivellato의 결과(10명 중 1명 미만 이주)를 제시하면서 기록이 불완전하다는 점과 'likely'로 잠정성을 정확히 반영한다. 덧붙인 '해외로 나갈 유인' 구절은 결과를 확정하지 않고 맥락만 더한다.
A: 잠정적 결과를 'proves'와 'fully stopped'로 과장했다. 노트에서는 학자 본인이 기록이 불완전하다고 경고한다.
B: 법적 금지와 재산 몰수 처벌은 기록으로 확인된 확정적 사실인데 'may possibly', 'perhaps'로 불필요하게 약화했다. 또 이주에 관한 결과도 제시하지 않는다.
D: 확실성 수준은 적절해 보이지만, 수출 비중 추정치는 Rossi의 별도 연구에서 나온 것이다. 이를 Trivellato의 연구로 잘못 돌렸다.
g.explanation_en:
Correct answer C: It presents Trivellato's finding (fewer than one in ten glassmakers left), and it reflects her caution in two ways: it mentions that the records are incomplete, and it uses "likely." The extra phrase about incentives to work abroad only adds context and doesn't claim the finding is certain.
A: It overstates a tentative result by using "proves" and "fully stopped," even though the historian herself warns that the records are incomplete.
B: The legal ban and the property-seizure penalty are facts confirmed by archival records, yet this choice weakens them with "may possibly" and "perhaps." It also never presents the finding about departures.
D: Its hedged tone looks appropriate, but the export-share estimate comes from Rossi's separate study, not from Trivellato's work.
g.design: 노트에서 확정적 사실(법·처벌)과 잠정적 추정(이주 비율)을 함께 제시했다. 오답 셋은 각각 과장, 불필요한 약화, 다른 연구와의 혼동에 해당하고, 모두 정답과 같은 'Trivellato's analysis...' 문장 틀을 쓴다. 질문에는 'likely'나 'incomplete' 같은 핵심어를 넣지 않았다.

c.instruction: 학술적 소재(연구, 인물, 현상 등)에 대한 3~4문장의 짧은 지문을 만들고, 마지막 문장은 앞 내용 중 특정 목적이나 강조점(예: 결과가 아니라 의도, 수치가 아니라 방향성)에 부합하는 전환어를 골라야 정답이 되게 하라. 오답 3개는 (1)앞 문장의 결과·부수적 사실과는 맞지만 지문의 핵심 강조점과는 어긋나는 전환어, (2)방향은 맞지만 논리관계(원인/대조 등)가 틀린 전환어, (3)전혀 다른 내용과 연결되는 전환어로 구성하라. 지문에 여러 개의 정보가 나열되되 그중 한 가지만 답과 직결되도록 설계한다.
c.seed: economics and business — English East India Company's monopoly charter and private military enforcement of trade routes seventeenth century

g.passage: In 1600, Queen Elizabeth I granted the English East India Company a charter giving it exclusive rights to English trade east of the Cape of Good Hope. Later charters went further, allowing the company to build forts, raise troops, and make war on rival powers in Asia. Historians note, however, that the directors in London saw these military powers narrowly: armed ships and garrisons were meant less to seize territory than to keep rival European merchants and unlicensed English "interlopers" off the routes the charter reserved. ______ the company's fortified posts at Madras and Bombay were located and staffed mainly as guarded harbors and warehouses, not as launching points for conquest inland.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: As its territory expanded,
Even so,
In terms of profits,
In keeping with this aim,
g.explanation:
정답 D: 셋째 문장의 핵심은 군사력의 '목적'이다. 영토 장악이 아니라 독점 항로를 지키는 것이었다는 점이다. 마지막 문장은 요새가 정복 거점이 아니라 경비가 딸린 항구와 창고로 운영되었다고 말하므로, 바로 그 목적에 들어맞는 사례이다. 따라서 '이 목적에 따라'라는 뜻의 전환어가 자연스럽다.
A: 요새 건설권과 전쟁 수행권이라는 부수적 사실만 보면 영토 확장을 떠올리기 쉽다. 하지만 지문은 영토 장악을 분명히 부정하고, 마지막 문장도 내륙 정복을 부정한다.
B: 마지막 문장이 앞 내용과 같은 방향의 근거인데도 대조 관계로 연결하므로 논리 관계가 틀렸다.
C: 지문에는 수익에 관한 내용이 없어서 전혀 다른 화제로 연결된다.
g.explanation_en:
Why D is correct: The third sentence is about the purpose of the company's military power. Its armed force was meant to guard the trade routes reserved by the charter, not to seize territory. The last sentence describes the forts at Madras and Bombay as guarded harbors and warehouses, not bases for inland conquest. That example fits the stated goal, so "In keeping with this aim" is the logical link.
Why A is wrong: The company's right to build forts and wage war might suggest expansion. But the passage rejects territorial seizure, and the last sentence rules out inland conquest.
Why B is wrong: "Even so" signals a contrast. The last sentence actually supports the previous point, so the relationship is wrong.
Why C is wrong: The passage never talks about profits, so this transition jumps to an unrelated topic.
g.design: This passage contains several facts: the charter, the war powers, and the purpose those powers served. Only the purpose (guarding the routes, not conquest) points to the answer. The wrong choices are (1) A, which matches the incidental fact about forts and war powers but contradicts the main point, (2) B, which signals contrast even though the last sentence supports the point before it, and (3) C, which links to an unrelated topic.

c.instruction: 서로 배치되거나 상반된 것처럼 보이는 두 가지 관찰(실험 결과, 사례, 수치)이 제시된 짧은 지문을 만들고, 두 관찰을 종합했을 때 나오는 결론을 마지막 문장에서 올바른 전환어로 연결해야 정답이 되게 하라. 오답 3개는 (1)한쪽 관찰만 반영한 전환어, (2)두 관찰이 상반된다는 점만 보고 단순 대조로 처리한 전환어, (3)종합 결론과 무관한 전환어로 구성하라. 계산이나 복잡한 수치 없이 정성적 진술만으로 구성한다.
c.seed: economics and business — Japanese silk industry cocoon standardization and cooperative marketing defeating Italian competition early twentieth century

g.passage: In the early 1900s, inspectors at American silk mills routinely judged the best Italian raw silk to be finer and more lustrous, skein for skein, than anything arriving from Japan. Yet over the same decades, those mills shifted their purchases decisively toward Japanese silk, which Japanese cooperatives had begun sorting by standardized cocoon grades so that every bale of a given grade matched the others closely. ______ the factor that won American buyers was evidently not the excellence of any single skein but the assurance that thread from one shipment would run on high-speed power looms just like thread from the last.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Taken together,
Nevertheless,
In other words,
Similarly,
g.explanation:
정답 A: 지문은 서로 어긋나 보이는 두 관찰을 제시한다. 하나는 이탈리아산 실이 타래 하나하나로 보면 품질이 더 높았다는 것이고, 다른 하나는 그런데도 미국 공장들이 표준화된 일본산 실로 구매를 옮겼다는 것이다. 마지막 문장은 두 관찰을 합쳐 얻는 결론이다. 구매자가 중시한 것은 최고 품질이 아니라 균일성이었다는 것이므로 종합을 나타내는 'Taken together,'가 알맞다.
B 오답: 'Nevertheless'는 두 관찰이 상반된다는 점만 보고 단순 대조로 처리한 것이다. 마지막 문장은 둘째 관찰과 대립하지 않는다. 오히려 두 관찰의 긴장을 풀어 주는 설명이다.
C 오답: 'In other words'는 둘째 관찰(표준화된 등급)만 다시 말하는 것으로 본 선택이다. 첫째 관찰(이탈리아산이 더 우수함)과 대비해야 나오는 'not the excellence of any single skein'이라는 부분을 반영하지 못한다.
D 오답: 'Similarly'는 앞 내용과 비슷한 다른 사례를 덧붙일 때 쓴다. 마지막 문장은 새로운 유사 사례가 아니라 결론이므로 맥락과 관계없다.
g.explanation_en:
Correct answer A: The passage gives two observations that seem to clash. First, inspectors judged Italian silk finer, skein for skein. Second, American mills still shifted toward Japanese silk that was sorted into standardized grades. The last sentence draws a conclusion that only works when you combine both points: buyers valued consistency more than peak quality. "Taken together," signals exactly that kind of synthesis.
B is wrong: "Nevertheless," treats the final sentence as a simple contrast because the two observations look opposed. But the final sentence doesn't contradict the second observation. It explains why the two observations fit together.
C is wrong: "In other words," treats the final sentence as a restatement of the second observation alone. That ignores the part about "not the excellence of any single skein," which depends on the first observation about Italian quality.
D is wrong: "Similarly," would introduce a parallel example. The final sentence is a conclusion, not a new comparable case.
g.design: Two observations seem to clash: Italian silk was judged better skein by skein, yet buyers chose Japanese silk. The last sentence needs a transition that combines both. Each wrong answer matches one assigned misconception: B (Nevertheless) treats it as a simple contrast, C (In other words) reflects only one observation, and D (Similarly) has nothing to do with the conclusion.

c.instruction: 한 문장 안에서 수식어구나 비교 표현이 인접한 명사가 아니라 문장 앞부분의 다른 요소(주어나 앞 문장의 대상)를 가리키도록 설계된 짧은 지문을 만들고, 이 실제 지시 관계를 올바르게 파악해야 정답 전환어를 고를 수 있게 하라. 오답 3개는 (1)인접한 명사를 지시 대상으로 잘못 본 전환어, (2)문법적으로는 자연스럽지만 실제 지시관계와 어긋나는 전환어, (3)전혀 다른 요소를 지시 대상으로 삼은 전환어로 구성하라. 문장은 짧고 단순한 구조를 유지한다.
c.seed: economics and business — Scottish herring fishing industry and landed estates' investment in salting infrastructure expanding domestic export capacity

g.passage: In the early 1800s, most herring landed at Wick, in northern Scotland, was eaten within a few miles of the town. During the 1810s, local landed estates paid for curing sheds, salt stores, and a cooperage on the town's harbor. ______ the same fish, salted and packed in barrels inspected to a government standard, was soon leaving Wick for Baltic and Irish ports in large quantities.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Likewise,
As a result,
Nonetheless,
For example,
g.explanation:
'the same fish'는 바로 앞 문장의 시설(헛간·창고·통 공방)이 아니라 첫 문장의 주어인 '윅에 들어온 청어'를 가리킨다. 즉 한때 지역에서만 소비되던 청어가, 영지가 염장 시설에 투자한 뒤로 대량 수출되었다는 흐름이다. 둘째 문장의 투자가 셋째 문장의 수출 확대를 가능하게 했으므로 인과 관계를 나타내는 'As a result,'가 정답이다.
A(Likewise): 셋째 문장을 바로 앞의 시설 건설과 나란한 또 하나의 투자·확장으로 잘못 본 선택지다. 셋째 문장의 주어는 시설이 아니라 청어이며, 내용도 투자와 비슷한 일이 아니라 투자의 결과다.
C(Nonetheless): 문법상으로는 자연스럽게 읽히지만, 수출 증가는 투자에도 불구하고 일어난 일이 아니라 투자 덕분에 일어난 일이다.
D(For example): 셋째 문장을 영지가 한 투자의 한 사례로 본 선택지다. 그러나 이 문장은 투자의 사례가 아니라 첫 문장에서 말한 청어가 이후 어떻게 되었는지를 서술한다.
g.explanation_en:
The phrase "the same fish" doesn't point to the facilities in the sentence right before it (the sheds, stores, and cooperage). It points back to the subject of the first sentence: the herring landed at Wick. So the passage moves like this: the herring used to be eaten only near the town, the estates then paid for curing facilities, and afterward that herring was exported in large amounts. The investment made the exports possible, so the cause-and-effect transition "As a result," is correct.
A (Likewise) treats the last sentence as another investment, similar to the facilities just mentioned. But the subject of the last sentence is the fish, and it describes a result of the investment, not a similar action.
C (Nonetheless) sounds fine grammatically, but the exports didn't grow in spite of the investment. They grew because of it.
D (For example) treats the last sentence as one example of the estates' investment. In fact, it tells what later happened to the herring from the first sentence.
g.design: The phrase "the same fish" skips past the facilities in the sentence just before it and refers back to the herring in the first sentence. Students have to see that link to recognize the cause-and-effect relationship. The wrong answers are: a parallel transition that wrongly ties the sentence to the nearby facilities (Likewise), a contrast that is grammatical but has the logic backward (Nonetheless), and an example transition that treats the sentence as a case of the investment (For example).

c.instruction:
- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).
- 세부 기술 힌트: 수식어가 짧은 주어-동사 수 일치, 시제 일관성, 대명사 격/수 일치처럼 한 규칙을 묻는 문제.
c.seed: economics and business — French Bordeaux wine négociant system and shipper control of classification driving price premium differentiation

g.passage: In France's Bordeaux region, négociants (merchant shippers) long controlled how wine moved from estates to buyers around the world. The official ranking of the region's top estates, drafted in 1855 largely from these merchants' sales records, ______ a major reason that some Bordeaux wines sell for many times the price of wines made just a few miles away.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: remain
have remained
remains
are remaining
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'ranking'이므로 동사도 단수형이어야 하고, 그래서 C가 정답이다. 주어와 동사 사이의 'of the region's top estates'와 삽입구 'drafted in 1855 … records'는 수식어일 뿐이라 동사의 수에 영향을 주지 않는다. A, B, D는 모두 복수형 동사이다. 이 선택지들은 동사 바로 앞에 있는 복수 명사 'estates'나 'records'를 주어로 착각하게 만든다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "ranking," so the verb also has to be singular. That makes C the correct answer. The phrase "of the region's top estates" and the inserted phrase "drafted in 1855 ... records" are just modifiers that sit between the subject and the verb, so they don't change the verb's number. A, B, and D are all plural verb forms. They tempt you to treat a nearby plural noun like "estates" or "records" as the subject.
g.design: The subject and verb are separated by modifiers that contain plural nouns. All four choices use the same verb in present-tense forms, so the only thing to decide is whether the verb should be singular or plural.

c.instruction:
- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).
- 세부 기술 힌트: 수식어가 짧은 주어-동사 수 일치, 시제 일관성, 대명사 격/수 일치처럼 한 규칙을 묻는 문제.
c.seed: economics and business — Swedish ball-bearing manufacturer SKF and licensing agreements spreading manufacturing technology across European firms

g.passage: Founded in Sweden in 1907, the ball-bearing manufacturer SKF quickly grew by allowing other companies to use its designs. According to economic historians, the licensing agreements signed by SKF ______ an important reason that advanced bearing technology appeared in factories across Europe during the early twentieth century.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: is
was
has been
are
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 복수 명사 "agreements"이고, "signed by SKF"는 짧은 수식어일 뿐이다. 따라서 동사도 복수형이어야 하므로 D "are"가 정답이다. A "is", B "was", C "has been"은 모두 단수 동사로, 바로 앞의 단수 명사 "SKF"에 동사를 맞추는 흔한 실수를 노린 선택지이다. 이 오답들은 복수 주어와 수가 일치하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the plural noun "agreements." The phrase "signed by SKF" is just a short modifier, so the verb has to be plural, which makes D, "are," the correct answer. Choices A ("is"), B ("was"), and C ("has been") are all singular verbs. They play on a common mistake: matching the verb to the nearby singular noun "SKF." None of them agrees in number with the plural subject.
g.design: This easy item tests one rule: subject-verb agreement when a short modifier separates the subject from the verb. All three distractors are singular verbs that seem to fit the nearby noun "SKF."

c.instruction: 그래프나 표에 두 개 이상의 변수(또는 텍스트 설명과 그래프 수치)가 함께 제시된 자료를 주고, 두 요소를 동시에 봐야만 결론을 낼 수 있는 질문을 만들어라. 정답은 두 변수를 모두 반영해야 하고, 오답 3개는 각각 '한쪽 변수만 본 결론', '다른 쪽 변수만 본 결론', '자료에 없는 제3의 변수로 결론'을 만든 것으로 구성하라.
c.seed: economics and business — Indian indigo dye cartel and price fixing by London traders during colonial monopoly period

g.passage: In the early nineteenth century, much of the indigo grown in Bengal was sold through a small group of London brokerage houses. Economic historian Mira Sandhu argues that these houses operated as an informal cartel: rather than competing, they coordinated their bids at the quarterly London auctions to hold down the prices paid to Bengal planters. Sandhu notes that a cartel of this kind would leave a specific signature in auction records. If the houses were truly competing, the price per chest should have risen in years when the Bengal harvest was small, since scarcity would push buyers to outbid one another. Under coordination, however, prices would stay nearly flat regardless of harvest size, while the share of chests bought by the leading houses would remain consistently high. Sandhu has compiled auction records that report, for each year from 1815 to 1830, both the size of the Bengal harvest and the average price per chest paid at auction.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Sandhu's claim about the London brokerage houses?
options: In years when the Bengal harvest fell well below average, the average auction price per chest stayed within a few percent of its level in abundant years.
Across the period, the average auction price per chest changed by only a few percent from one year to the next.
In several years, the Bengal harvest was less than half the size of the harvest in the preceding year.
Over the period, the cost of shipping a chest of indigo from Calcutta to London rose more steeply than the auction price per chest.
g.design: 정답은 수확량과 가격 두 변수를 함께 연결(흉작에도 가격 평탄)해야 성립한다. B는 가격만 보고, C는 수확량만 보며, D는 자료에 없는 운송비라는 제3의 변수를 쓴다.
g.explanation:
정답 A: Sandhu는 경쟁 시장이라면 흉작인 해에 가격이 올라야 하지만 담합이 있으면 수확량과 관계없이 가격이 거의 그대로일 것이라고 예측한다. A는 수확량(흉작)과 가격(거의 변화 없음)을 함께 보여 주므로 이 예측과 바로 맞아떨어진다.
B(가격만 봄): 가격이 해마다 안정적이었다는 것만으로는 부족하다. 그 기간에 수확량 자체가 안정적이었다면 경쟁 시장에서도 가격은 평탄하게 나온다. 수확량과 연결해야 의미가 생긴다.
C(수확량만 봄): 수확량이 크게 변했다는 사실만 있고 그때 가격이 어땠는지가 없다. 따라서 경쟁인지 담합인지 가려낼 수 없다.
D(제3의 변수): 운송비는 Sandhu가 정한 신호(수확량 대비 가격)에 들어 있지 않고 자료에도 없는 변수이므로 주장을 직접 뒷받침하지 못한다.
g.explanation_en:
Correct answer, A: Sandhu predicts that if the market were competitive, prices would rise in years with small harvests. Under a cartel, prices would stay nearly flat no matter how big the harvest was. Choice A links the two variables together: harvests were low, yet prices barely moved. That is exactly the pattern Sandhu says a cartel would leave.
B (looks only at price): Steady prices from year to year don't prove anything by themselves. If harvests were also steady, a competitive market would produce flat prices too. You need to tie price to harvest size before the pattern means anything.
C (looks only at harvest size): This tells you harvests varied a lot, but it says nothing about how prices responded. Without that, you can't tell competition from coordination.
D (brings in an outside variable): Shipping costs aren't part of Sandhu's test or her data, so this finding can't directly support her claim.

c.instruction: 지문에 상관관계나 동시 발생 사실만 제시하고, 이를 근거로 특정 가설(주장)의 인과성을 지지하는지 판단해야 하는 문항을 만들어라. 정답은 인과 방향과 대안 설명 가능성을 함께 고려해 타당하게 지지하는 것이어야 하고, 오답 3개는 각각 '상관을 그대로 인과로 오해', '인과 방향을 반대로 설정', '무관한 제3의 원인을 인과로 제시'로 구성하라.
c.seed: economics and business — German Ruhr coal mining and vertical integration with steel mills reducing transaction costs dramatically

g.passage: In the late nineteenth century, many steel firms in Germany's Ruhr district bought coal mines of their own instead of purchasing coal on the open market. Economic historian Lena Brandt notes that the vertically integrated firms, which owned both mines and mills, reported much lower costs for negotiating, monitoring, and enforcing coal deliveries than steel firms that bought from independent mines did. Brandt argues that integration itself caused these savings: once a mill owned its supplier, it no longer had to haggle over prices, write detailed contracts, or guard against a supplier withholding coal at critical moments. Critics point out, however, that the firms that integrated tended to be the largest and best-managed in the region to begin with.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Brandt's argument?
options: Across the Ruhr district, steel firms that owned coal mines consistently reported lower coal-procurement costs than steel firms of every size that did not own mines.

When individual steel firms acquired coal mines, their spending on contract negotiation and delivery enforcement fell sharply within a few years, even for firms whose size and management staff did not change.
Steel firms that had already achieved unusually low coal-procurement costs were later much more likely than other firms to acquire coal mines of their own.
During the period when integration spread, new railway lines across the Ruhr lowered transport costs for coal shipped from both independent and firm-owned mines.
g.explanation:
정답 B: 같은 기업을 인수 전과 후로 비교하므로, 비판자들이 제기한 대안 설명(원래 크고 경영이 잘된 기업이라는 점)을 규모와 경영진이 변하지 않았다는 조건으로 통제한다. 비용 감소가 인수 뒤에 나타나므로 인과 방향도 '통합→절감'으로 맞는다. 따라서 통합 자체가 비용 절감을 낳았다는 Brandt의 주장을 직접 지지한다.
A(상관을 인과로 오해): 기업 규모를 맞춰 비교해도 결국 통합 기업과 비통합 기업을 한 시점에서 비교한 상관관계일 뿐이다. 통합 기업은 경영 능력처럼 다른 점에서도 달랐을 수 있으므로 통합이 원인임을 보여 주지 못한다.
C(인과 방향 반대): 비용이 낮은 기업이 나중에 통합했다는 것은 낮은 비용이 통합을 낳았음을 시사한다. 이는 오히려 Brandt의 주장을 약화한다.
D(무관한 제3의 원인): 철도는 독립 광산의 석탄과 기업 소유 광산의 석탄 모두의 비용을 낮췄다. 또 이는 운송비일 뿐 협상·감시·이행 같은 거래비용이 아니다. 통합의 효과를 가려내지 못하며, 오히려 다른 원인이 있었음을 보여 준다.
g.explanation_en:
Correct answer, B: This finding compares the same firms before and after they acquired mines. Because their size and management stayed the same, it rules out the critics' alternative explanation that integrated firms were simply bigger and better run. The savings also came after the acquisition, so the cause runs from integration to lower costs. That directly supports Brandt's claim that integration itself caused the savings.
A mistakes correlation for causation. Even when firms of similar size are compared, it's still a snapshot of integrated firms versus non-integrated ones. The integrated firms could have differed in other ways, such as management quality, so this doesn't show that integration was the cause.
C reverses the direction of cause. If firms that already had low costs were the ones that later integrated, then low costs led to integration, not the other way around. That actually weakens Brandt's argument.
D offers an unrelated third cause. The railways cut costs for coal from both independent and firm-owned mines, and they affected transport costs, not the costs of negotiating, monitoring, and enforcing deliveries. So this finding can't single out integration as the cause of the savings.
g.design: The passage gives only a correlation and includes a confounder raised by critics. The correct answer is a before-and-after comparison within the same firms that controls for the confounder. Each wrong answer matches one assigned trap: a cross-sectional correlation, reverse causation, and an unrelated third cause.

c.instruction: 지문에 가설(주장)만 제시하고, 그 가설을 뒷받침하려면 어떤 추가 증거나 결과가 있어야 하는지 묻는 문항을 만들어라. 정답은 지문에 없는 가상의 결과이지만 가설의 논리 구조와 정확히 들어맞아야 하고, 오답 3개는 각각 '가설과 무관한 사실', '가설을 반박하는 결과', '이미 지문에 있는 사실을 재진술한 것'으로 구성하라.
c.seed: economics and business — British pottery manufacturers' brand licensing and knockoff litigation defending designs in Staffordshire region

g.passage: In the late eighteenth century, Staffordshire pottery firms such as Wedgwood faced a steady stream of cheaper imitations of their most popular designs. Some manufacturers responded by suing copyists, while others instead licensed their patterns to smaller regional workshops in exchange for fees. Economic historian Clara Venn argues that licensing was not merely a source of extra income: by allowing approved workshops to produce authorized versions, she claims, the original firms reduced the market space available to unauthorized copyists, because buyers seeking a lower-priced version of a famous design could now obtain a legitimate one. Venn notes that the firms that licensed most widely were also among the largest and best-capitalized in the region.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Venn's claim?
options: Staffordshire firms that licensed their patterns tended to have more capital and larger workforces than firms that relied only on lawsuits.
Court records show that lawsuits brought by Staffordshire potteries against copyists were frequently decided in the original firms' favor.

Surviving sales inventories show that after a firm began licensing a given pattern, sales of unauthorized imitations of that pattern fell, while imitations of the same firm's unlicensed patterns did not decline.
Merchants' records indicate that unauthorized imitations of licensed patterns continued to sell at roughly the same volume after licensed versions reached the market.
g.design: 가설의 인과 구조(라이선스→저가 정품 공급→무단 모조품 시장 축소)를 비교군까지 갖춰 검증하는 가상 결과를 정답으로 두고, 오답은 지문 재진술·무관 사실·반박 결과로 구성했다.
g.explanation:
정답 C: Venn의 주장은 라이선스 정품이 저가 수요를 흡수해 무단 모조품의 시장을 줄였다는 것이다. 같은 회사 안에서 라이선스를 준 문양만 모조품 판매가 줄고 라이선스하지 않은 문양은 줄지 않았다면, 회사 규모 같은 다른 요인을 통제한 상태에서 감소가 라이선스 때문이라는 점이 드러나므로 주장을 직접 뒷받침한다.
A(지문 재진술): 라이선스를 널리 준 회사가 크고 자본이 많았다는 점은 지문에 이미 나와 있고, 모조품 시장이 줄었는지에 대해서는 아무것도 말해 주지 않는다.
B(무관한 사실): 소송 결과는 다른 전략(소송)에 관한 것이지 라이선스의 효과와는 관계가 없다.
D(반박): 라이선스 정품이 나온 뒤에도 모조품 판매가 그대로였다면 주장을 약화시킨다.
g.explanation_en:
C is correct. Venn claims that licensing shrank the market for unauthorized copies, because buyers who wanted a cheaper version could now buy a legitimate one. Look at what C compares: within the same firm, imitations fell only for the patterns that were licensed, while imitations of unlicensed patterns did not fall. Because both groups belong to the same firm, firm size can't explain the difference, so the drop points to licensing itself. That fits Venn's claim exactly.
A is wrong because it only repeats something the passage already says (the firms that licensed most widely were large and well-capitalized). It tells you nothing about whether copyists lost sales.
B is wrong because it is about lawsuits, the other strategy, so it has nothing to do with whether licensing worked.
D is wrong because if imitations kept selling at the same volume after licensed versions appeared, that would weaken Venn's claim, not support it.

issues: answer_leak:질문의 주체·수치를 정답만 반복(정답 1개 고유 일치, 오답 0)|정답이 가장 긴 선택지(32단어, 오답 최대 23)

c.instruction: 지문에 '한때 ~라고 여겨졌으나(통념)' 다음 'however/but/실제로는' 류의 전환어와 함께 이를 뒤집는 새 증거나 반박 문장을 제시하고, 빈칸이 그 반박된 결과를 표현하도록 한다. 정답은 통념과 정반대 방향의 의미를 가진 어휘로 하고, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 통념 쪽 단어를 그대로 쓴 것, (2) 전환어를 못 읽고 통념과 같은 방향이지만 강도만 다른 단어, (3) 반박 대상과 무관한 제3의 의미 단어로 구성한다. 전환 지점 앞뒤 문장만으로 답이 결정되게 하고 문장 길이나 어휘 난이도는 중간 수준을 유지한다.
c.seed: economics and business — Portuguese cork manufacturing cluster and bark harvesting sustainability practices maintaining long-term supply chains

g.passage: Because cork oaks can be stripped of their bark only once every nine years, analysts long assumed that Portugal's cork industry would be held back by a supply too slow to keep pace with global demand. Recent studies of the cluster around Santa Maria da Feira, however, show that the nine-year harvesting cycle has in fact made supply highly predictable: processors know years in advance how much bark each estate will yield and plan their investments accordingly. Far from limiting the industry, the slow cycle has proved ______ to its long-term stability.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: detrimental
somewhat inconvenient
incidental
integral
g.explanation: 정답 D(integral): 'however'와 'Far from limiting' 뒤에서 느린 수확 주기가 공급을 예측 가능하게 만들어 산업 안정에 기여했다고 말하므로, 안정성에 '필수적인/핵심적인'이라는 뜻이 들어가야 한다. A(detrimental, 해로운)는 반박된 통념을 그대로 되풀이한 말이다. B(somewhat inconvenient, 다소 불편한)는 통념과 같은 부정적 방향이고 강도만 약하게 한 것이라 전환어와 맞지 않는다. C(incidental, 부수적인)는 해롭다/이롭다는 논점과 상관없이 '관련이 적다'는 제3의 의미여서, 주기 덕분에 투자 계획이 가능해졌다는 근거와 어긋난다.
g.explanation_en: D (integral) is correct. The words "however" and "Far from limiting" signal a reversal: the slow harvesting cycle made supply predictable and allowed processors to plan their investments. That means the cycle is essential to the industry's stability. A (detrimental) just repeats the old assumption that the text rejects. B (somewhat inconvenient) points in the same negative direction as that assumption, only more weakly, so it ignores the reversal. C (incidental) brings in an unrelated idea, that the cycle barely matters, which contradicts the evidence that the cycle directly made planning possible.
g.design: 통념(느린 주기가 산업 제약)→however로 예측 가능성 증거→빈칸에 반대 방향 'integral'. 오답은 통념어(detrimental), 같은 방향의 약한 강도(somewhat inconvenient), 무관한 제3 의미(incidental)로 구성했다.

c.instruction: 지문에 'is not X, but rather Y' 또는 'it isn't that A; instead B' 형태로 부정어 뒤에 대조 표현이 이어지는 문장을 만들고, 빈칸이 그 대조 표현(B) 자리에 오게 한다. 정답은 부정된 개념(X)과 반대 극성을 가진 어휘로 하고, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 부정어를 무시하고 X와 같은 의미 단어, (2) 부정 구조를 이중으로 잘못 해석해 극성을 다시 뒤집은 단어, (3) 대조 구조와 무관한 유사 발음/철자 단어로 구성한다.
c.seed: economics and business — Swiss watchmaking cottage system and canton specialization reducing production costs through geographic concentration

g.passage: In the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, much Swiss watchmaking ran on a cottage system. Merchants sent parts to farm families in the Jura Mountains, and each district specialized in a single stage of production: some valleys made rough movements, while workshops in Geneva finished cases and dials. It might seem that spreading production across so many households would have multiplied expenses. Economic historians argue, however, that the arrangement did not add to merchants' costs; instead, concentrating each task in one district ______ those costs. Neighbors shared specialized tools, trained one another's apprentices, and sent finished parts only short distances.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: pared
swelled
propped up
paired
g.explanation:
정답 A(pared): 'did not add to costs; instead … ______ those costs' 구조에서 빈칸에는 '비용을 늘리다'와 극성이 반대인 말이 들어가야 한다. 이웃끼리 공구를 함께 쓰고, 서로의 견습생을 가르치고, 부품을 짧은 거리만 보냈다는 마지막 문장도 비용 절감을 뒷받침한다. 따라서 '깎아 줄이다'라는 뜻의 pared가 맞다.
B(swelled): '부풀리다'는 부정된 개념인 add to와 같은 뜻이다. 'not'을 무시한 오답이다.
C(propped up): '떠받쳐 유지하다'는 비용을 높은 수준으로 지탱한다는 뜻이다. 부정 뒤의 대조를 한 번 더 뒤집어 다시 비용을 높이는 쪽으로 읽은 오답이다.
D(paired): pared와 발음·철자가 비슷하지만 '짝짓다'라는 뜻이다. 비용에 대한 대조 구조와 아무 관계가 없다.
g.explanation_en:
Choice A, "pared," is correct. The sentence says the arrangement "did not add to" costs and that "instead" concentration ______ them. So the blank needs the opposite of increasing costs. The last sentence supports this: neighbors shared tools, trained one another's apprentices, and shipped parts only short distances. All of these save money, so "pared" (cut down) fits.
B, "swelled," means the same as "add to." It ignores the word "not."
C, "propped up," means holding costs at a high level. It reverses the contrast a second time, so the meaning goes back to costs staying high instead of falling.
D, "paired," looks and sounds like "pared" but means "matched in twos." That makes no sense with costs.
g.design: 'did not add to costs; instead ______ those costs'라는 부정-대조 구조를 만들고, 빈칸을 대조 쪽(B 자리)에 두었다. 오답은 세 가지로 구성했다. 부정어를 무시한 동의어 swelled, 극성을 다시 뒤집은 propped up, 철자가 비슷한 paired이다.

c.instruction: 지문을 두 단계(예: 상황 묘사 후 화자의 숙고, 또는 기존 주장 소개 후 저자의 반박/선언)로 구성하고, 빈칸을 두 번째 단계의 시작 지점에 배치해 앞 단계와 다른 서술 기능을 하도록 한다. 정답은 두 번째 단계의 기능(숙고, 반박, 선언 등)에 맞는 어휘로 하고, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 첫 번째 단계에 어울리는 단어, (2) 두 단계 어디에도 맞지 않는 중립적 단어, (3) 의미는 비슷하나 문장이 요구하는 품사/기능이 다른 단어로 구성한다.
c.seed: economics and business — Belgian brewing guilds and beer style protection preventing foreign competition through recipe standardization laws

g.passage: For generations, historians have praised the recipe standardization laws enforced by Belgian brewing guilds in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries, crediting them with preserving distinctive regional beer styles and guaranteeing drinkers a reliable product. Economic historian Marieke Verhulst, however, ______ this account: after examining surviving guild ledgers, she found that the laws required ingredients that only local suppliers could provide, suggesting that the rules served less to protect quality than to shut foreign brewers out of town markets.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: upholds
challenges
summarizes
skeptical of
g.explanation:
지문은 두 단계로 되어 있다. 첫 단계는 길드 규정이 품질을 지켰다는 기존 통설을 소개하고, 둘째 단계는 'however'로 시작해 Verhulst의 반박을 내놓는다. 그녀는 규정이 외국 양조업자를 시장에서 몰아내는 역할을 했다는 증거를 제시한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 통설을 반박한다는 뜻의 동사가 필요하고, 정답은 B 'challenges'이다.
A 'upholds'(지지하다)는 첫 단계의 칭송하는 어조에는 어울린다. 하지만 'however' 및 뒤따르는 반대 증거와 모순된다.
C 'summarizes'(요약하다)는 중립적인 단어라서 어느 단계의 기능에도 맞지 않는다. 그녀는 통설을 요약하는 것이 아니라 새로운 증거로 뒤집는다.
D 'skeptical of'는 의미는 비슷하다. 그러나 형용사구이므로 주어 뒤에 동사가 필요한 이 문장에 넣으면 문법이 성립하지 않는다(be동사가 없음).
g.explanation_en:
The text has two stages. The first stage presents the traditional view that the guild laws protected quality. The second stage begins with "however" and gives Verhulst's rebuttal: she offers evidence that the laws actually kept foreign brewers out of town markets. So the blank needs a verb meaning "disputes," and the answer is B, "challenges."
A, "upholds," fits the praising tone of the first stage. However, it contradicts "however" and the opposing evidence that follows.
C, "summarizes," is neutral and doesn't match the function of either stage. Verhulst doesn't restate the old view; she overturns it with new evidence.
D, "skeptical of," has a similar meaning. But it is an adjective phrase, and this sentence needs a verb after the subject. Without "is," the sentence would be ungrammatical.
g.design: 빈칸을 둘째 단계인 반박의 시작 지점, 즉 'however' 직후의 동사 자리에 두었다. 오답은 다음 세 가지로 구성했다. 첫 단계에 맞는 단어(upholds), 어느 단계에도 맞지 않는 중립적 단어(summarizes), 뜻은 비슷하지만 품사가 다른 단어(skeptical of).

c.instruction: 텍스트 1은 주장과 이유를, 텍스트 2는 같은 주제의 다른 접근을 각각 짧게 제시하되 서로를 언급하지 않게 쓴다. 질문은 '텍스트 2의 저자라면 텍스트 1의 주장에 어떻게 반응할 것인가'로 한다. 정답은 텍스트 2의 전제에서만 도출되는 반응으로 만들고, 오답 3개는 텍스트 1의 내용을 반복하는 선택지, 텍스트 2의 결론만 되풀이하는 선택지, 텍스트 2가 다루지 않은 쟁점을 끌어온 선택지로 만든다.
c.seed: economics and business — Norwegian salmon farming and open-net cage regulation creating externality costs shifting to wild fisheries

g.passage:
Text 1
Norway's open-net salmon pens let sea lice and escaped farm fish spread into surrounding waters, imposing costs on wild salmon stocks and the river fisheries that depend on them. Because farm operators do not pay for this damage, some economists argue that the government should levy a per-tonne tax on farmed salmon output, so that the price of farmed fish reflects the harm it causes.

Text 2
In 2017, Norway divided its coast into production zones and began adjusting each zone's allowed growth according to measured lice levels on nearby wild salmon. Researchers studying the system note that the damage from a pen depends heavily on its location: a farm near a major salmon river's migration route can do far more harm than an equally large farm in a fjord that wild fish rarely pass through.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the proposal described in Text 1?
options: By agreeing that because farm operators do not pay for lice and escapes, farmed salmon is priced below its true cost to society
By maintaining that allowed growth in each production zone should be adjusted according to lice levels measured on wild salmon
By suggesting that a charge set only by the amount of salmon produced would fail to track how much harm a given farm actually causes
By arguing that a tax on farmed salmon would raise prices for consumers and weaken Norway's position in export markets
g.explanation: 정답 C: Text 2의 전제는 피해가 생산량이 아니라 위치(야생 연어 이동 경로와의 거리)에 따라 크게 달라진다는 것이다. 따라서 톤당 일률 과세는 같은 생산량이라도 피해가 다른 양식장을 똑같이 취급하게 되어 실제 피해를 반영하지 못한다고 반응할 것이다. A: Text 1의 논거(외부비용 미지불)를 되풀이할 뿐 Text 2의 관점에서 나오는 반응이 아니다. B: Text 2가 소개한 제도(구역별 성장 조정)를 반복할 뿐, 톤당 세금이라는 제안에 대한 평가가 담겨 있지 않다. D: 소비자 가격·수출 경쟁력은 Text 2가 전혀 다루지 않은 쟁점이다.
g.explanation_en: C is correct. Text 2's key premise is that the harm a pen causes depends mainly on where it sits: a farm on a major river's migration route does far more damage than an equally large farm in a fjord that wild fish rarely pass through. A tax based only on tonnes produced would charge those two farms the same amount, so it wouldn't track the harm each one actually causes. A just repeats Text 1's own reasoning about unpaid costs, so it isn't a response that comes from Text 2's perspective. B restates the zone system Text 2 describes, but it never evaluates the per-tonne tax proposal. D brings in consumer prices and export markets, which Text 2 never discusses.
g.design: The texts never mention each other. The correct answer comes only from Text 2's point that harm depends on location, which exposes the weakness of a tax based on output. Each wrong answer follows one assigned pattern: it repeats Text 1, restates Text 2's conclusion, or raises an outside issue.

c.instruction: 텍스트 1은 하나의 결론을 이끄는 주장을, 텍스트 2는 그 주장의 핵심 근거를 약하게 만들 수 있는 별개의 관찰이나 연구를 제시한다. 질문은 '텍스트 2의 저자가 텍스트 1의 어느 부분에 가장 이의를 제기할 것인가'로 한다. 정답은 텍스트 1의 결론이 아니라 그 결론이 기대는 가정으로 하고, 오답 3개는 결론 자체, 텍스트 1의 부수적 세부, 텍스트 2가 오히려 동의하는 부분으로 만든다.
c.seed: economics and business — Indonesian spice monopoly and Dutch trading post enforcement preventing cultivation outside Java colonial control

g.passage:
Text 1
For roughly a century and a half, the Dutch East India Company (VOC) kept cloves and nutmeg scarce and expensive in European markets. Company fleets made regular "extirpation" voyages to burn unauthorized clove trees on outlying islands, and garrisons on the Banda Islands guarded the nutmeg groves. Historian Pieter Lindqvist argues that this enforcement was what confined spice cultivation to Dutch-held islands. So when the company's naval patrols thinned in the 1760s and agents of the French administrator Pierre Poivre slipped seedlings out of the region, the monopoly's days were numbered.

Text 2
Botanist Amara Siregar's review of colonial garden records from Mauritius complicates the story of the smuggled seedlings. Most of the trees that Poivre's agents carried out died within months. Nutmeg in particular proved hard to grow: it needs specific soils, shade, and steady humidity, and it requires both male and female trees, which cannot be told apart until they flower years later. Profitable plantations outside the Moluccas appeared only after decades of repeated failed attempts.
g.question: Based on the texts, the author of Text 2 would most likely take issue with which element of the argument presented in Text 1?
options: The claim that the VOC's control of the spice trade could not be sustained indefinitely once the late eighteenth century arrived
The claim that garrisons were stationed on the Banda Islands to protect the nutmeg groves
The claim that agents working for Poivre managed to carry spice seedlings out of Dutch-held territory
The claim that Dutch policing was the main obstacle that kept the spices from being grown in other places
g.explanation:
정답 D: Text 1의 논증은 '단속(나무 소각·순찰)이 재배를 네덜란드 영토에 묶어 두었다'는 가정에 기대고 있으며, 그래서 단속이 약해지자 독점이 끝났다고 결론짓는다. Text 2는 밀반출된 묘목 대부분이 죽었고, 육두구는 토양·그늘·습도 조건이 까다로우며 암수 구별에도 수년이 걸려 수십 년간 재배에 실패했다고 보고한다. 즉 다른 지역에서 재배되지 못한 주된 이유는 단속이 아니라 원예적인 어려움일 수 있다는 것이므로, 바로 이 가정을 약화한다.
A(오답): Text 1의 결론에 해당한다. Text 2는 독점이 결국 끝났다는 사실 자체를 부정하지 않고, 이유를 설명하는 방식에만 문제를 제기한다.
B(오답): 부수적인 세부 사항이다. Text 2는 반다 제도의 수비대에 대해 아무 언급도 하지 않는다.
C(오답): Text 2가 오히려 전제로 받아들이는 내용이다. 묘목이 반출되었다는 사실은 인정하고, 반출된 묘목이 대부분 죽었다는 점만 덧붙인다.
g.explanation_en:
Correct answer, D: Text 1's argument depends on an assumption: Dutch enforcement (burning trees and running patrols) was what kept spice growing limited to Dutch-held islands. That is why Text 1 concludes the monopoly ended once enforcement weakened. Text 2 reports that most smuggled seedlings died. Nutmeg needs particular soils, shade, and humidity, and growers had to wait years to tell male trees from female ones, so attempts failed for decades. This points to the difficulty of growing the plants, not policing, as the real barrier, which weakens exactly that assumption.
A is wrong: This is Text 1's conclusion. Text 2 never denies that the monopoly eventually ended. It only questions why.
B is wrong: This is a side detail. Text 2 says nothing about the garrisons on Banda.
C is wrong: Text 2 actually accepts this point. It agrees the seedlings were taken out and then explains that most of them died.
g.design: In Text 1, the conclusion that the monopoly ended rests on an unstated premise that enforcement was the main barrier. Text 2's horticultural evidence attacks that premise. The wrong answers are the conclusion itself (A), a side detail (B), and a point Text 2 accepts (C). All four options use the same "The claim that…" frame, and the question doesn't use the key words of the correct answer.

c.instruction: 텍스트 1의 저자가 좋은 설명이나 해결책의 기준(예: 재현 가능성, 단순성, 장기적 효과)을 분명히 드러내게 쓰고, 텍스트 2는 그 기준과 어긋날 수 있는 결론을 내리게 쓴다. 질문은 '텍스트 1의 저자의 기준에서 텍스트 2의 결론을 어떻게 평가할 것인가'로 한다. 오답 3개는 텍스트 2 저자의 기준으로 평가한 결과, 두 저자의 기준을 섞은 평가, 일반 상식에 따른 평가로 만든다.
c.seed: economics and business — Australian wool grease price volatility and futures market hedging adoption by grazier cooperatives

g.passage:
Text 1
Economists studying risk management in Australian agriculture often ask whether a hedging strategy "worked." In my view, a strategy should be judged not by whether it produced gains in a particular season but by whether it reduced the variability of a producer's income across many seasons. A hedge that loses money in a year when prices happen to rise has still done its job if it made earnings more predictable over time.

Text 2
When several grazier cooperatives in New South Wales began selling futures contracts on wool grease in 2019, they hoped to protect members from sudden price drops. That year, however, lanolin demand from cosmetics manufacturers surged, and spot prices for wool grease climbed sharply. The cooperatives, locked into lower contract prices, earned considerably less than unhedged neighbors. Many members concluded that the futures program had been a costly mistake, and two cooperatives abandoned it the following year.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 1 most likely evaluate the conclusion reached by the cooperative members described in Text 2?
options: As premature, because a single season's shortfall relative to unhedged producers says little about whether the program steadied members' earnings over a longer span
As reasonable, because the program left members earning substantially less than neighboring producers who chose not to hedge in 2019
As partly justified, because the program should be retained only if it eventually yields higher average profits than remaining unhedged would
As understandable, because unexpected shifts in cosmetics demand make wool grease prices too unpredictable for any financial strategy to manage
g.explanation:
정답 A: Text 1 저자의 기준은 특정 시즌의 이익이 아니라 여러 시즌에 걸친 소득 변동성 감소이다. Text 2의 조합원들은 한 해(2019)의 손실만 보고 실패라 판단했으므로, Text 1 저자는 이를 성급한 결론으로 볼 것이다.
B: Text 2 조합원들의 기준(그해 이웃 대비 수익)으로 평가한 것으로, Text 1 저자가 명시적으로 거부한 기준이다.
C: 장기 관점(Text 1)과 수익 기준(Text 2)을 섞은 평가. Text 1 저자는 평균 이익이 아니라 예측 가능성을 기준으로 삼는다.
D: '가격이 너무 예측 불가하면 헤지가 무의미하다'는 일반 상식적 평가로, 오히려 변동성이 클수록 헤지의 의의가 있다는 Text 1 관점과 어긋나고 지문에 근거도 없다.
g.explanation_en:
A is correct: The author of Text 1 judges a hedge by whether it reduces income variability across many seasons, not by results in one season. The members in Text 2 decided the program failed based only on 2019, when they earned less than unhedged neighbors. By Text 1's standard, that's a premature verdict, since one year can't show whether earnings became more predictable over time.
B is wrong because it uses the members' own standard (profit compared with neighbors in a single year), which is exactly the standard Text 1 rejects.
C is wrong because it blends the two views: it takes a long-term timeframe from Text 1 but keeps a profit-based test from Text 2. Text 1 cares about predictability, not higher average profits.
D is wrong because it relies on a general assumption that very volatile prices can't be managed. Text 1 actually implies that volatility is what hedging is meant to address, and neither text supports D's claim.
g.design: Text 1 sets an explicit criterion (multi-season variance reduction); Text 2's members judge by single-season relative profit. Distractors: Text 2's criterion (B), a blend of both criteria (C), and a commonsense view (D).

c.seed: economics and business — German optical lens manufacturing and patent pools for precision instrument industry standardization early twentieth century

g.passage: In the early twentieth century, several German makers of optical lenses agreed to share their patents with one another. Before this arrangement, each firm used its own measurements for lens threads and mounts, so a lens from one company often would not fit a microscope from another. By pooling their patents, the firms were able to ______ these measurements, so that parts from different makers could finally be used together.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: diversify
standardize
conceal
multiply
g.explanation: 지문은 회사마다 측정 기준이 달라 부품이 서로 맞지 않았는데, 특허 공유 이후 여러 제조사의 부품을 함께 쓸 수 있게 되었다고 말한다. 따라서 측정 기준을 '통일하다'는 뜻의 B가 정답이다. A는 '다양화하다'로, 기준이 더 제각각이 되면 호환성 문제가 오히려 커진다. C는 '숨기다'로, 측정값을 숨기면 부품을 함께 쓸 수 있게 된다는 결과와 이어지지 않는다. D는 '늘리다'로, 기준의 수를 늘리는 것은 호환성을 높이는 것과 반대된다.
g.explanation_en: The text says each firm used different measurements, so parts did not fit together, and that after the patent pool, parts from different makers could finally be used together. That means the firms made the measurements uniform, so B is correct. A means "make more varied," which would make the fit problem worse. C means "hide," and hiding measurements would not let parts work together. D means "increase in number," and having more sets of measurements is the opposite of making parts compatible.
g.design: The answer depends on one clear contrast in the text: measurements that didn't match before versus parts that work together after. The wrong choices are real verbs about changing measurements that could seem plausible but go against the result described in the passage.

c.seed: economics and business — Peruvian silver mining labor exploitation and encomienda system extracting colonial wealth through forced wage suppression

g.passage: In the late 1500s, Spanish colonial officials in Peru forced Indigenous workers to labor in the silver mines of Potosí through a system called the mita. Workers were paid wages far below what they needed to survive, and many had to rely on their families to send food. Historians argue that these low wages were not accidental: officials deliberately kept pay ______ so that more of the mines' wealth would flow to Spain.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: generous
steady
meager
public
g.design: 빈칸 바로 앞의 '생존에 필요한 수준보다 훨씬 낮은 임금'과 '부가 스페인으로 흘러가도록'이라는 직접 단서 하나로 풀리게 했다. 오답은 모두 임금을 꾸밀 수 있는 그럴듯한 형용사로 만들었다.
g.explanation: 지문은 임금이 생존에 필요한 수준보다 훨씬 낮았고, 관리들이 부를 스페인으로 보내려고 일부러 임금을 낮게 유지했다고 말한다. 따라서 '아주 적은'이라는 뜻의 C(meager)가 정답이다. A(generous, 후한)는 지문 내용과 정반대이다. B(steady, 꾸준한)는 임금에 쓸 수는 있지만 금액이 적다는 핵심을 담지 못한다. D(public, 공개된)는 임금이 얼마나 낮았는지와 아무 관련이 없다.
g.explanation_en: The text says the wages were far below what workers needed to survive, and that officials kept pay low on purpose so more wealth would go to Spain. So C (meager), meaning very small, is the correct answer. A (generous) means the opposite of what the text describes. B (steady) can describe pay, but it doesn't say anything about the pay being small, which is the main point. D (public) has nothing to do with how low the wages were.

c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Hildegard von Bingen's illuminated manuscripts and medieval theological symbolism integration

g.passage: Hildegard von Bingen, the twelfth-century German abbess, recorded her visions in a work called Scivias, and the most famous copy of it, made at her own monastery around 1175, paired the text with thirty-five vivid illuminations. Many art historians once treated these images as decorative supplements, pictures added to make a difficult theological book more appealing. More recent scholars, however, point out that the illuminations frequently present information the written text does not. In one image depicting the cosmos as an egg-shaped structure, for instance, the placement of flames, winds, and stars encodes a hierarchy of divine forces that Hildegard's prose describes only loosely. Readers who consulted the manuscript would therefore have needed to study word and image together to grasp her full account of creation.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: The illuminations in the Scivias manuscript were added mainly to make Hildegard's challenging theological writing more attractive to readers.
The egg-shaped image of the cosmos in the Scivias manuscript is the most detailed of the work's thirty-five illuminations.
Hildegard's written descriptions of her visions were too loose to be understood by readers without the help of later commentators.
The illuminations in the Scivias manuscript function as a source of theological meaning in their own right rather than as mere ornament.
g.design: 정답은 '이미지가 텍스트에 없는 정보를 전달 → 함께 읽어야 함'을 연결해 '독자적 의미 원천'으로 바꿔 말했고, 오답은 과거 견해(A), 예시 과장(B), 산문 'loosely' 왜곡(C)으로 부분 근거를 갖게 했다.
g.explanation: 정답은 D이다. 지문은 예전 견해(장식)를 소개한 뒤, 최근 학자들이 삽화가 본문에 없는 신학적 정보를 담고 있어 글과 그림을 함께 읽어야 한다고 본다는 점을 중심 내용으로 제시한다. A는 지문이 반박하는 예전 견해일 뿐이다. B는 하나의 예시를 다루지만 그것이 가장 상세하다는 비교는 지문에 없다. C는 산문이 'loosely' 서술한다는 세부를 과장했고, 후대 주석가는 언급되지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: D is correct. The text first describes an older view that the illuminations were only decoration, then explains that recent scholars find the images carry theological information the text leaves out, so readers had to study word and image together. A just restates the older view, and the text argues against it. B focuses on one example, but the text never says that image is the most detailed of the thirty-five. C stretches the point that the prose is "loose" in one place, and the text never brings up later commentators.

c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Zeami's concept of ma (negative space) in Japanese Noh theatre performance theory

g.passage: In his treatises on Noh theatre, the fifteenth-century actor and playwright Zeami Motokiyo praised moments he described as "where nothing is done." Between a dance and a chant, or between two gestures, a performer may stand completely still, and audiences often find these pauses more moving than the movements around them. Some modern commentators have treated such pauses as simple rests, breaks that let the actor recover and the audience absorb what came before. Zeami, however, insisted that the interval, later linked to the concept of ma, works only when the actor's inner concentration never slackens. If the performer's attention drifts during the stillness, he warned, the pause turns into mere emptiness and the audience loses interest. In Zeami's view, then, what spectators respond to in these moments is not the absence of action but a focused intensity that the actor keeps up without showing it outwardly.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Zeami held that the still intervals in Noh move audiences because the performer stays fully focused within them, not because they offer a break from action.
Zeami held that the still intervals in Noh move audiences because they give spectators time to reflect on the dances and chants that come before them.
Zeami held that the still intervals in Noh move audiences more than any dance or chant, so performers should lengthen them whenever possible.
Zeami held that the still intervals in Noh move audiences only when the performer signals his inner concentration through subtle facial expressions.
g.explanation: 지문은 정지 순간을 단순한 휴식으로 보는 현대 해석을 소개한 뒤, 제아미는 배우의 내면 집중이 계속 유지되어야만 그 순간이 효과를 낸다고 보았다고 반박하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 지문이 제아미의 견해가 아니라 반박 대상으로 제시한 현대 비평가들의 '휴식' 해석이다. C는 정지 순간이 더 감동적일 수 있다는 진술을 과장하고, 지문에 없는 '정지를 늘려야 한다'는 주장을 덧붙였다. D는 집중이 겉으로 드러나지 않는다는 마지막 문장과 정면으로 어긋난다.
g.explanation_en: The text sets up the modern view that the pauses are simple rests, then shows that Zeami disagreed: for him, the pauses work only because the actor's inner concentration never lets up. That makes A the answer. B describes the modern commentators' "rest" view, which the text presents as the idea Zeami rejected, not his own position. C exaggerates the claim that pauses are often more moving, and the text never says performers should make them longer. D contradicts the final sentence, which says the actor keeps up this intensity without showing it outwardly.
g.design: 오답 B는 지문에 실제로 등장하는 대조 견해, C는 지문 표현을 과장, D는 핵심어(집중)를 공유하나 세부가 반대 — 대조 구조를 정독해야 배제 가능.
