c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — The tonal system of Hindustani classical music and raag interpretation cultural specificity

g.passage:
Text 1
Some Western listeners describe Hindustani raags as simply "scales," like the major and minor scales of European music. On this view, once a listener learns which notes a raag uses, the listener understands the raag well enough to follow any performance of it.

Text 2
A raag is more than a set of notes. Two raags can share exactly the same notes yet sound completely different, because each has its own rules about which notes to stress, how to glide between them, and which phrases to repeat. Musicians learn these rules through years of study within the tradition, so knowing the notes alone tells a listener very little.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the view described in Text 1?
options: By agreeing that a raag's notes are enough to understand it, since Western scales and raags are built on the same basic principles
By agreeing that a raag's notes are enough to understand it, but adding that listeners should first learn the major and minor scales
By arguing that a raag's notes are unimportant, since performers are free to choose any notes they wish in each performance
By arguing that a raag's notes are not enough to understand it, since raags with identical notes can differ in how those notes are used
g.explanation: Text 1은 라가를 사용하는 음만 알면 이해할 수 있는 '음계'로 보는 시각을 소개한다. Text 2는 같은 음을 쓰는 두 라가도 강조·글리산도·반복 악구 규칙이 달라 전혀 다르게 들린다고 하므로, 음만으로는 부족하다고 반박할 것이다. 따라서 정답은 D이다. A와 B는 Text 2가 분명히 거부하는 '음만으로 충분하다'는 견해에 동의하므로 틀렸다. C는 연주자가 아무 음이나 고를 수 있다고 하지만, Text 2는 오히려 라가마다 엄격한 규칙이 있다고 말한다.
g.explanation_en: Text 1 presents the view that a raag is just a scale, so knowing its notes is enough to understand it. Text 2 says two raags can use exactly the same notes yet sound completely different because of rules about stress, glides, and phrases, so its author would reject that view. That makes D the correct answer. A and B both agree that the notes are enough, which is exactly what Text 2 denies. C claims performers can choose any notes they like, but Text 2 actually stresses that each raag has strict rules.
g.design: Easy: Text 2 directly contradicts Text 1 with one explicit clue (same notes, different raags). Every option uses the same "By agreeing/arguing that... since..." frame, and the wrong answers are common misreadings: siding with the view or overstating it.

c.instruction: 지문에 두 변수 사이의 이론적 관계(예: A가 클수록 B도 커진다, 정직한 신호일수록 비용이 크다)를 제시하고, 이 이론을 새로운 구체적 집단이나 사례에 적용했을 때 나올 결론을 빈칸으로 묻는다. 정답은 이론이 제시한 방향을 그대로 새 사례에 적용한 것이어야 하며, 오답 3개는 각각 관계의 방향을 반대로 뒤집기, 원인과 결과를 바꾸기, 이론과 무관한 제3의 요인을 결론으로 제시하기의 실제 오개념을 사용해 만든다.
c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Leonora Carrington's surrealist painting synthesizing alchemy and female transgressive imagination

g.passage: Art historian Mira Valdés argues that in Leonora Carrington's paintings, the density of alchemical symbolism—crucibles, eggs, distilling vessels—tracks how far a work departs from conventional depictions of women. In Valdés's account, Carrington borrowed alchemy's language of transmutation precisely because it offered a ready vocabulary for imagining female figures who escape assigned roles; the more transgressive the vision of womanhood a canvas pursued, the more heavily it leaned on that borrowed vocabulary. Valdés notes that Carrington's early Mexican portraits commissioned by patrons show women in fairly customary domestic poses, whereas a later group of private works depicts women as sorceresses reconfiguring the kitchen into a laboratory. If Valdés is correct, a viewer comparing these two groups should expect that ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the private works will contain markedly more crucibles, eggs, and other alchemical motifs than the commissioned portraits do.
the commissioned portraits will contain markedly more crucibles, eggs, and other alchemical motifs than the private works do.
the private works became more transgressive because Carrington first decided to add more alchemical motifs to them.
the private works will differ from the commissioned portraits mainly in being painted on larger canvases with brighter pigments.
g.explanation:
정답 A: Valdés의 이론은 '여성상이 더 위반적일수록 연금술 상징이 더 많다'는 정비례 관계다. 후기 개인 작품(부엌을 실험실로 바꾸는 마녀)이 의뢰 초상(관습적 가사 자세)보다 더 위반적이므로, 연금술 모티프가 더 많을 것으로 예상된다.
B: 관계의 방향을 뒤집은 오답이다. 관습적인 초상화에 상징이 더 많다는 것은 이론과 정반대다.
C: 인과를 뒤바꾼 오답이다. 이론은 위반적 비전을 추구하기 위해 연금술 어휘를 빌렸다고 하므로, 위반성이 원인이고 상징 사용은 결과다. 또한 이 선택지는 두 집단을 비교했을 때 무엇을 보게 될지 예측하지 않는다.
D: 이론과 무관한 제3의 요인(캔버스 크기·안료)을 결론으로 내세운 오답이다.
g.explanation_en:
A is correct. Valdés's theory sets up a direct relationship: the more transgressive a canvas's vision of womanhood, the more it relies on alchemical symbolism. The later private works, which show sorceresses turning the kitchen into a laboratory, are more transgressive than the commissioned portraits of women in customary domestic poses. So the private works should contain more alchemical motifs.
B flips the direction of the relationship. It assigns more symbolism to the more conventional works.
C reverses cause and effect. In the theory, Carrington borrowed alchemical vocabulary in order to pursue a transgressive vision, so transgression is the cause and the symbolism is the result. C also fails to predict what a viewer comparing the two groups would actually see.
D brings in a factor the theory never mentions (canvas size and pigment), so nothing in the passage supports it.
g.design: I stated a positive relationship between how transgressive a work's vision is and how dense its alchemical symbolism is, then applied it to two new groups of works. Each wrong answer uses one of the three assigned misconceptions: reversing the direction, swapping cause and effect, or bringing in an unrelated third factor.

c.instruction: 짧은 표나 그래프 하나와 이를 설명하는 가설 문장 하나를 함께 제시하고, 두 정보를 결합해야만 답할 수 있는 결론을 빈칸으로 묻는다. 정답은 시각 자료의 특정 수치와 가설 문장을 연결해야 나오고, 오답 3개는 각각 시각 자료만 보고 가설을 무시한 결론, 가설 문장만 보고 시각 자료를 무시한 결론, 시각 자료의 다른 항목을 잘못 짝지은 결론으로 만든다.
c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — The rhetorical function of apostrophe in Romantic era English lyric poetry composition

g.passage:
Literary scholar Nadia Okafor studies apostrophe, the rhetorical device in which a poet directly addresses an absent person, an abstraction, or a nonhuman thing (e.g., "O wild West Wind"). Okafor hypothesizes that when a Romantic poet addresses something incapable of replying, the addressee's silence gradually undermines the speaker's confidence, so that the poet abandons the address and turns toward first-person reflection as the poem proceeds. To examine this idea, she measured how much of each of several poems consists of apostrophic lines.

Percentage of lines in apostrophe

| Poem | Addressee | First half | Second half |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shelley, "Ode to the West Wind" (1820) | the wind | 62% | 58% |
| Keats, "Ode to a Nightingale" (1819) | a bird | 55% | 21% |
| Wordsworth, "Tintern Abbey" (1798) | his sister | 8% | 40% |
| Coleridge, "Dejection: An Ode" (1802) | a lady | 30% | 33% |

Based on the table, a reader could conclude that among the poems Okafor examined, ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: Shelley's "Ode to the West Wind" most closely fits Okafor's hypothesis, since it devotes a larger share of its lines to apostrophe than any other poem in the table does.
Keats's "Ode to a Nightingale" most closely fits Okafor's hypothesis, since its speaker addresses a creature that cannot reply and its apostrophic share drops markedly between the poem's halves.
every poem addressing a silent or absent figure most closely fits Okafor's hypothesis, since such addressees cannot answer and therefore must erode the speaker's confidence over time.
Wordsworth's "Tintern Abbey" most closely fits Okafor's hypothesis, since its apostrophic share changes by a greater amount between the poem's halves than that of any other poem.
g.explanation:
정답 B: 가설이 맞으려면 두 조건이 필요하다. ①대답할 수 없는 대상에게 말을 걸어야 하고, ②시의 후반부로 갈수록 돈호법 비율이 줄어야 한다. 「나이팅게일에게」는 새에게 말을 걸며, 돈호법 비율이 55%에서 21%로 크게 떨어진다. 그래서 두 조건을 모두 충족한다.
A(표만 보고 가설을 무시한 오답): 셸리의 시는 돈호법 비율이 가장 높다. 하지만 62%에서 58%로 거의 줄지 않는다. 가설이 다루는 것은 '감소'이지 전체 양이 아니다.
C(가설만 보고 표를 무시한 오답): 가설을 모든 시에 일반화했다. 그러나 셸리의 시는 거의 줄지 않고, 콜리지의 시는 오히려 늘어나므로 표가 이를 반박한다.
D(표의 다른 항목을 잘못 짝지은 오답): 워즈워스의 시가 변화 폭(+32)은 가장 크다. 하지만 비율이 증가했으므로 가설과 방향이 반대이다. 또 말을 거는 대상인 누이는 대답할 수 있는 사람이다.
g.explanation_en:
Correct answer (B): The hypothesis needs two things: (1) the poet addresses something that can't reply, and (2) apostrophe declines as the poem goes on. Keats addresses a bird, and his apostrophe falls from 55% to 21%. Only this poem meets both conditions.
A uses only the table and ignores the hypothesis. Shelley's poem has the highest share of apostrophe, but it barely changes (62% to 58%). The hypothesis is about a decline, not about the total amount.
C uses only the hypothesis and ignores the table. It applies the hypothesis to every poem, but the data contradict this: Shelley's share hardly drops, and Coleridge's rises.
D picks the wrong row. Wordsworth's poem shows the biggest change, but it's an increase, which is the opposite direction. Also, his addressee is his sister, a person who could reply.
g.design: The table and the hypothesis have to be used together. The right answer needs both a silent addressee and a drop in apostrophe. Each wrong answer fails in a different way: A uses only the table, C uses only the hypothesis, and D picks the row with the biggest change even though it goes the wrong direction.

c.instruction: 하나의 결론이나 가설을 먼저 제시한 뒤, 그것을 뒷받침/약화/무관하게 만드는 추가 사실 하나를 골라야 하는 빈칸 문제를 만든다. 정답은 가설의 핵심 조건을 직접 충족하거나 위배하는 사실이어야 하며, 오답 3개는 각각 표면적으로만 관련 있어 보이지만 실제로는 무관한 사실, 가설과 반대 방향으로 작용하는 사실을 지지 사실인 것처럼 제시한 것, 결론과 무관한 배경 정보를 결론 지지처럼 위장한 것으로 만든다.
c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Anselm Kiefer's postmodern artistic engagement with German historical trauma and memory

g.passage: Some critics have charged that Anselm Kiefer's early works, in which he photographed himself giving the Nazi salute at sites across Europe, risked glamorizing the very regime they invoked. Art historian Lisa Saltzman offers a different reading: she argues that Kiefer staged these gestures not to celebrate the past but to force German viewers of the postwar generation to confront a history their society had largely chosen to leave unspoken. If Saltzman is correct, the works should have provoked discomfort chiefly among audiences who shared that silence, so her interpretation would be most strongly supported if it were found that ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: Kiefer later turned to materials such as lead, straw, and ash, which many critics regard as symbols of destruction and loss.
viewers in countries that had been occupied by Germany responded to the photographs with more anger than German viewers did.
German reviewers of the period frequently objected that the photographs exposed matters that their country had tacitly agreed not to discuss.
Kiefer studied under Joseph Beuys, an artist known for using performance to address social and political questions.
g.design: 가설의 핵심 조건(침묵을 공유한 독일 관객이 불편함을 느낌)을 직접 충족하는 사실을 정답으로 두고, 오답은 표면적 관련(후기 재료), 반대 방향(비독일 관객의 더 큰 분노), 위장된 배경(보이스 사사)으로 구성했다.
g.explanation:
정답 C: Saltzman의 해석에 따르면 이 작품들은 과거에 대해 침묵해 온 전후 독일 관객을 겨냥했으므로, 불편함은 주로 그 침묵을 공유한 사람들에게서 나타나야 한다. 독일 평론가들이 '나라가 말하지 않기로 암묵적으로 합의한 것을 드러냈다'며 반발했다는 사실은 이 핵심 조건을 그대로 충족한다.
A: 후기 재료가 상실을 상징한다는 점은 주제상 관련 있어 보이지만, 초기 사진 작품을 관객이 어떻게 받아들였는지와는 상관이 없다.
B: 반응이 주로 독일 관객이 아닌 피점령국 관객에게서 나왔다는 것이므로 가설과 반대 방향을 가리킨다. 오히려 작품이 침묵을 깨뜨렸다기보다 나치를 미화한 것처럼 보였다는 비판 쪽에 가깝다.
D: 보이스에게 배웠다는 것은 전기적 배경일 뿐이다. 작품의 의도나 관객 반응에 대해서는 아무것도 보여 주지 않는다.
g.explanation_en:
Correct answer, C: Saltzman says Kiefer's photographs were aimed at postwar German viewers who had stayed silent about the Nazi past. If she is right, the discomfort should show up mainly among the people who shared that silence. German reviewers complaining that the works exposed things their country had quietly agreed not to discuss fits that condition exactly.
A: Kiefer's later materials are related to the theme of loss, but they tell us nothing about how audiences reacted to the early photographs.
B: This says the strongest reaction came from viewers outside Germany, not German viewers. That points the opposite way from the hypothesis and fits better with the critics' claim that the works seemed to glorify the regime.
D: Studying under Beuys is just background about Kiefer's training. It says nothing about what the works were meant to do or how viewers received them.

c.instruction: 짧은 지문에 '주장→근거→결론' 또는 순서가 있는 2~3개 사건을 넣고, 특정 문장 하나가 전체 흐름에서 어떤 논리적 역할(예: 결론을 예비하는 전환, 앞선 주장을 제한하는 단서)을 하는지 묻는다. 정답은 두 단계 이상을 연결해야 나오도록 만들고, 오답 3개는 각각 '한 단계만 본 역할', '역할을 인접 문장과 혼동', '전체 목적과 개별 문장 기능을 뒤바꾼 것'으로 구성한다.
c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — The development of perspective in Chinese landscape painting and the concept of 'distance without distance' in Song dynasty aesthetics

g.passage: Western viewers encountering Song dynasty landscape scrolls have often judged them to lack perspective, since the paintings contain no single vanishing point toward which lines converge. Yet the eleventh-century painter and theorist Guo Xi described three distinct kinds of distance—looking up at a peak from its base, peering from the front of a mountain into the valleys behind it, and gazing across level ground toward far-off hills—and he urged painters to combine all three within one composition. __Such a combination is impossible for an observer fixed in one spot, because each view requires the eye to stand somewhere different.__ A Song scroll, then, does not fail to achieve a single coherent viewpoint; it deliberately sets that viewpoint aside so that the viewer can wander through the landscape as if traveling within it, experiencing distance without being held at a distance.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It explains why Guo Xi divided distance into three separate types, showing that each type corresponds to a different subject a painter might depict.
It offers evidence supporting the view of Western viewers mentioned earlier, conceding that Song paintings could not represent space convincingly.
It states the main claim of the text, asserting that Song landscape scrolls are designed to let viewers travel imaginatively through the scene.
It draws out an implication of Guo Xi's advice that links it to the absence of a vanishing point, setting up the claim that this absence was intentional.
g.design: 밑줄 문장은 앞의 곽희 이론(근거)과 뒤의 결론(의도적 포기)을 잇는 다리 역할이라, 두 단계를 연결해야 정답이 나온다. 오답은 한 단계만 본 역할(A), 인접 문장인 서구 비판과 혼동한 역할(B), 개별 문장 기능을 전체 목적과 뒤바꾼 역할(C)로 구성했다.
g.explanation:
정답 D: 밑줄 문장은 곽희가 말한 세 가지 거리를 한 화면에 결합하면 시점이 하나일 수 없다는 함의를 끌어낸다. 이를 통해 첫 문장의 '소실점이 없다'는 관찰과 이론을 연결하고, 마지막 문장의 결론, 즉 단일 시점은 의도적으로 내려놓은 것이라는 주장을 준비한다.
A(한 단계만 봄): 밑줄 문장은 세 가지 거리를 나눈 이유를 설명하지 않는다. 세 거리를 결합할 때 생기는 결과를 말할 뿐이고, 각 거리를 '서로 다른 소재'와 짝짓지도 않는다.
B(인접 문장과 혼동): '고정된 관찰자에게는 불가능하다'는 표현을 서구 관람자의 비판을 인정하는 말로 잘못 읽은 선택지다. 실제로 지문은 그 비판을 반박하는 쪽으로 나아간다.
C(전체 목적과 개별 기능을 뒤바꿈): 감상자가 풍경 속을 거닐게 한다는 주장은 마지막 문장의 결론이자 지문 전체의 요지이다. 밑줄 문장 자체의 기능은 아니다.
g.explanation_en:
Correct answer, D: The underlined sentence draws out a consequence of Guo Xi's advice. If you combine all three kinds of distance in one painting, no single fixed viewpoint is possible. That ties his theory to the missing vanishing point mentioned in the first sentence. It also sets up the final sentence's conclusion that the single viewpoint was set aside on purpose.
A only looks at one step. The sentence doesn't explain why Guo Xi divided distance into three types. It describes what happens when you combine them, and it never matches each type to a different subject.
B mixes up the sentence with the earlier Western judgment. "Impossible for an observer fixed in one spot" doesn't agree with that criticism. The passage goes on to argue against it.
C swaps the passage's overall purpose with this one sentence's job. The idea that viewers travel through the scene is the claim made in the last sentence and the main point of the whole text. It isn't what the underlined sentence does.

c.instruction: 두 인물 또는 두 텍스트의 입장을 짧게 제시하고, 한쪽이 다른 쪽의 특정 주장에 대해 보일 반응(동의/반박/보완)을 직접 언급하지 않은 채 추론하도록 묻는다. 정답은 두 입장의 차이를 바탕으로 간접 추론해야 나오게 하고, 오답 3개는 '두 입장을 뒤바꿔 반응을 반대로 서술', '한쪽 입장만 근거로 사용', '텍스트에 없는 새로운 반응을 지어낸 것'으로 만든다.
c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Pauline Oliveros's deep listening philosophy and feminist compositional practice redefining experimental music pedagogy

g.passage: Composer Pauline Oliveros developed "Deep Listening," a practice in which performers attend not only to sounds they produce but to the entire sonic environment, including breath, room resonance, and distant traffic. Music educator Rachel Mendes argues that Oliveros's exercises belong in conservatory curricula chiefly because they sharpen students' pitch discrimination and ensemble timing—skills already central to conventional training. Musicologist Tomás Ibarra reads Oliveros differently. He notes that her early essays criticized the conservatory model itself, in which a single trained authority decides which sounds count as music and which count as noise. __For Ibarra, the exercises' value lies precisely in dissolving that hierarchy, since a student who learns to treat a cough in the audience as material equal to a scripted chord has stopped deferring to any single arbiter of musical worth.__ Teaching Deep Listening, he concludes, means questioning the institution that would host it.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It specifies the grounds on which Ibarra would likely dispute Mendes's view that Oliveros's practice simply reinforces skills conventional training already prizes.
It specifies the grounds on which Mendes would likely dispute Ibarra's view that Oliveros's practice should challenge the authority of conservatories.
It specifies the grounds on which Oliveros herself developed exercises for heightening awareness of an entire sonic environment.
It specifies the grounds on which Ibarra would likely recommend replacing conservatory pitch training with improvisation in public spaces.
g.explanation: 정답 A: 밑줄 문장은 Ibarra가 Deep Listening의 가치를 '판정 위계의 해체'에서 찾는다고 설명한다. 이는 Mendes가 이 연습을 기존 훈련(음정 판별, 합주 타이밍)을 강화하는 도구로 본 것과 정면으로 어긋나므로, Ibarra가 Mendes의 주장에 반박할 근거를 제시하는 셈이다. 다만 지문은 그 반박을 직접 언급하지 않는다. B: 두 입장을 뒤바꾼 오답이다. 밑줄 문장은 Mendes가 아니라 Ibarra의 관점을 담고 있다. C: Oliveros의 연습 소개라는 한쪽 내용만 근거로 삼았다. 밑줄 문장은 Oliveros가 왜 연습을 만들었는지가 아니라 Ibarra의 해석을 설명한다. D: 지문에 없는 반응을 지어냈다. 음정 훈련을 공공장소 즉흥연주로 대체하자는 제안은 어디에도 나오지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: A is correct. The underlined sentence explains that Ibarra values Deep Listening because it dissolves the hierarchy in which one authority judges musical worth. That conflicts with Mendes's claim that the exercises mainly sharpen skills conventional training already values, so the sentence gives Ibarra grounds to dispute Mendes, even though the passage never states that dispute directly. B is wrong because it swaps the two positions: the sentence presents Ibarra's view, not Mendes's. C is wrong because it relies only on the description of Oliveros's practice. The sentence gives Ibarra's interpretation, not Oliveros's reasons for creating the exercises. D is wrong because it makes up a reaction the passage never mentions: replacing pitch training with improvisation in public spaces.
g.design: The underlined sentence states only Ibarra's reading, so the student has to compare it with Mendes's position to infer an implied rebuttal. The wrong answers use the same sentence frame: one swaps the two positions, one relies on only one side, and one makes up a new reaction.

c.instruction: 실험 결과나 비용-효과 같은 구체적 근거 하나를 지문에 제시하고, 이 근거가 특정 결론을 뒷받침하는 정확한 논리적 역할(전면 입증/부분 입증/반증/조건부 지지)을 고르게 한다. 정답은 근거의 범위와 결론의 범위가 정확히 일치하는 것으로 하고, 오답 3개는 각각 '근거가 실제보다 넓은 결론을 지지한다고 과장', '근거의 일부만 반영해 좁게 해석', '근거와 결론의 인과 방향을 뒤바꾼 것'으로 만든다.
c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — The architectural acoustics of Inca stonework and trapezoidal doorway engineering in Andean seismic resilience

g.passage: Visitors to Inca sites such as Ollantaytambo often remark on the trapezoidal doorways, which narrow toward the top, and on the mortarless stone walls whose blocks interlock so tightly that sound seems to travel strangely along them. Some scholars have proposed that both features served a single purpose: protecting buildings from the earthquakes common in the Andes. To test part of this claim, engineer Lucía Paredes built scaled models of a trapezoidal doorway and a rectangular doorway, each set in identical mortarless walls, and placed them on a shake table. __Under simulated tremors of equal strength, the walls around the trapezoidal openings shifted noticeably less than those around the rectangular openings and settled back into place afterward, while Paredes's tests offered no information about whether the walls' acoustic qualities played any role.__ Paredes concludes that the trapezoidal shape likely contributed to the structures' seismic resilience, though whether Inca builders also shaped their walls with sound in mind remains an open question.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents a finding that establishes that both the doorway shape and the acoustic properties of the walls were designed to withstand earthquakes.
It presents a finding that supports one component of the scholars' proposal while leaving another component of that proposal untested.
It presents a finding that shows only that trapezoidal walls recover their position after shaking, without bearing on how much they move during it.
It presents a finding that suggests repeated earthquakes caused Inca doorways to take on a trapezoidal shape over time.
g.explanation: 정답 B: 학자들의 주장은 사다리꼴 문과 음향적 특성 둘 다 내진 목적이라는 것이다. 밑줄 실험은 사다리꼴 형태의 내진 효과만 뒷받침하고 음향 부분은 검증하지 않았음을 명시하므로 부분 입증이다. A는 근거를 음향까지 확장한 과장이다. C는 '덜 움직였다'는 결과를 빼고 복원만 반영한 좁은 해석이다. D는 형태가 내진성을 낳았다는 방향을 지진이 형태를 만들었다는 것으로 뒤집었다.
g.explanation_en: B is correct. The scholars proposed that two features, the trapezoidal doorways and the walls' acoustic qualities, both served earthquake protection. The underlined sentence reports that trapezoidal openings reduced wall movement, which supports the doorway part of that claim. It also says outright that the tests revealed nothing about acoustics, so that part stays untested. That makes the finding partial support. A overstates the evidence by stretching it to cover acoustics. C reads the result too narrowly: it ignores that the walls shifted less, not just that they settled back. D flips cause and effect. The text says the shape helped the walls resist earthquakes, not that earthquakes created the shape.
g.design: Shake-table evidence matches only one half of a two-part claim (partial support). The wrong answers overstate the claim, read the evidence too narrowly, or reverse cause and effect, and all four options share the same sentence frame.
